Index 4
s.back()

0-Based Indexing: First character s[0] ya s.front(), last character s[s.size() - 1] ya s.back(). Length check s.size() is an $O(1)$ constant time lookup.

2. The 12 Core String Problems: Brute, Better & Optimal Solutions

Problem 1

Reverse a String II

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy

Given a string s and an integer k, reverse the first k characters for every 2k characters counting from the start of the string. If fewer than k characters remain, reverse all of them. If between k and 2k remain, reverse first k and leave the rest.

Example 1:
Input: s = "abcdefg", k = 2
Output: "bacdfeg"
Explanation: Block 1 (chars 0..3): "abcd" → reverse first 2 ("ab" → "ba") → "bacd". Block 2 (chars 4..6): "efg" → reverse first 2 ("ef" → "fe") → "feg". Output = "bacdfeg".
Example 2:
Input: s = "abcd", k = 2
Output: "bacd"
Explanation: Reverse first 2 characters "ab" to "ba", leave "cd" as is.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Index ko har baar 2k se aage jump karao: for (int i = 0; i < n; i += 2 * k). Har window me hume sirf min(k, n - i) characters ko in-place reverse karna hota hai using two pointers!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: s = "abcdefg", k = 2
i = 0: Window starts at 0. Reversing first 2 chars: s[0..1] ("ab" → "ba"). String becomes: "bacdefg".
i = 4: Jump i += 4. Remaining chars from index 4 are "efg" (length 3 ≥ k). Reverse s[4..5] ("ef" → "fe"). String becomes: "bacdfeg".
i = 8: Jump i += 4. 8 ≥ 7 → Loop terminates.
Result: "bacdfeg"
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Extract 2k-sized chunks into substring tokens, reverse first k characters of each chunk, and re-concatenate.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
🟡 Better Approach:
Use extra string buffer, appending reversed k slices and intact remaining slices.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
In-place two pointers jumping 2k steps: reverse(s.begin() + i, s.begin() + min(i + k, n)). Zero auxiliary allocations.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

string reverseBrute(string s) {
    string rev = "";
    for (int i = (int)s.length() - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        rev += s[i];
    }
    return rev;
}

int main() {
    string s = "hello";
    cout << reverseBrute(s) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

string reverseBetter(string s) {
    reverse(s.begin(), s.end());
    return s;
}

int main() {
    string s = "hello";
    cout << reverseBetter(s) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
using namespace std;

void reverseOptimal(string& s) {
    int left = 0, right = (int)s.length() - 1;
    while (left < right) {
        swap(s[left], s[right]);
        left++;
        right--;
    }
}

int main() {
    string s = "hello";
    reverseOptimal(s);
    cout << s << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 2

Check if String is Palindrome

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy

A phrase is a palindrome if, after converting all uppercase letters into lowercase letters and removing all non-alphanumeric characters, it reads the same forward and backward.

Example 1:
Input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"
Output: true
Explanation: Cleaned string reads "amanaplanacanalpanama", which is identical backwards and forwards.
Example 2:
Input: s = "race a car"
Output: false
Explanation: Cleaned string reads "raceacar" vs reversed "racaecar" → mismatch at index 3.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Extra string create karke memory waste karne ke bajaye Two Pointers use karo: left = 0 aur right = n - 1. Non-alphanumeric characters par pointer aage badhao, aur alphanumeric characters ko tolower() karke compare karo!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: s = "race a car"
• left = 0 ('r'), right = 9 ('r') → Match!
• left = 1 ('a'), right = 8 ('a') → Match!
• left = 2 ('c'), right = 7 ('c') → Match!
• left = 3 ('e'), right = 5 ('a') → Mismatch ('e' != 'a')!
Returns false instantly!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Filter all alphanumeric characters into a new string, reverse it, and compare with the cleaned string using operator==.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
🟡 Better Approach:
Clean string into new string, then use two pointers inwards to compare characters without full reversal.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Two pointers on the original string directly. Skip isalnum() false characters and compare tolower(). O(1) extra space.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

bool isPalindromeBrute(string s) {
    string rev = s;
    reverse(rev.begin(), rev.end());
    return rev == s;
}

int main() {
    string s = "racecar";
    cout << (isPalindromeBrute(s) ? "true" : "false") << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

bool isPalindromeBetter(const string& s) {
    int n = s.length();
    for (int i = 0; i < n / 2; i++) {
        if (s[i] != s[n - 1 - i]) return false;
    }
    return true;
}

int main() {
    string s = "racecar";
    cout << (isPalindromeBetter(s) ? "true" : "false") << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

bool isPalindromeOptimal(const string& s) {
    int left = 0, right = (int)s.length() - 1;
    while (left < right) {
        if (s[left] != s[right]) return false;
        left++;
        right--;
    }
    return true;
}

int main() {
    string s = "racecar";
    cout << (isPalindromeOptimal(s) ? "true" : "false") << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 3

Largest Odd Number in String

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy

You are given a string num, representing a large integer. Return the largest-valued odd integer (as a substring) that is a non-empty substring of num, or an empty string "" if no odd integer exists.

Example 1:
Input: num = "52"
Output: "5"
Explanation: The only odd numbers are "5". Substring "5" is returned.
Example 2:
Input: num = "35427"
Output: "35427"
Explanation: "35427" is already an odd number because its last digit is 7.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Koi bhi decimal number odd tab hota hai jab uska last digit odd ho! Largest number lene ke liye hum prefix ko jitna lamba ho sake utna bada chahte hain. Isliye string ko right-to-left scan karo: pehla odd digit index i par milte hi prefix num.substr(0, i + 1) largest odd number hoga!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: num = "35427"
i = 4: char = '7'. (7 - '0') % 2 == 1 (Odd digit found!).
Because index 4 is the rightmost odd digit, prefix from 0 to 4 is the largest possible odd substring.
Returns num.substr(0, 5) = "35427" in O(1) steps!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Generate all substrings, convert valid ones or compare digit-by-digit, verify odd parity of last digit, and return max string.
Time: O(N^2) • Space: O(N)
🟡 Better Approach:
Scan from left to right, maintaining the index of the last seen odd digit, then take substring from 0 to that index.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Scan string from right to left (index n-1 down to 0). The first odd digit found gives the largest odd prefix num.substr(0, i + 1).
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

string largestOddNumberBrute(string num) {
    string maxOdd = "";
    for (int i = 0; i < (int)num.length(); i++) {
        string sub = num.substr(0, i + 1);
        char last = sub.back();
        if ((last - '0') % 2 != 0) {
            maxOdd = sub;
        }
    }
    return maxOdd;
}

int main() {
    cout << largestOddNumberBrute("35427") << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

string largestOddNumberBetter(string num) {
    int lastOddIdx = -1;
    for (int i = 0; i < (int)num.length(); i++) {
        if ((num[i] - '0') % 2 != 0) {
            lastOddIdx = i;
        }
    }
    if (lastOddIdx == -1) return "";
    return num.substr(0, lastOddIdx + 1);
}

int main() {
    cout << largestOddNumberBetter("35427") << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

string largestOddNumberOptimal(const string& num) {
    for (int i = (int)num.length() - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        if ((num[i] - '0') % 2 != 0) {
            return num.substr(0, i + 1);
        }
    }
    return "";
}

int main() {
    cout << largestOddNumberOptimal("35427") << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 4

Longest Common Prefix

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy

Write a function to find the longest common prefix string amongst an array of strings. If there is no common prefix, return an empty string "".

Example 1:
Input: strs = ["flower", "flow", "flight"]
Output: "fl"
Explanation: Characters 'f' and 'l' are common to all three strings.
Example 2:
Input: strs = ["dog", "racecar", "car"]
Output: ""
Explanation: No common prefix among the input strings.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Lexicographical Sorting Trick: Agar hum strings array ko sort kar dein, to sabse pehli string (strs[0]) aur sabse aakhiri string (strs.back()) me sabse zyada difference hoga. Agar prefix in dono ke beech match karta hai, to beech ki saari strings me wo guarantee ke saath match karega!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: strs = ["flower", "flow", "flight"]
Step 1 (Sort): ["flight", "flow", "flower"].
Step 2 (Compare extremes): first = "flight", last = "flower".
• k = 0: 'f' == 'f' → prefix = "f"
• k = 1: 'l' == 'l' → prefix = "fl"
• k = 2: 'i' != 'o' → Mismatch! Break loop.
Final Prefix: "fl"
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Vertical scanning: iterate column by column across all strings. If any string does not match character at column i, terminate.
Time: O(N * M) • Space: O(1)
🟡 Better Approach:
Divide and conquer: find common prefix of left half and right half recursively, then merge.
Time: O(N * M) • Space: O(M log N)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Sort the array of strings lexicographically. Compare only the first and last strings character by character.
Time: O(N * M log N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

string longestCommonPrefixBrute(vector<string>& strs) {
    if (strs.empty()) return "";
    string prefix = strs[0];
    for (int i = 1; i < (int)strs.size(); i++) {
        while (strs[i].find(prefix) != 0) {
            prefix = prefix.substr(0, prefix.length() - 1);
            if (prefix.empty()) return "";
        }
    }
    return prefix;
}

int main() {
    vector<string> strs = {"flower", "flow", "flight"};
    cout << longestCommonPrefixBrute(strs) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <string>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

string longestCommonPrefixBetter(vector<string> strs) {
    if (strs.empty()) return "";
    sort(strs.begin(), strs.end());
    string first = strs.front(), last = strs.back();
    string ans = "";
    for (int i = 0; i < min(first.length(), last.length()); i++) {
        if (first[i] != last[i]) break;
        ans += first[i];
    }
    return ans;
}

int main() {
    vector<string> strs = {"flower", "flow", "flight"};
    cout << longestCommonPrefixBetter(strs) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

string longestCommonPrefixOptimal(const vector<string>& strs) {
    if (strs.empty()) return "";
    for (int col = 0; col < (int)strs[0].length(); col++) {
        char ch = strs[0][col];
        for (int row = 1; row < (int)strs.size(); row++) {
            if (col >= (int)strs[row].length() || strs[row][col] != ch) {
                return strs[0].substr(0, col);
            }
        }
    }
    return strs[0];
}

int main() {
    vector<string> strs = {"flower", "flow", "flight"};
    cout << longestCommonPrefixOptimal(strs) << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 5

Isomorphic Strings

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy

Given two strings s and t, determine if they are isomorphic. Two strings are isomorphic if the characters in s can be replaced to get t, preserving the order of characters. No two characters may map to the same character, but a character may map to itself.

Example 1:
Input: s = "egg", t = "add"
Output: true
Explanation: 'e' maps to 'a', and 'g' maps to 'd'.
Example 2:
Input: s = "foo", t = "bar"
Output: false
Explanation: 'o' cannot map to both 'a' and 'r'.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Bijection check: Hume do array chahiye m1[256] aur m2[256] jo store karein ki har character last time kis index par dikha tha. Agar kisi position par m1[s[i]] != m2[t[i]], iska matlab inka mapping match nahi karta!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: s = "egg", t = "add"
• i = 0: m1['e'] = 0, m2['a'] = 0 → Match! Update m1['e']=1, m2['a']=1.
• i = 1: m1['g'] = 0, m2['d'] = 0 → Match! Update m1['g']=2, m2['d']=2.
• i = 2: m1['g'] = 2, m2['d'] = 2 → Match! Update m1['g']=3, m2['d']=3.
All positions match → returns true!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Use two unordered_map data structures to check forward and backward bijection mapping.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
🟡 Better Approach:
Encode both strings into normalized integer pattern strings by assigning sequential IDs to first occurrences, then compare patterns.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Two 256-sized arrays recording last seen positions (i + 1). If m1[s[i]] != m2[t[i]], return false. O(1) space.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

bool isIsomorphicBrute(string s, string t) {
    if (s.length() != t.length()) return false;
    for (int i = 0; i < (int)s.length(); i++) {
        for (int j = i + 1; j < (int)s.length(); j++) {
            if ((s[i] == s[j] && t[i] != t[j]) || (s[i] != s[j] && t[i] == t[j])) {
                return false;
            }
        }
    }
    return true;
}

int main() {
    cout << (isIsomorphicBrute("egg", "add") ? "true" : "false") << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <unordered_map>
using namespace std;

bool isIsomorphicBetter(string s, string t) {
    if (s.length() != t.length()) return false;
    unordered_map<char, char> mapST, mapTS;
    for (int i = 0; i < (int)s.length(); i++) {
        if (mapST.count(s[i]) && mapST[s[i]] != t[i]) return false;
        if (mapTS.count(t[i]) && mapTS[t[i]] != s[i]) return false;
        mapST[s[i]] = t[i];
        mapTS[t[i]] = s[i];
    }
    return true;
}

int main() {
    cout << (isIsomorphicBetter("egg", "add") ? "true" : "false") << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

bool isIsomorphicOptimal(const string& s, const string& t) {
    if (s.length() != t.length()) return false;
    int m1[256] = {0}, m2[256] = {0};
    for (int i = 0; i < (int)s.length(); i++) {
        if (m1[(unsigned char)s[i]] != m2[(unsigned char)t[i]]) return false;
        m1[(unsigned char)s[i]] = i + 1;
        m2[(unsigned char)t[i]] = i + 1;
    }
    return true;
}

int main() {
    cout << (isIsomorphicOptimal("egg", "add") ? "true" : "false") << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 6

Rotate String

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy

Given two strings s and goal, return true if and only if s can become goal after some number of shifts on s.

Example 1:
Input: s = "abcde", goal = "cdeab"
Output: true
Explanation: After 2 shifts, "abcde" becomes "cdeab".
Example 2:
Input: s = "abcde", goal = "abced"
Output: false
Explanation: Characters 'd' and 'e' are swapped, so it is not a valid cyclic shift.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Super Elegant Trick: Agar hum string s ko double kar dein (s + s), to s ke saare possible cyclic rotations us s + s ke andar ek contiguous substring ke roop me appear hote hain! Bas check karo (s + s).find(goal) != string::npos.
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: s = "abcde", goal = "cdeab"
1. Check length: s.size() == goal.size() (5 == 5).
2. Concatenate: doubleS = s + s = "abcdeabcde".
3. Search for "cdeab": found at index 2 ("ab[cdeab]cde")!
Found → returns true!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Simulate all N possible rotations one by one by shifting the first character to the back and comparing with goal.
Time: O(N^2) • Space: O(N)
🟡 Better Approach:
Construct s + s and run KMP pattern matching algorithm to find goal in O(N) time.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Check lengths match. Return (s.length() == goal.length() && (s + s).find(goal) != string::npos).
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

bool rotateStringBrute(string s, string goal) {
    if (s.length() != goal.length()) return false;
    int n = s.length();
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (s == goal) return true;
        s = s.substr(1) + s[0];
    }
    return false;
}

int main() {
    cout << (rotateStringBrute("abcde", "cdeab") ? "true" : "false") << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <queue>
using namespace std;

bool rotateStringBetter(string s, string goal) {
    if (s.length() != goal.length()) return false;
    queue<char> q1, q2;
    for (char c : s) q1.push(c);
    for (char c : goal) q2.push(c);
    int k = goal.length();
    while (k--) {
        char ch = q2.front();
        q2.pop();
        q2.push(ch);
        if (q1 == q2) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

int main() {
    cout << (rotateStringBetter("abcde", "cdeab") ? "true" : "false") << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

bool rotateStringOptimal(const string& s, const string& goal) {
    if (s.length() != goal.length()) return false;
    return (s + s).find(goal) != string::npos;
}

int main() {
    cout << (rotateStringOptimal("abcde", "cdeab") ? "true" : "false") << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 7

Valid Anagram

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy

Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s, and false otherwise.

Example 1:
Input: s = "anagram", t = "nagaram"
Output: true
Explanation: Both strings have identical character frequencies.
Example 2:
Input: s = "rat", t = "car"
Output: false
Explanation: 'r' and 'a' match, but 't' != 'c'.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Size-26 count array banao: s ke character par count[c - 'a']++ karo aur t ke character par count[c - 'a']-- karo. Agar dono anagram hain, to saare count exactly 0 honge!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: s = "anagram", t = "nagaram"
Frequencies incremented for s: a: 3, n: 1, g: 1, r: 1, m: 1.
Frequencies decremented for t: a: -3, n: -1, g: -1, r: -1, m: -1.
Net frequency table: all 26 indices are exactly 0.
Returns true!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Sort both strings using std::sort and check if sorted strings are identical (s == t).
Time: O(N log N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Use unordered_map to count frequencies and compare.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(K) where K <= 26
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Fixed-size array of 26 integers. Single pass: count[s[i] - 'a']++ and count[t[i] - 'a']--. Verify all counts == 0.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

bool isAnagramBrute(string s, string t) {
    if (s.length() != t.length()) return false;
    sort(s.begin(), s.end());
    sort(t.begin(), t.end());
    return s == t;
}

int main() {
    cout << (isAnagramBrute("anagram", "nagaram") ? "true" : "false") << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <unordered_map>
using namespace std;

bool isAnagramBetter(string s, string t) {
    if (s.length() != t.length()) return false;
    unordered_map<char, int> freq;
    for (char c : s) freq[c]++;
    for (char c : t) {
        if (!freq.count(c) || freq[c] == 0) return false;
        freq[c]--;
    }
    return true;
}

int main() {
    cout << (isAnagramBetter("anagram", "nagaram") ? "true" : "false") << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

bool isAnagramOptimal(const string& s, const string& t) {
    if (s.length() != t.length()) return false;
    int count[26] = {0};
    for (int i = 0; i < (int)s.length(); i++) {
        count[s[i] - 'a']++;
        count[t[i] - 'a']--;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < 26; i++) {
        if (count[i] != 0) return false;
    }
    return true;
}

int main() {
    cout << (isAnagramOptimal("anagram", "nagaram") ? "true" : "false") << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 8

Sort Characters by Frequency

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Medium

Given a string s, sort it in decreasing order based on the frequency of the characters. The frequency of a character is the number of times it appears in the string.

Example 1:
Input: s = "tree"
Output: "eert"
Explanation: 'e' appears 2 times, while 'r' and 't' both appear once. "eetr" is also a valid answer.
Example 2:
Input: s = "cccaaa"
Output: "aaaccc"
Explanation: Both 'c' and 'a' appear 3 times. "cccaaa" is also valid.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Bucket Sort pattern: Kisi bhi character ki frequency maximum N ho sakti hai. Isliye vector<string> buckets(n + 1) banate hain jahan index frequency hai. Reverse iterate karke strings append karte hain in $O(N)$!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: s = "tree"
Frequency count: e: 2, t: 1, r: 1.
Buckets: bucket[2] = "ee", bucket[1] = "tr".
Collect from top: bucket[2] gives "ee", bucket[1] gives "tr".
Result: "eetr"
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Count frequencies, copy pairs to vector, sort by frequency descending, and build result string.
Time: O(N log N) • Space: O(N)
🟡 Better Approach:
Use max-heap (priority_queue) of pair to extract highest frequency characters.
Time: O(N log K) • Space: O(N + K)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Bucket sort on frequencies from 1 to N. Build result by iterating buckets backwards. O(N) linear time.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

string frequencySortBrute(string s) {
    int n = s.length();
    vector<pair<int, char>> freqs;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        int cnt = 0;
        for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) if (s[j] == s[i]) cnt++;
        freqs.push_back({cnt, s[i]});
    }
    sort(freqs.begin(), freqs.end(), [](const pair<int, char>& a, const pair<int, char>& b) {
        if (a.first != b.first) return a.first > b.first;
        return a.second < b.second;
    });
    string ans = "";
    for (auto& p : freqs) ans += p.second;
    return ans;
}

int main() {
    cout << frequencySortBrute("tree") << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <queue>
using namespace std;

string frequencySortBetter(string s) {
    unordered_map<char, int> freq;
    for (char c : s) freq[c]++;
    priority_queue<pair<int, char>> pq;
    for (auto& p : freq) pq.push({p.second, p.first});
    string ans = "";
    while (!pq.empty()) {
        auto [count, ch] = pq.top();
        pq.pop();
        ans.append(count, ch);
    }
    return ans;
}

int main() {
    cout << frequencySortBetter("tree") << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include <unordered_map>
using namespace std;

string frequencySortOptimal(const string& s) {
    unordered_map<char, int> freq;
    for (char c : s) freq[c]++;
    int n = s.length();
    vector<string> buckets(n + 1, "");
    for (auto& p : freq) buckets[p.second].append(p.second, p.first);
    string ans = "";
    for (int i = n; i > 0; i--) {
        if (!buckets[i].empty()) ans += buckets[i];
    }
    return ans;
}

int main() {
    cout << frequencySortOptimal("tree") << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 9

Reverse Words in a String

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Medium

Given an input string s, reverse the order of the words. The words should be returned concatenated by a single space, removing leading, trailing, and multiple intervening spaces.

Example 1:
Input: s = "the sky is blue"
Output: "blue is sky the"
Explanation: Words reversed in order: "blue", "is", "sky", "the".
Example 2:
Input: s = " hello world "
Output: "world hello"
Explanation: Extra spaces stripped and words reversed.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
In-Place Two-Step Algorithm: Pehle poori string ko reverse kar do (`reverse(s.begin(), s.end())`), phir har individual word ko do-pointers se identify karke in-place reverse kar do!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: s = "the sky"
1. Reverse entire string: "yks eht"
2. Reverse word 1 ("yks" → "sky"): "sky eht"
3. Reverse word 2 ("eht" → "the"): "sky the"
Final Clean Result: "sky the"
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Use stringstream to parse words into a vector, then traverse vector backwards.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
🟡 Better Approach:
Right-to-left two-pointer scan extracting words and appending them with space.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
In-place two-step algorithm: reverse entire string, reverse each word in-place, and shift to eliminate extra spaces.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include <sstream>
using namespace std;

string reverseWordsBrute(string s) {
    stringstream ss(s);
    string word;
    vector<string> words;
    while (ss >> word) {
        words.push_back(word);
    }
    string result = "";
    for (int i = (int)words.size() - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        result += words[i];
        if (i > 0) result += " ";
    }
    return result;
}

int main() {
    string s = "the sky is blue";
    cout << reverseWordsBrute(s) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

string reverseWordsBetter(string s) {
    string result = "";
    int i = s.length() - 1;
    while (i >= 0) {
        while (i >= 0 && s[i] == ' ') i--;
        if (i < 0) break;
        int j = i;
        while (i >= 0 && s[i] != ' ') i--;
        if (!result.empty()) result += " ";
        result += s.substr(i + 1, j - i);
    }
    return result;
}

int main() {
    string s = "  hello world  ";
    cout << reverseWordsBetter(s) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

string reverseWordsOptimal(string s) {
    reverse(s.begin(), s.end());
    int n = s.size();
    int idx = 0;
    for (int start = 0; start < n; start++) {
        if (s[start] != ' ') {
            if (idx != 0) s[idx++] = ' ';
            int end = start;
            while (end < n && s[end] != ' ') end++;
            reverse(s.begin() + idx, s.begin() + idx + (end - start));
            for (int k = start; k < end; k++) s[idx++] = s[k];
            reverse(s.begin() + idx - (end - start), s.begin() + idx);
            start = end - 1;
        }
    }
    s.resize(idx);
    return s;
}

int main() {
    string s = "a good   example";
    cout << reverseWordsOptimal(s) << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 10

Maximum Nesting Depth of Parentheses

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy

Given a valid parentheses string (VPS) s, return the nesting depth of s.

Example 1:
Input: s = "(1+(2*3)+((8)/4))+1"
Output: 3
Explanation: Digit 8 is nested inside 3 pairs of parentheses.
Example 2:
Input: s = "(1)+((2))+(((3)))"
Output: 3
Explanation: Innermost number 3 has depth 3.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Bas do integer counters: currDepth aur maxDepth. Jab bhi '(' dikhe to currDepth++ karo aur maxDepth = max(maxDepth, currDepth) karo; jab ')' dikhe to currDepth-- karo!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: s = "(1+(2*3))"
'(' → currDepth = 1, maxDepth = 1
'(' → currDepth = 2, maxDepth = 2 (Peak)
')' → currDepth = 1
')' → currDepth = 0. Answer = 2.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Use std::stack pushing '(' and checking stack size at each peak.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
🟡 Better Approach:
Store prefix depth in an auxiliary array and find max.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Single pass counters currDepth and maxDepth. Increment on '(', decrement on ')'. O(1) space.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <stack>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

int maxDepthBrute(string s) {
    stack<char> st;
    int maxD = 0;
    for (char c : s) {
        if (c == '(') {
            st.push(c);
            maxD = max(maxD, (int)st.size());
        } else if (c == ')') {
            if (!st.empty()) st.pop();
        }
    }
    return maxD;
}

int main() {
    string s = "(1+(2*3)+((8)/4))+1";
    cout << maxDepthBrute(s) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

int maxDepthBetter(string s) {
    int n = s.length();
    vector<int> depths(n, 0);
    int curr = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (s[i] == '(') curr++;
        else if (s[i] == ')') curr--;
        depths[i] = curr;
    }
    int maxD = 0;
    for (int d : depths) maxD = max(maxD, d);
    return maxD;
}

int main() {
    string s = "(1)+((2))+(((3)))";
    cout << maxDepthBetter(s) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

int maxDepthOptimal(string s) {
    int currDepth = 0;
    int maxDepthVal = 0;
    for (char c : s) {
        if (c == '(') {
            currDepth++;
            maxDepthVal = max(maxDepthVal, currDepth);
        } else if (c == ')') {
            currDepth--;
        }
    }
    return maxDepthVal;
}

int main() {
    string s = "(1+(2*3)+((8)/4))+1";
    cout << maxDepthOptimal(s) << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 11

Roman to Integer

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy

Given a Roman numeral string s, convert it to an integer.

Example 1:
Input: s = "MCMXCIV"
Output: 1994
Explanation: M = 1000, CM = 900, XC = 90, IV = 4 → 1994.
Example 2:
Input: s = "LVIII"
Output: 58
Explanation: L = 50, V = 5, III = 3 → 58.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Right-to-Left scan: prevVal maintain karo. Agar current Roman numeral ka value prevVal se chhota hai, to subtract karo (jaise IV me 1 < 5); warna add karo!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: s = "MCMXCIV"
V (5) → +5, prev=5
I (1 < 5) → -1, total = 4, prev=1
C (100 > 1) → +100, total = 104, prev=100
X (10 < 100) → -10, total = 94, prev=10
M (1000) → +1000, total = 1094, prev=1000
C (100 < 1000) → -100, total = 994, prev=100
M (1000) → +1000, total = 1994. Result = 1994.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Check two-character substrings first for all 6 subtractive special cases ("IV", "IX", etc.).
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
🟡 Better Approach:
Use unordered_map with left-to-right comparison against s[i+1].
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Right-to-left scan with switch-case lookup and prevValue comparison. Zero map overhead, O(1) space.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

int romanToIntBrute(string s) {
    int total = 0;
    int i = 0;
    int n = s.length();
    while (i < n) {
        if (i + 1 < n) {
            string two = s.substr(i, 2);
            if (two == "IV") { total += 4; i += 2; continue; }
            if (two == "IX") { total += 9; i += 2; continue; }
            if (two == "XL") { total += 40; i += 2; continue; }
            if (two == "XC") { total += 90; i += 2; continue; }
            if (two == "CD") { total += 400; i += 2; continue; }
            if (two == "CM") { total += 900; i += 2; continue; }
        }
        char c = s[i];
        if (c == 'I') total += 1;
        else if (c == 'V') total += 5;
        else if (c == 'X') total += 10;
        else if (c == 'L') total += 50;
        else if (c == 'C') total += 100;
        else if (c == 'D') total += 500;
        else if (c == 'M') total += 1000;
        i++;
    }
    return total;
}

int main() {
    string s = "MCMXCIV";
    cout << romanToIntBrute(s) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <unordered_map>
using namespace std;

int romanToIntBetter(string s) {
    unordered_map<char, int> mp = {
        {'I', 1}, {'V', 5}, {'X', 10}, {'L', 50},
        {'C', 100}, {'D', 500}, {'M', 1000}
    };
    int total = 0;
    int n = s.length();
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (i + 1 < n && mp[s[i]] < mp[s[i + 1]]) {
            total -= mp[s[i]];
        } else {
            total += mp[s[i]];
        }
    }
    return total;
}

int main() {
    string s = "LVIII";
    cout << romanToIntBetter(s) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

inline int getVal(char c) {
    switch (c) {
        case 'I': return 1;
        case 'V': return 5;
        case 'X': return 10;
        case 'L': return 50;
        case 'C': return 100;
        case 'D': return 500;
        case 'M': return 1000;
        default: return 0;
    }
}

int romanToIntOptimal(string s) {
    int total = 0;
    int prev = 0;
    for (int i = (int)s.length() - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        int curr = getVal(s[i]);
        if (curr < prev) total -= curr;
        else total += curr;
        prev = curr;
    }
    return total;
}

int main() {
    string s = "MCMXCIV";
    cout << romanToIntOptimal(s) << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 12

String to Integer (atoi)

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Medium

Implement the myAtoi(string s) function which converts a string to a 32-bit signed integer with whitespace skipping, sign handling, and clamping.

Example 1:
Input: s = " -042"
Output: -42
Explanation: Leading spaces skipped, negative sign parsed, 042 becomes -42.
Example 2:
Input: s = "1337c0d3"
Output: 1337
Explanation: Reading stops at character 'c'.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Skip spaces, read sign, and accumulate digits. Sabse important hai Integer Overflow Prevention: Before multiplying by 10, check if ans > (INT_MAX - digit) / 10 to clamp immediately to INT_MAX or INT_MIN without using 64-bit types!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: s = " -042"
1. Skip 3 spaces → index 3.
2. Parse '-' → sign = -1, index 4.
3. Parse '0' → ans = 0
4. Parse '4' → ans = 4
5. Parse '2' → ans = 42
Return sign * ans = -42
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Extract digit characters into string buffer, convert using long long with sign, clamp within INT_MIN to INT_MAX.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
🟡 Better Approach:
Process digits with 64-bit integer accumulator, then clamp to 32-bit integer boundaries.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Pure 32-bit arithmetic with proactive overflow check: ans > (INT_MAX - digit) / 10. Clamps instantly with O(1) memory.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <climits>
using namespace std;

int myAtoiBrute(string s) {
    int i = 0;
    int n = s.length();
    while (i < n && s[i] == ' ') i++;
    if (i == n) return 0;
    int sign = 1;
    if (s[i] == '+' || s[i] == '-') {
        if (s[i] == '-') sign = -1;
        i++;
    }
    string digits = "";
    while (i < n && isdigit(s[i])) {
        digits += s[i];
        i++;
    }
    if (digits.empty()) return 0;
    long long ans = 0;
    for (char c : digits) {
        ans = ans * 10 + (c - '0');
        if (sign == 1 && ans > INT_MAX) return INT_MAX;
        if (sign == -1 && -ans < INT_MIN) return INT_MIN;
    }
    return (int)(sign * ans);
}

int main() {
    string s = "   -042";
    cout << myAtoiBrute(s) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <climits>
using namespace std;

int myAtoiBetter(string s) {
    int i = 0;
    int n = s.length();
    while (i < n && s[i] == ' ') i++;
    if (i >= n) return 0;
    int sign = 1;
    if (s[i] == '+' || s[i] == '-') {
        sign = (s[i] == '-') ? -1 : 1;
        i++;
    }
    long long ans = 0;
    while (i < n && isdigit(s[i])) {
        ans = ans * 10 + (s[i] - '0');
        if (sign == 1 && ans >= INT_MAX) return INT_MAX;
        if (sign == -1 && -ans <= INT_MIN) return INT_MIN;
        i++;
    }
    return (int)(sign * ans);
}

int main() {
    string s = "4193 with words";
    cout << myAtoiBetter(s) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <climits>
using namespace std;

int myAtoiOptimal(string s) {
    int i = 0;
    int n = s.length();
    while (i < n && s[i] == ' ') i++;
    if (i >= n) return 0;
    int sign = 1;
    if (s[i] == '+' || s[i] == '-') {
        sign = (s[i] == '-') ? -1 : 1;
        i++;
    }
    int ans = 0;
    while (i < n && isdigit(s[i])) {
        int digit = s[i] - '0';
        if (ans > (INT_MAX - digit) / 10) {
            return (sign == 1) ? INT_MAX : INT_MIN;
        }
        ans = ans * 10 + digit;
        i++;
    }
    return sign * ans;
}

int main() {
    string s = "-91283472332";
    cout << myAtoiOptimal(s) << endl;
    return 0;
}

Chapter 9 • Recursion Fundamentals & Call Stack Patterns

DSA Basic Recursion — Complete C++ Notes: Base Cases, State Passing & 12 Core Problems

Call Stack • Base Case • State Passing • Divide & Conquer • Recursion Trees

1. Recursion Architecture: Call Stack & The 2 Fundamental Parts

Recursion ek aisi programming technique hai jisme ek function kisi problem ko solve karne ke liye apne aap ko smaller input arguments ke saath call karta hai. Jab tak problem ek aisi state me na pahunch jaye jiska answer direct pata ho (known as the Base Case), tab tak function calls memory stack par pile up hoti rehti hain.

Call Stack Trace: countdown(3) Winding & Unwinding
1. Winding Phase (Stack Pushing)
countdown(0) → Base Case: Stop!
countdown(1) → Prints 1, calls countdown(0)
countdown(2) → Prints 2, calls countdown(1)
countdown(3) → Prints 3, calls countdown(2)
2. Unwinding Phase (Stack Popping)
countdown(0) returns → Popped from stack
countdown(1) completes → Popped from stack
countdown(2) completes → Popped from stack
countdown(3) completes → Execution terminates

The 2 Inviolable Components of Every Recursive Function:
1. Base Case: Wo condition jahan recursion stop ho jata hai bina aur recursive calls lagaye.
2. Recursive Case: Jahan function smaller/reduced input par khud ko call karke problem ka size chhota karta hai.

The 3 Golden Questions for Designing Any Recursion:
  1. Base Case kya hai? (Smallest valid input jiska answer hum directly jante hain, jaise n == 0 ya left ≥ right).
  2. Har call me input kaise reduce ho raha hai? (n - 1, n / 10, ya left + 1, right - 1).
  3. Return hone par kya combine hoga? (Sum accumulation, boolean AND/OR, ya in-place character swaps).
Problem 1

Recursion with Parameters: Print 1 to N

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy

Given an integer n, write a recursive function to print all numbers from 1 to n in ascending order without using any iterative loops (for, while, do-while). State advancement must rely purely on function parameter recursion or call-stack unwinding.

Example 1:
Input: n = 5
Output: 1 2 3 4 5
Explanation: Function prints numbers sequentially from 1 up to 5 separated by space.
Example 2:
Input: n = 1
Output: 1
Explanation: Single value output terminating immediately when base condition is reached.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Jab function call hota hai, to har call ka apna activation frame stack par banta hai. Backtracking approach me, hum pehle print(n - 1) call karte hain, phir print karte hain — isse call stack unwinding ke dauraan automatically 1 se n tak ascending order me print ho jata hai bina kisi auxiliary forward counter ke!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: n = 3 (Backtracking)
  1. Call print(3) → calls print(2) (Stack: [3])
  2. Call print(2) → calls print(1) (Stack: [3, 2])
  3. Call print(1) → calls print(0) (Stack: [3, 2, 1])
  4. Call print(0) → base case n == 0 hit, returns.
  5. Resume print(1): prints 1 , pops stack.
  6. Resume print(2): prints 2 , pops stack.
  7. Resume print(3): prints 3 , pops stack. Final: 1 2 3.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Simple iterative for-loop running sequentially from 1 to n.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
🟡 Better Approach:
Tail recursive parameter passing advancing counter i + 1 forward until base condition i > n.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) Auxiliary Call Stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Backtracking single-parameter recursion (print(n - 1); cout << n;). Stack unwinding prints in ascending order with no state parameter.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) Call Stack
Time: O(N) Space: O(N) Stack
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

void printNumbersBrute(int n) {
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        cout << i << " ";
    }
}

int main() {
    printNumbersBrute(5);
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++)

using namespace std;

void printNumbersBetter(int i, int n) {
    if (i > n) return;
    cout << i << " ";
    printNumbersBetter(i + 1, n);
}

int main() {
    printNumbersBetter(1, 5);
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

void printNumbersOptimal(int n) {
    if (n == 0) return;
    printNumbersOptimal(n - 1);
    cout << n << " ";
}

    printNumbersOptimal(5);
    return 0;
}
Problem 2

Sum of First N Numbers

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy

Given an integer n, compute and return the sum of all positive integers from 1 up to n ($1 + 2 + \dots + n$) using recursion and mathematical reduction.

Example 1:
Input: n = 5
Output: 15
Explanation: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15.
Example 2:
Input: n = 3
Output: 6
Explanation: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Sum of N numbers can be naturally divided into: current number $n$ plus the sum of first $n - 1$ numbers: sum(n) = n + sum(n - 1). Base case: jab $n = 0$, sum $0$ return hota hai. Mathematically, direct Gauss formula $n \times (n + 1) / 2$ gives $O(1)$ constant time with zero recursion overhead.
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: n = 3 (Functional Recursion)
  1. sum(3) calls 3 + sum(2)
  2. sum(2) calls 2 + sum(1)
  3. sum(1) calls 1 + sum(0)
  4. sum(0) hits base case n == 0, returns 0.
  5. sum(1) returns 1 + 0 = 1.
  6. sum(2) returns 2 + 1 = 3.
  7. sum(3) returns 3 + 3 = 6. Final Result: 6.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Iterative accumulation using a standard for-loop from 1 to n.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
🟡 Better Approach:
Functional recursive divide & conquer returning n + sum(n - 1).
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) Call Stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Direct mathematical Gauss formula: n * (n + 1) / 2. Computes result instantly in constant time.
Time: O(1) • Space: O(1)
Time: O(1) Math / O(N) Rec Space: O(1) Math / O(N) Stack
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

int sumOfNBrute(int n) {
    int sum = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        sum += i;
    }
    return sum;
}

int main() {
    cout << sumOfNBrute(5) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

void sumOfNBetter(int n, int currentSum) {
    if (n < 1) {
        cout << currentSum << endl;
        return;
    }
    sumOfNBetter(n - 1, currentSum + n);
}

int main() {
    sumOfNBetter(5, 0);
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

int sumOfNOptimal(int n) {
    if (n == 0) return 0;
    return n + sumOfNOptimal(n - 1);
}

    cout << sumOfNOptimal(5) << endl;

Problem 3

Factorial of a Given Number

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy

Given a non-negative integer n, compute $n!$ (factorial of n), which is the product of all positive integers less than or equal to $n$. Note that by definition $0! = 1$.

Example 1:
Input: n = 4
Output: 24
Explanation: 4 * 3 * 2 * 1 = 24.
Example 2:
Input: n = 0
Output: 1
Explanation: 0! is mathematically defined as 1.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Factorial follows recurrence relation: $n! = n \times (n - 1)!$. Base case: jab $n \le 1$, value 1 hoti hai. Function recursively call stack me depth tak jata hai aur return hote waqt running product accumulate karta hai.
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: n = 4 (Functional Recursion)
  1. fact(4) calls 4 * fact(3)
  2. fact(3) calls 3 * fact(2)
  3. fact(2) calls 2 * fact(1)
  4. fact(1) hits base case n ≤ 1, returns 1.
  5. fact(2) receives 1 → computes 2 * 1 = 2.
  6. fact(3) receives 2 → computes 3 * 2 = 6.
  7. fact(4) receives 6 → computes 4 * 6 = 24. Final Result = 24.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Iterative multiplication loop from 1 to n.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
🟡 Better Approach:
Parameterized recursive accumulation maintaining running product in argument.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) Call Stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Functional recursive divide & conquer returning n * fact(n - 1) with base case n ≤ 1.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) Call Stack
Time: O(N) Space: O(N) Stack
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

long long factorialBrute(int n) {
    long long ans = 1;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        ans *= i;
    }
    return ans;
}

int main() {
    cout << factorialBrute(5) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

void factorialBetter(int n, long long prod) {
    if (n <= 1) {
        cout << prod << endl;
        return;
    }
    factorialBetter(n - 1, prod * n);
}

int main() {
    factorialBetter(5, 1);
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

long long factorialOptimal(int n) {
    if (n <= 1) return 1;
    return n * factorialOptimal(n - 1);
}

int main() {
    cout << factorialOptimal(5) << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 4

Sum of Array Elements II

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy

Given an array of integers nums of size n, calculate the sum of all elements in the array using recursion without any loops.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [1, 2, 3, 4], n = 4
Output: 10
Explanation: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10.
Example 2:
Input: nums = [5], n = 1
Output: 5
Explanation: Single element array returns its only value.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Array ko recursive subproblem me divide karte hain: index i se lekar end tak ka sum = nums[i] + sumArray(i + 1). Base case: jab i == n, koi element nahi bacha, to return 0.
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: nums = [1, 2, 3], n = 3
  1. sumArr(0) calls nums[0] (1) + sumArr(1)
  2. sumArr(1) calls nums[1] (2) + sumArr(2)
  3. sumArr(2) calls nums[2] (3) + sumArr(3)
  4. sumArr(3) hits base case idx == 3, returns 0.
  5. sumArr(2) computes 3 + 0 = 3.
  6. sumArr(1) computes 2 + 3 = 5.
  7. sumArr(0) computes 1 + 5 = 6. Final Result = 6.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Standard iterative loop summing nums[i] sequentially.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
🟡 Better Approach:
Parameterized recursion passing accumulator sum forward in arguments.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) Call Stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Divide and conquer recursive reduction: nums[i] + sum(i + 1, n) with base case i == n.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) Auxiliary Stack
Time: O(N) Space: O(N) Stack
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

int arraySumBrute(const vector<int>& arr) {
    int total = 0;
    for (int x : arr) total += x;
    return total;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> arr = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    cout << arraySumBrute(arr) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

int arraySumBetter(const vector<int>& arr, int idx) {
    if (idx == (int)arr.size()) return 0;
    return arr[idx] + arraySumBetter(arr, idx + 1);
}

int main() {
    vector<int> arr = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    cout << arraySumBetter(arr, 0) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

int arraySumOptimal(const vector<int>& arr, int left, int right) {
    if (left == right) return arr[left];
    if (left > right) return 0;
    int mid = left + (right - left) / 2;
    return arraySumOptimal(arr, left, mid) + arraySumOptimal(arr, mid + 1, right);
}

int main() {
    vector<int> arr = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    cout << arraySumOptimal(arr, 0, (int)arr.size() - 1) << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 5

Reverse a String I

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy

Given a string s, reverse the string in-place using a recursive two-pointer technique swapping symmetrically placed characters.

Example 1:
Input: s = "hello"
Output: "olleh"
Explanation: Characters at symmetric ends swap ('h' with 'o', 'e' with 'l').
Example 2:
Input: s = "code"
Output: "edoc"
Explanation: Symmetric swaps: ('c' with 'e', 'o' with 'd').
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Do pointers left = 0 aur right = n - 1 rakhte hain. Har recursive call me s[left] aur s[right] ko swap karte hain aur left + 1, right - 1 ke liye recurse karte hain. Base case: jab left ≥ right, string fully reverse ho chuki hai.
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: s = "abcd", left = 0, right = 3
  1. left = 0, right = 3: swap s[0] ('a') & s[3] ('d') → "dbca", recurse (1, 2).
  2. left = 1, right = 2: swap s[1] ('b') & s[2] ('c') → "dcba", recurse (2, 1).
  3. left = 2, right = 1: base condition left ≥ right met, terminates.
  4. Final String: "dcba".
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Extra string creation appending characters in reverse order.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
🟡 Better Approach:
Iterative two-pointer in-place swapping while left < right.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
In-place two-pointer recursion swapping symmetrically and recursing on (left + 1, right - 1).
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) Call Stack
Time: O(N) Space: O(N) Stack
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

string reverseStringBrute(string s) {
    if (s.empty()) return "";
    return s.back() + reverseStringBrute(s.substr(0, s.length() - 1));
}

int main() {
    cout << reverseStringBrute("recursion") << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
using namespace std;

void reverseStringBetter(string& s, int i) {
    int n = s.length();
    if (i >= n / 2) return;
    swap(s[i], s[n - 1 - i]);
    reverseStringBetter(s, i + 1);
}

int main() {
    string str = "recursion";
    reverseStringBetter(str, 0);
    cout << str << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
using namespace std;

void reverseStringOptimal(string& s, int left, int right) {
    if (left >= right) return;
    swap(s[left], s[right]);
    reverseStringOptimal(s, left + 1, right - 1);
}

int main() {
    string str = "recursion";
    reverseStringOptimal(str, 0, str.length() - 1);
    cout << str << endl;
    return 0;

Problem 6

Check if String Is Palindrome

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy

Given a string s, check if it reads the same forwards and backwards using recursive symmetric index validation.

Example 1:
Input: s = "radar"
Output: true
Explanation: "radar" is identical forwards and backwards.
Example 2:
Input: s = "hello"
Output: false
Explanation: 'h' != 'o', mismatch found on first check.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Ek string palindrome tab hoti hai jab uska pehla aur aakhiri character match kare AND beech ka substring bhi palindrome ho. Single index i se dono symmetric characters s[i] aur s[n - 1 - i] check kiye ja sakte hain bina do pointers ke!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: s = "madam", n = 5
  1. i = 0: check s[0] ('m') == s[4] ('m') → Match! Recurse i = 1.
  2. i = 1: check s[1] ('a') == s[3] ('a') → Match! Recurse i = 2.
  3. i = 2: i ≥ n / 2 (2 ≥ 2) base case reached → return true.
  4. Result: true.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Create reversed copy of string and compare using standard equality operator.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
🟡 Better Approach:
Iterative two-pointer loop checking symmetric characters from outside inwards.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Single-index recursive verification checking s[i] == s[n - 1 - i] up to n / 2.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) Call Stack
Time: O(N) Space: O(N) Stack
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

bool isPalindromeBrute(string s) {
    string rev = s;
    reverse(rev.begin(), rev.end());
    return rev == s;
}

int main() {
    cout << (isPalindromeBrute("racecar") ? "true" : "false") << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

bool isPalindromeBetter(const string& s) {
    int left = 0, right = s.length() - 1;
    while (left < right) {
        if (s[left] != s[right]) return false;
        left++;
        right--;
    }
    return true;
}

int main() {
    cout << (isPalindromeBetter("racecar") ? "true" : "false") << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

bool isPalindromeOptimal(const string& s, int left, int right) {
    if (left >= right) return true;
    if (s[left] != s[right]) return false;
    return isPalindromeOptimal(s, left + 1, right - 1);
}

int main() {
    string s = "racecar";
    cout << (isPalindromeOptimal(s, 0, s.length() - 1) ? "true" : "false") << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 7

Check if Number Is Prime

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy-Medium

Given an integer n ($n \ge 2$), determine recursively whether n is a prime number (has no divisors other than 1 and itself).

Example 1:
Input: n = 11
Output: true
Explanation: 11 has only two divisors: 1 and 11.
Example 2:
Input: n = 15
Output: false
Explanation: 15 is divisible by 3 and 5.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Divisor $d = 2$ se check shuru karte hain. Agar $d \times d > n$, iska matlab $\sqrt{n}$ tak koi divisor nahi mila, to number prime hai. Agar $n \% d == 0$, to composite hai. Warna $d + 1$ ke sath recursive call karte hain. Isse $O(\sqrt{n})$ calls me result mil jata hai.
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: n = 17, start d = 2
  1. d = 2: 2 * 2 = 4 ≤ 17, 17 % 2 = 1 ≠ 0. Recurse d = 3.
  2. d = 3: 3 * 3 = 9 ≤ 17, 17 % 3 = 2 ≠ 0. Recurse d = 4.
  3. d = 4: 4 * 4 = 16 ≤ 17, 17 % 4 = 1 ≠ 0. Recurse d = 5.
  4. d = 5: 5 * 5 = 25 > 17. Base case d * d > n triggered → return true.
  5. Result: true.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Trial division testing all potential divisors from 2 up to n - 1.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
🟡 Better Approach:
Linear recursive trial division testing d up to n - 1.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) Call Stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Optimized recursive trial division with d * d ≤ n boundary stopping at $\sqrt{n}$.
Time: O(sqrt(N)) • Space: O(sqrt(N)) Call Stack
Time: O(sqrt(N)) Space: O(sqrt(N)) Stack
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

bool isPrimeBrute(int n, int i = 2) {
    if (n <= 1) return false;
    if (i == n) return true;
    if (n % i == 0) return false;
    return isPrimeBrute(n, i + 1);
}

int main() {
    cout << (isPrimeBrute(29) ? "Prime" : "Not Prime") << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

bool isPrimeBetter(int n) {
    if (n <= 1) return false;
    for (int i = 2; i * i <= n; i++) {
        if (n % i == 0) return false;
    }
    return true;
}

int main() {
    cout << (isPrimeBetter(29) ? "Prime" : "Not Prime") << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

bool isPrimeOptimal(int n, int i = 2) {
    if (n <= 1) return false;
    if (i * i > n) return true;
    if (n % i == 0) return false;
    return isPrimeOptimal(n, i + 1);
}

int main() {
    cout << (isPrimeOptimal(29) ? "Prime" : "Not Prime") << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 8

Reverse an Array 2

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy

Given an array of integers nums of size n, reverse the array elements in-place using single-index recursion where the opposite index is derived mathematically as n - 1 - i.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
Output: [5, 4, 3, 2, 1]
Explanation: Symmetrical elements swap in-place.
Example 2:
Input: nums = [10, 20]
Output: [20, 10]
Explanation: Array of 2 elements reverses directly.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Do pointers ki jagah ek single index $i$ use karte hain. Symmetrical counterpart index $n - 1 - i$ hota hai. Swap karne ke baad i + 1 call karte hain jab tak $i \ge n / 2$ na ho jaye.
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: nums = [1, 2, 3, 4], n = 4
  1. i = 0: swap nums[0] (1) and nums[3] (4) → [4, 2, 3, 1], recurse i = 1.
  2. i = 1: swap nums[1] (2) and nums[2] (3) → [4, 3, 2, 1], recurse i = 2.
  3. i = 2: i ≥ n / 2 (2 ≥ 2) base case hit → return.
  4. Final Array: [4, 3, 2, 1].
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Auxiliary array copy in reverse order.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
🟡 Better Approach:
Iterative two-pointer swap using std::swap.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
In-place single-index recursion swapping nums[i] and nums[n - 1 - i] up to n / 2.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) Call Stack
Time: O(N) Space: O(N) Stack
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

void reverseArrayBrute(vector<int>& arr) {
    int n = arr.size();
    vector<int> temp(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) temp[i] = arr[n - 1 - i];
    arr = temp;
}

#include <vector>
#include <utility>

void reverseArrayBetter(vector<int>& arr) {

    while (left < right) {
        swap(arr[left++], arr[right--]);
    }
}

void reverseArrayOptimal(vector<int>& arr, int left, int right) {

Problem 9

Check if Array Is Sorted II

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy

Given an array of integers nums of size n, recursively check whether the array is sorted in non-decreasing order (nums[i] ≤ nums[i+1] for all valid $i$).

Example 1:
Input: nums = [1, 2, 4, 7, 9]
Output: true
Explanation: Every element is less than or equal to its successor.
Example 2:
Input: nums = [1, 3, 2, 5]
Output: false
Explanation: nums[1] (3) > nums[2] (2), unsorted violation found.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Array sorted tab hota hai jab nums[i] ≤ nums[i+1] satisfy ho AND baaki ka remaining subarray starting at i+1 bhi sorted ho. Base case: jab i == n - 1, single element array always sorted hota hai to return true.
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: nums = [2, 5, 8], n = 3
  1. i = 0: compare nums[0] (2) ≤ nums[1] (5) → Valid! Recurse i = 1.
  2. i = 1: compare nums[1] (5) ≤ nums[2] (8) → Valid! Recurse i = 2.
  3. i = 2: i == n - 1 (2 == 2) base case reached → return true.
  4. Result: true.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Nested loops checking for any inversion pair nums[i] > nums[j] where i < j.
Time: O(N^2) • Space: O(1)
🟡 Better Approach:
Iterative single-pass loop verifying adjacent element ordering.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Recursive divide-and-conquer checking adjacent pair and advancing index i + 1.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) Call Stack
Time: O(N) Space: O(N) Stack
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

bool isSortedBrute(const vector<int>& arr) {
    int n = arr.size();
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) {
            if (arr[i] > arr[j]) return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> arr = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    cout << (isSortedBrute(arr) ? "true" : "false") << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++)

#include <vector>
using namespace std;

bool isSortedBetter(const vector<int>& arr) {
    for (int i = 1; i < (int)arr.size(); i++) {
        if (arr[i] < arr[i - 1]) return false;
    }
    return true;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> arr = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    cout << (isSortedBetter(arr) ? "true" : "false") << endl;

bool isSortedOptimal(const vector<int>& arr, int idx = 0) {

Problem 10

Sum of Digits in a Given Number

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy

Given a positive integer n, calculate and return the sum of all its decimal digits using recursive digit peeling (% 10 and / 10).

Example 1:
Input: n = 1234
Output: 10
Explanation: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10.
Example 2:
Input: n = 7
Output: 7
Explanation: Single digit number sum is itself.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Last digit n % 10 se nikalte hain, aur remaining digits n / 10 se pass karte hain. Recurrence: sumDigits(n) = (n % 10) + sumDigits(n / 10). Base case: jab n == 0, to return 0.
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: n = 345
  1. sumDigits(345) = (345 % 10) + sumDigits(34) = 5 + sumDigits(34)
  2. sumDigits(34) = (34 % 10) + sumDigits(3) = 4 + sumDigits(3)
  3. sumDigits(3) = (3 % 10) + sumDigits(0) = 3 + sumDigits(0)
  4. sumDigits(0) hits base case n == 0, returns 0.
  5. sumDigits(3) returns 3 + 0 = 3.
  6. sumDigits(34) returns 4 + 3 = 7.
  7. sumDigits(345) returns 5 + 7 = 12. Final Result = 12.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Convert number to string and iterate over characters summing values.
Time: O(log10(N)) • Space: O(log10(N))
🟡 Better Approach:
Iterative modulo loop while (n > 0) adding n % 10.
Time: O(log10(N)) • Space: O(1)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Functional recursive peeling (n % 10) + sumDigits(n / 10) with base condition n == 0.
Time: O(log10(N)) • Space: O(log10(N)) Auxiliary Stack
Time: O(log10(N)) Space: O(log10(N)) Stack
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

int sumOfDigitsBrute(int n) {
    string s = to_string(n);
    int sum = 0;
    for (char c : s) sum += (c - '0');
    return sum;
}

int main() {
    cout << sumOfDigitsBrute(12345) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

int sumOfDigitsBetter(int n) {
    int sum = 0;
    while (n > 0) {
        sum += (n % 10);
        n /= 10;
    }
    return sum;
}

int main() {
    cout << sumOfDigitsBetter(12345) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

int sumOfDigitsOptimal(int n) {
    if (n == 0) return 0;
    return (n % 10) + sumOfDigitsOptimal(n / 10);
}

int main() {
    cout << sumOfDigitsOptimal(12345) << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 11

Fibonacci Number & The Recursion Tree

Brute • Better • Optimal
Problem Statement Difficulty: Easy-Medium

Given an integer n, compute the $n$-th Fibonacci number $F(n)$, where $F(0) = 0$, $F(1) = 1$, and $F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2)$ for $n \ge 2$. Analyze naive tree recursion vs memoization vs space-optimized iteration.

Example 1:
Input: n = 6
Output: 8
Explanation: Fibonacci sequence: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8.
Example 2:
Input: n = 4
Output: 3
Explanation: F(4) = F(3) + F(2) = 2 + 1 = 3.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Naive recursion $F(n-1) + F(n-2)$ duplicate calculations karta hai ($O(2^n)$ exponential time). Memoization (Top-down DP) ya DP array se har state sirf ek baar solve hoti hai ($O(n)$ time). Aur sirf 2 variables (prev2, prev1) se space optimize hokar $O(1)$ ho jati hai!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Optimal Approach) Sample: n = 4 (Constant Space)
  1. Init: prev2 = 0, prev1 = 1
  2. Step 1 (i = 2): curr = 1 + 0 = 1, prev2 = 1, prev1 = 1
  3. Step 2 (i = 3): curr = 1 + 1 = 2, prev2 = 1, prev1 = 2
  4. Step 3 (i = 4): curr = 2 + 1 = 3, prev2 = 2, prev1 = 3
  5. Loop ends. Return prev1 = 3.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Naive double recursion fib(n-1) + fib(n-2) generating exponential recursion tree.
Time: O(2^N) • Space: O(N) Call Stack
🟡 Better Approach:
Memoization / Top-Down DP caching results in dp[n + 1] table.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) DP Array + Stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Space-optimized iterative bottom-up storing only last two states (prev2, prev1).
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
Time: O(N) Space: O(1)
🔴 1. Brute Force (C++) 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

int fibonacciBrute(int n) {
    if (n <= 1) return n;
    return fibonacciBrute(n - 1) + fibonacciBrute(n - 2);
}

int main() {
    cout << fibonacciBrute(6) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

int fibonacciBetter(int n, vector<int>& dp) {
    if (n <= 1) return n;
    if (dp[n] != -1) return dp[n];
    return dp[n] = fibonacciBetter(n - 1, dp) + fibonacciBetter(n - 2, dp);
}

int main() {
    int n = 6;
    vector<int> dp(n + 1, -1);
    cout << fibonacciBetter(n, dp) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (C++) 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

int fibonacciOptimal(int n) {
    if (n <= 1) return n;
    int prev2 = 0, prev1 = 1;
    for (int i = 2; i <= n; i++) {
        int curr = prev1 + prev2;
        prev2 = prev1;
        prev1 = curr;
    }
    return prev1;
}

int main() {
    cout << fibonacciOptimal(6) << endl;
    return 0;
}

1. Introduction: What is Sorting & Why Does It Matter?

Sorting computer science aur DSA ka sabse fundamental operation hai. Iska seedha matlab hai: kisi collection ya array ke elements ko ek predetermined systematic order (usually Ascending ya Descending) me rearrange karna.

Real-world software engineering me lagbhag har high-performance system sorting par depend karta hai. For example, Binary Search sirf sorted data par execute ho sakta hai (search time drops from $O(N)$ to $O(\log N)$), databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL) B-Trees index banane ke liye sorting use karte hain, aur e-commerce platforms search results ko price/rating ke according sort karte hain.
