💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Pura triangle generate karne ke 2 best ways hain:
• Way A (DP addition): Har cell mat[i][j] = mat[i-1][j-1] + mat[i-1][j].
• Way B (Row generator function): Har row row = 1..numRows ke liye Pascal II ka single-pass ratio generator call karo. Ye ultra-clean, modular, aur mathematical approach hai. Total operations = total elements = $O(N^2)$.
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (numRows = 4) Building Rows
Row 1: [1]
Row 2: [1, 1]
Row 3: [1, 1+1=2, 1] → [1, 2, 1]
Row 4: [1, 1+2=3, 2+1=3, 1] → [1, 3, 3, 1]
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
For every position (r, c), call a separate combination function nCr from scratch.
Time: O(N³) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Classic Dynamic Programming: set first and last elements to 1, fill inside elements using sum of parents above.
Time: O(N²) • Space: O(1) auxiliary (excluding answer)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Construct each row dynamically using the ratio formula ans = ans * (row - col) / col.
Time: O(N²) • Space: O(1) auxiliary

Problem 19 • Medium FAQ

Rotate Matrix by 90 Degrees Clockwise

Problem #48 • Core
Problem Statement Difficulty: Medium

You are given an n × n 2D matrix representing an image. Rotate the image by 90 degrees (clockwise) in-place without allocating another 2D matrix.

Example 1:
Input: matrix = [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]]
Output: [[7,4,1],[8,5,2],[9,6,3]]
Example 2:
Input: matrix = [[5,1,9,11],[2,4,8,10],[13,3,6,7],[15,14,12,16]]
Output: [[15,13,2,5],[14,3,4,1],[12,6,8,9],[16,7,10,11]]
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
90-degree clockwise rotation 2 simple geometric steps ka combination hota hai:
Step 1: Transpose Matrix: Rows ko columns me convert karo (swap matrix[i][j] with matrix[j][i] for all i < j).
Step 2: Reverse Each Row: Har horizontal row ko reverse kar do (reverse(row.begin(), row.end())). In do steps ke baad matrix perfectly 90 degree clockwise rotate ho jata hai without any extra space ($O(1)$ auxiliary space)!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Transpose + Reverse) 3 × 3 Matrix
Original: [[1,2,3], [4,5,6], [7,8,9]]
Step 1 (Transpose): [[1,4,7], [2,5,8], [3,6,9]]
Step 2 (Reverse Rows):
Row 0: [1,4,7] → [7,4,1]
Row 1: [2,5,8] → [8,5,2]
Row 2: [3,6,9] → [9,6,3]. Match!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Allocate an extra $N imes N$ matrix ans, map ans[j][n-1-i] = matrix[i][j], then copy back.
Time: O(N²) • Space: O(N²) extra
🟡 Better Approach:
Layer-by-layer 4-way cyclic rotation: simultaneously swap 4 corresponding edge cells clockwise.
Time: O(N²) • Space: O(1) in-place
🟢 Optimal Approach:
In-place Transpose followed by row-wise reversal. Extremely fast, cache-optimal, and elegant.
Time: O(N²) • Space: O(1) in-place

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

void rotateBetter(vector<vector<int>>& matrix) {
    int n = matrix.size();
    for (int i = 0; i < n / 2; i++) {
        for (int j = i; j < n - i - 1; j++) {
            int temp = matrix[i][j];
            matrix[i][j] = matrix[n - 1 - j][i];
            matrix[n - 1 - j][i] = matrix[n - 1 - i][n - 1 - j];
            matrix[n - 1 - i][n - 1 - j] = matrix[j][n - 1 - i];
            matrix[j][n - 1 - i] = temp;
        }
    }
}

    for (const auto& r : mat) {

🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Transpose + Reverse) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

void rotateOptimal(vector<vector<int>>& matrix) {
    int n = matrix.size();
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) {
            swap(matrix[i][j], matrix[j][i]);
        }
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        reverse(matrix[i].begin(), matrix[i].end());
    }
}

    rotateOptimal(mat);

    }

}
Problem 20 • FAQs (Medium)

Set Matrix Zeroes

Problem #73 • Core
Problem Statement Difficulty: Core / Medium

Given an m × n integer matrix, if an element is 0, set its entire row and column to 0 in-place without allocating extra 2D matrices.

Example 1:
Input: matrix = [[1,1,1],[1,0,1],[1,1,1]]
Output: [[1,0,1],[0,0,0],[1,0,1]]
Example 2:
Input: matrix = [[0,1,2,0],[3,4,5,2],[1,3,1,5]]
Output: [[0,0,0,0],[0,4,5,0],[0,3,1,0]]
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Extra array lene ki jagah matrix ki pehli row aur pehli column ko hi markers ki tarah use karo!
• matrix[..][0] row markers track karega.
• matrix[0][..] col markers track karega.
• matrix[0][0] par row 0 aur col 0 dono overlap hote hain, isliye column 0 ke liye ek alag boolean variable col0 = 1 banao. Sub-matrix [1..m-1][1..n-1] ko pehle zero set karo, fir 0th row aur 0th col ko appropriately zero karo! $O(1)$ space.
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (In-Place Markers) 3 × 3 with mat[1][1]=0
Scan: cell (1, 1) has 0 → mark mat[1][0]=0 and mat[0][1]=0
Inner matrix update: row 1 and col 1 become 0
Row 0 & Col 0: check mat[0][0] and col0 → untouched
Final: [[1,0,1], [0,0,0], [1,0,1]]
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
For every 0, mark row & col non-zeros with a special marker -1, then replace all -1 with 0.
Time: O((N×M)×(N+M)) • Space: O(1)
🟡 Better Approach:
Two auxiliary dummy arrays: row[m] and col[n] storing zero markers.
Time: O(N × M) • Space: O(N + M)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
In-place state encoding using matrix's 1st row, 1st col, and a single variable col0.
Time: O(N × M) • Space: O(1) in-place

#include <iostream>

void setZeroesOptimal(vector<vector<int>>& matrix) {

    int col0 = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
            if (matrix[i][j] == 0) {
                matrix[i][0] = 0;
                if (j != 0) matrix[0][j] = 0;
                else col0 = 0;
            }
        }
    }
    for (int i = 1; i < m; i++) {
        for (int j = 1; j < n; j++) {
            if (matrix[i][0] == 0 || matrix[0][j] == 0) {
                matrix[i][j] = 0;
            }
        }
    }
    if (matrix[0][0] == 0) {
        for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) matrix[0][j] = 0;
    }
    if (col0 == 0) {
        for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) matrix[i][0] = 0;
    }
}

Problem 21 • FAQs (Medium)

Two Sum: Check Pair with Given Target

Problem #1 • Basic
Problem Statement Difficulty: Basic / Easy

Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target. You may assume each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [2, 7, 11, 15], target = 9
Output: [0, 1]
Explanation: nums[0] + nums[1] == 9, return [0, 1].
Example 2:
Input: nums = [3, 2, 4], target = 6
Output: [1, 2]
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Agar hum kisi number x = nums[i] par khade hain, to hame pair banane ke liye doosra number more = target - x chahiye! Ek Hash Map (unordered_map<int, int>) maintain karo jo har number ka index store kare. Har step par check karo: kya more pehle map me dekha gaya hai? Agar haan, to [mpp[more], i] answer mil gaya! Agar nahi, to mpp[x] = i insert karke aage badho. Single linear pass $O(N)$!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Hash Map Lookup) [2, 7, 11, 15], target = 9
i = 0 (val 2): needed = 9 - 2 = 7 → not in map → map[2] = 0
i = 1 (val 7): needed = 9 - 7 = 2 → 2 is present in map at index 0!
Return [0, 1] immediately!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Two nested loops checking all possible pairs $(i, j)$ with $i < j$.
Time: O(N²) • Space: O(1)
🟡 Better Approach:
Store elements with indices in pairs, sort, and use Two Pointers.
Time: O(N log N) • Space: O(N)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Single pass Hash Map recording element indices with instantaneous complement check.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
Problem #1 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Nested Loop Scan) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

vector<int> twoSumBrute(const vector<int>& nums, int target) {
    int n = nums.size();
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) {
            if (nums[i] + nums[j] == target) return {i, j};
        }
    }
    return {};
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {2, 7, 11, 15};
    vector<int> res = twoSumBrute(nums, 9);
    cout << res[0] << " " << res[1] << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Sort + Two Pointers) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

vector<int> twoSumBetter(const vector<int>& nums, int target) {
    int n = nums.size();
    vector<pair<int, int>> arr(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) arr[i] = {nums[i], i};
    sort(arr.begin(), arr.end());
    int left = 0, right = n - 1;
    while (left < right) {
        int sum = arr[left].first + arr[right].first;
        if (sum == target) return {arr[left].second, arr[right].second};
        if (sum < target) left++;
        else right--;
    }
    return {};
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {2, 7, 11, 15};
    vector<int> res = twoSumBetter(nums, 9);
    cout << res[0] << " " << res[1] << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Hash Map Single Pass) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <unordered_map>
using namespace std;

vector<int> twoSumOptimal(const vector<int>& nums, int target) {
    unordered_map<int, int> mpp;
    int n = nums.size();
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        int more = target - nums[i];
        if (mpp.find(more) != mpp.end()) {
            return {mpp[more], i};
        }
        mpp[nums[i]] = i;
    }
    return {};
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {2, 7, 11, 15};
    vector<int> res = twoSumOptimal(nums, 9);
    cout << res[0] << " " << res[1] << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 22 • Medium FAQ

3 Sum: Unique Triplets Sum to Zero

Problem #15 • Core
Problem Statement Difficulty: Medium

Given an integer array nums, return all the unique triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] such that i ≠ j, i ≠ k, and j ≠ k, and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0. Duplicate triplets must not be returned.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [-1, 0, 1, 2, -1, -4]
Output: [[-1, -1, 2], [-1, 0, 1]]
Explanation: Triplets sum to 0 with distinct indices.
Example 2:
Input: nums = [0, 1, 1]
Output: []
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Duplicate triplets eliminate karne ka sabse powerful foundation hai Sorting ($O(N log N)$).
Array sort karne ke baad, pointer i ko fix karo ($0$ to $n-3$).
Agar i > 0 && nums[i] == nums[i-1] ho, to duplicate skip karo.
Remaining part ke liye Two Pointers lagao: left = i + 1 aur right = n - 1:
• sum == 0: Triplet mil gaya! Result me store karo, aur consecutive duplicates skip karo using while loops for both left and right.
• sum < 0: left++ (sum badhao).
• sum > 0: right-- (sum ghatao).
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Sorted Array) [-4, -1, -1, 0, 1, 2]
i=0 (nums[i]=-4): left=-1, right=2 → sum = -3 < 0 → left++ ... no triplet
i=1 (nums[i]=-1): left=-1, right=2 → sum = 0! Triplet [-1, -1, 2] → left++, right--
    left=0, right=1 → sum = 0! Triplet [-1, 0, 1]
i=2 (nums[i]=-1): nums[2] == nums[1] → Duplicate! Skip i=2
Final Triplets: [[-1, -1, 2], [-1, 0, 1]]
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
3 nested loops generating all triplets, sorted and stored in std::set<vector<int>>.
Time: O(N³ log K) • Space: O(2 × K)
🟡 Better Approach:
2 nested loops + Hash Set to look up target complement -(nums[i] + nums[j]).
Time: O(N² log K) • Space: O(N + K)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Sort + Two Pointers with in-place duplicate pointer hopping. Zero auxiliary data structures.
Time: O(N²) • Space: O(1) auxiliary

vector<vector<int>> threeSumBrute(vector<int>& nums) {

🟡 2. Better Approach (Hash Set Lookup) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <set>
#include <unordered_set>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

vector<vector<int>> threeSumBetter(vector<int>& nums) {
    int n = nums.size();
    set<vector<int>> st;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        unordered_set<int> hashset;
        for (int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) {
            int third = -(nums[i] + nums[j]);
            if (hashset.find(third) != hashset.end()) {
                vector<int> temp = {nums[i], nums[j], third};
                sort(temp.begin(), temp.end());
                st.insert(temp);
            }
            hashset.insert(nums[j]);
        }
    }
    return vector<vector<int>>(st.begin(), st.end());
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {-1, 0, 1, 2, -1, -4};
    vector<vector<int>> res = threeSumBetter(nums);
    for (const auto& t : res) cout << "[" << t[0] << "," << t[1] << "," << t[2] << "] ";
    cout << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Sort + Two Pointers) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

vector<vector<int>> threeSumOptimal(vector<int>& nums) {
    int n = nums.size();
    vector<vector<int>> ans;
    sort(nums.begin(), nums.end());

    for (int i = 0; i < n - 2; i++) {
        if (i > 0 && nums[i] == nums[i - 1]) continue;

        int left = i + 1, right = n - 1;
        while (left < right) {
            int sum = nums[i] + nums[left] + nums[right];
            if (sum == 0) {
                ans.push_back({nums[i], nums[left], nums[right]});
                while (left < right && nums[left] == nums[left + 1]) left++;
                while (left < right && nums[right] == nums[right - 1]) right--;
                left++;
                right--;
            } else if (sum < 0) {
                left++;
            } else {
                right--;
            }
        }
    }
    return ans;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {-1, 0, 1, 2, -1, -4};
    vector<vector<int>> res = threeSumOptimal(nums);
    for (const auto& t : res) cout << "[" << t[0] << "," << t[1] << "," << t[2] << "] ";
    cout << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 23 • Medium FAQ

4 Sum: Unique Quadruplets Sum to Target

Problem #18 • Pro
Problem Statement Difficulty: Medium-Hard / Pro

Given an array nums of n integers and an integer target, return an array of all the unique quadruplets [nums[a], nums[b], nums[c], nums[d]] such that nums[a] + nums[b] + nums[c] + nums[d] == target.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [1, 0, -1, 0, -2, 2], target = 0
Output: [[-2,-1,1,2], [-2,0,0,2], [-1,0,0,1]]
Example 2:
Input: nums = [2, 2, 2, 2, 2], target = 8
Output: [[2, 2, 2, 2]]
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
3Sum ka natural generalization!
1. Array ko pehle sort karo ($O(N log N)$).
2. Do nested loops lagao: i ($0$ to $n-4$) aur j ($i+1$ to $n-3$). Adjacent duplicate values skip karo (if (i > 0 && nums[i] == nums[i-1]) continue; and similarly for j).
3. Remaining do numbers ke liye Two Pointers k = j + 1 aur l = n - 1 use karo.
⚠️ Critical Overflow Pitfall: Chaar 32-bit integers ka sum integer limit ($2 imes 10^9$) exceed kar sakta hai! Isliye sum ko hamesha long long sum = (long long)nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] + nums[l]; compute karo.
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Target = 0) [-2, -1, 0, 0, 1, 2]
i = 0 (val = -2):
  • j = 1 (val = -1): k=2, l=5 → sum = -2-1+0+2 = -1 < 0 → k++ (k=3) → sum = 0! Add [-2, -1, 1, 2]
  • j = 2 (val = 0): k=3, l=5 → sum = -2+0+0+2 = 0! Add [-2, 0, 0, 2]
i = 1 (val = -1): j = 2 (val = 0): k=3, l=4 → sum = -1+0+0+1 = 0! Add [-1, 0, 0, 1]
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
4 nested loops with std::set<vector<int>> to filter duplicate quadruplets.
Time: O(N⁴) • Space: O(2 × K)
🟡 Better Approach:
3 nested loops + Hash Set to find complement target - (nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k]).
Time: O(N³ log K) • Space: O(N)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Sort + 2 Loops + Two Pointers with in-place duplicate skipping & 64-bit overflow prevention.
Time: O(N³) • Space: O(1) auxiliary

🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Sort + 2 Loops + Two Pointers) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

vector<vector<int>> fourSumOptimal(vector<int>& nums, int target) {
    int n = nums.size();
    vector<vector<int>> ans;
    sort(nums.begin(), nums.end());

    for (int i = 0; i < n - 3; i++) {
        if (i > 0 && nums[i] == nums[i - 1]) continue;

        for (int j = i + 1; j < n - 2; j++) {
            if (j > i + 1 && nums[j] == nums[j - 1]) continue;

            int k = j + 1, l = n - 1;
            while (k < l) {
                long long sum = (long long)nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] + nums[l];
                if (sum == target) {
                    ans.push_back({nums[i], nums[j], nums[k], nums[l]});
                    while (k < l && nums[k] == nums[k + 1]) k++;
                    while (k < l && nums[l] == nums[l - 1]) l--;
                    k++;
                    l--;
                } else if (sum < target) {
                    k++;
                } else {
                    l--;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return ans;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {1, 0, -1, 0, -2, 2};
    vector<vector<int>> res = fourSumOptimal(nums, 0);
    for (const auto& q : res) cout << "[" << q[0] << "," << q[1] << "," << q[2] << "," << q[3] << "] ";
    cout << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 24 • FAQs (Medium)

Sort an Array of 0s, 1s and 2s

Problem #75 • Core
Problem Statement Difficulty: Core / Medium

Given an array nums with n objects colored red, white, or blue (represented by integers 0, 1, and 2), sort them in-place so that objects of the same color are adjacent, in order 0, 1, and 2, without using the library sort.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [2, 0, 2, 1, 1, 0]
Output: [0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2]
Example 2:
Input: nums = [2, 0, 1]
Output: [0, 1, 2]
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Dutch National Flag (DNF) Algorithm: Array ko 3 pointers low = 0, mid = 0, high = n - 1 se 4 partitions me divide karo:
• [0 .. low-1]: saare 0s
• [low .. mid-1]: saare 1s
• [mid .. high]: abhi unsorted hai
• [high+1 .. n-1]: saare 2s
Loop while mid <= high:
• nums[mid] == 0: swap(nums[low], nums[mid]); low++; mid++;
• nums[mid] == 1: mid++;
• nums[mid] == 2: swap(nums[mid], nums[high]); high--; Single pass $O(N)$ me array sorted ho jata hai!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (DNF 3-Way Partition) [2, 0, 1]
Init: low=0, mid=0, high=2
mid=0 (val 2): swap(nums[0], nums[2]) → [1, 0, 2], high=1
mid=0 (val 1): mid++ (mid=1)
mid=1 (val 0): swap(nums[0], nums[1]) → [0, 1, 2], low=1, mid=2
mid=2 > high=1: Loop ends. Result: [0, 1, 2]
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Sort using std::sort.
Time: O(N log N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Two passes: pass 1 counts 0s, 1s, and 2s; pass 2 overwrites array.
Time: O(2N) = O(N) • Space: O(1)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Dutch National Flag 3-pointer partition in single pass.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) in-place

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

void sortColorsBetter(vector<int>& nums) {
    int c0 = 0, c1 = 0, c2 = 0;
    for (int x : nums) {
        if (x == 0) c0++;
        else if (x == 1) c1++;
        else c2++;
    }
    int idx = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < c0; i++) nums[idx++] = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < c1; i++) nums[idx++] = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < c2; i++) nums[idx++] = 2;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {2, 0, 2, 1, 1, 0};
    sortColorsBetter(nums);
    for (int x : nums) cout << x << " ";
    cout << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Dutch National Flag DNF) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

void sortColorsOptimal(vector<int>& nums) {
    int low = 0, mid = 0, high = (int)nums.size() - 1;
    while (mid <= high) {
        if (nums[mid] == 0) {
            swap(nums[low], nums[mid]);
            low++;
            mid++;
        } else if (nums[mid] == 1) {
            mid++;
        } else {
            swap(nums[mid], nums[high]);
            high--;
        }
    }
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {2, 0, 2, 1, 1, 0};
    sortColorsOptimal(nums);
    for (int x : nums) cout << x << " ";
    cout << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 25 • FAQs (Medium)

Kadane's Algorithm: Maximum Subarray Sum

Problem #53 • Core
Problem Statement Difficulty: Core / Medium

Given an integer array nums, find the contiguous subarray (containing at least one number) which has the largest sum and return its sum.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [-2, 1, -3, 4, -1, 2, 1, -5, 4]
Output: 6
Explanation: The subarray [4, -1, 2, 1] has the largest sum 6.
Example 2:
Input: nums = [5, 4, -1, 7, 8]
Output: 23
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Kadane's Algorithm: Har step par sum += nums[i] karte jao aur maximum sum maxi = max(maxi, sum) update karo. Agar kisi point par sum < 0 ho jaye, to ek negative sum ko aage carry karne se agle elements ka sum hamesha ghat hi jayega! Isliye jaise hi sum < 0 ho, usse aage carry forward mat karo aur sum = 0 reset kar do. Single pass $O(N)$!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Kadane) [-2, 1, -3, 4, -1, 2, 1]
-2: sum=-2 → maxi=-2 → sum < 0 → reset sum=0
1: sum=1 → maxi=1
-3: sum=-2 → sum < 0 → reset sum=0
4: sum=4 → maxi=4
-1: sum=3 → maxi=4
2: sum=5 → maxi=5
1: sum=6 → maxi=6. Result: 6
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
3 nested loops generating every possible subarray and computing its sum.
Time: O(N³) • Space: O(1)
🟡 Better Approach:
2 nested loops with running sum optimization.
Time: O(N²) • Space: O(1)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Kadane's Algorithm single pass with negative sum reset.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) in-place

#include <vector>
#include <climits>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

int maxSubArrayOptimal(const vector<int>& nums) {
    int sum = 0;
    int maxi = INT_MIN;
    for (int num : nums) {
        sum += num;
        if (sum > maxi) maxi = sum;
        if (sum < 0) sum = 0;
    }
    return maxi;
}

Problem 26 • FAQs (Medium)

Next Permutation

Problem #31 • Core
Problem Statement Difficulty: Core / Medium

Given an array of integers nums, find the lexicographically next greater permutation in-place. If no such permutation exists (the array is sorted descending), rearrange into the lowest possible order (sorted ascending).

Example 1:
Input: nums = [1, 2, 3]
Output: [1, 3, 2]
Example 2:
Input: nums = [3, 2, 1]
Output: [1, 2, 3]
Explanation: Array is in descending order, wraps around to lowest permutation.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
3-Step Canonical Algorithm:
1. Breakpoint: Right se scan karo aur pehla index ind dhundo jahan nums[ind] < nums[ind + 1] ho. Agar aisa koi index na mile, to array already last permutation hai, simply reverse(nums.begin(), nums.end()) kar do!
2. Swap Next Greater: Right se pehla element dhundo jo nums[ind] se strictly bada ho, aur unhe swap kar do!
3. Reverse Suffix: Index ind + 1 se lekar end tak ke elements ko reverse kar do taaki suffix ascending ho jaye. Time $O(N)$, Space $O(1)$.
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (3 Steps) [2, 1, 5, 4, 3, 0, 0]
Step 1 (Breakpoint): nums[1]=1 < nums[2]=5 → ind = 1
Step 2 (Next greater from right): nums[4]=3 > 1 → swap(nums[1], nums[4]) → [2, 3, 5, 4, 1, 0, 0]
Step 3 (Reverse suffix): reverse [5, 4, 1, 0, 0] → [0, 0, 1, 4, 5]
Final result: [2, 3, 0, 0, 1, 4, 5]
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Recursively generate all $N!$ permutations, sort them, find current, and return next.
Time: O(N! × N) • Space: O(N!)
🟡 Better Approach:
STL std::next_permutation(nums.begin(), nums.end()).
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
3-step in-place algorithmic scan: find breakpoint, swap next greater, reverse suffix.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) in-place
Problem #31 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Conceptual Permutation Tree) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

void recurPermute(int index, vector<int>& nums, vector<vector<int>>& ans) {
    if (index == (int)nums.size()) {
        ans.push_back(nums);
        return;
    }
    for (int i = index; i < (int)nums.size(); i++) {
        swap(nums[index], nums[i]);
        recurPermute(index + 1, nums, ans);
        swap(nums[index], nums[i]);
    }
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {1, 2, 3};
    vector<vector<int>> allPerms;
    recurPermute(0, nums, allPerms);
    cout << "Total permutations: " << allPerms.size() << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (STL next_permutation)

#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

void nextPermutationBetter(vector<int>& nums) {
    next_permutation(nums.begin(), nums.end());
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {1, 2, 3};
    nextPermutationBetter(nums);
    for (int x : nums) cout << x << " ";
    cout << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (3-Step Algorithm) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

void nextPermutationOptimal(vector<int>& nums) {
    int n = nums.size();
    int ind = -1;

    for (int i = n - 2; i >= 0; i--) {
        if (nums[i] < nums[i + 1]) {
            ind = i;
            break;
        }
    }

    if (ind == -1) {
        reverse(nums.begin(), nums.end());
        return;
    }

    for (int i = n - 1; i > ind; i--) {
        if (nums[i] > nums[ind]) {
            swap(nums[i], nums[ind]);
            break;
        }
    }

    reverse(nums.begin() + ind + 1, nums.end());
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {2, 1, 5, 4, 3, 0, 0};
    nextPermutationOptimal(nums);
    for (int x : nums) cout << x << " ";
    cout << endl;
    return 0;
}

Problem 27 • Hard FAQ

Majority Element-II (> ⌊n/3⌋ times)

Problem #229 • Core
Problem Statement Difficulty: Hard / Core

Given an integer array nums of size n, find all elements that appear more than ⌊n / 3⌋ times. The algorithm must run in linear $O(N)$ time and $O(1)$ space.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [3, 2, 3]
Output: [3]
Explanation: 3 appears 2 times, which is > 3/3 = 1.
Example 2:
Input: nums = [1, 2]
Output: [1, 2]
Explanation: Both appear 1 time, which is > 2/3 = 0.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Mathematical fact: kisi array me > ⌊n/3⌋ bar aane wale elements at most 2 hi ho sakte hain! (Kyunki 3 × (⌊n/3⌋ + 1) > n). Isliye hum Extended Boyer-Moore Voting Algorithm lagate hain with 2 candidate variables (el1, el2) aur 2 count variables (cnt1, cnt2):
• Agar cnt1 == 0 && x != el2 → el1 = x, cnt1 = 1.
• Agar cnt2 == 0 && x != el1 → el2 = x, cnt2 = 1.
• Agar x == el1 → cnt1++; agar x == el2 → cnt2++.
• Warna cnt1--; cnt2--; (3 distinct elements cancel each other!).
End me second linear pass se verify karo ki kya el1 ya el2 ka actual count > n/3 hai.
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (2-Candidate Voting) [1, 1, 1, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2]
After 1, 1, 1: el1=1, cnt1=3; el2=?, cnt2=0
After 3, 3: el1=1, cnt1=3; el2=3, cnt2=2
After 2: 2 != 1 and 2 != 3 → cnt1=2, cnt2=1
After 2: cnt1=1, cnt2=0
After 2: el2=2, cnt2=1. Candidates: 1 and 2.
Verification: count(1)=3 > 8/3=2, count(2)=3 > 2. Result: [1, 2]
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Count frequencies of every element using nested loops.
Time: O(N²) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Hash map frequency counting, then collect elements with frequency > $lfloor n/3 floor$.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Extended Boyer-Moore Voting Algorithm (2 candidates) + single verification pass.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) in-place
Problem #229 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Nested Loop Frequency) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

vector<int> majorityElement2Brute(const vector<int>& nums) {
    int n = nums.size();
    vector<int> ans;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (ans.size() == 0 || ans[0] != nums[i]) {
            int cnt = 0;
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
                if (nums[j] == nums[i]) cnt++;
            }
            if (cnt > n / 3) ans.push_back(nums[i]);
        }
        if (ans.size() == 2) break;
    }
    return ans;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {3, 2, 3};
    vector<int> res = majorityElement2Brute(nums);
    for (int x : res) cout << x << " ";
    cout << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Hash Map) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <unordered_map>
using namespace std;

vector<int> majorityElement2Better(const vector<int>& nums) {
    int n = nums.size();
    unordered_map<int, int> mpp;
    vector<int> ans;
    int threshold = (n / 3) + 1;

    for (int x : nums) {
        mpp[x]++;
        if (mpp[x] == threshold) {
            ans.push_back(x);
        }
        if (ans.size() == 2) break;
    }
    return ans;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {1, 2};
    vector<int> res = majorityElement2Better(nums);
    for (int x : res) cout << x << " ";
    cout << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Extended Boyer-Moore) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <climits>
using namespace std;

vector<int> majorityElement2Optimal(const vector<int>& nums) {
    int n = nums.size();
    int cnt1 = 0, cnt2 = 0;
    int el1 = INT_MIN, el2 = INT_MIN;

    for (int num : nums) {
        if (cnt1 == 0 && num != el2) {
            cnt1 = 1;
            el1 = num;
        } else if (cnt2 == 0 && num != el1) {
            cnt2 = 1;
            el2 = num;
        } else if (num == el1) {
            cnt1++;
        } else if (num == el2) {
            cnt2++;
        } else {
            cnt1--;
            cnt2--;
        }
    }

    cnt1 = 0; cnt2 = 0;
    for (int num : nums) {
        if (num == el1) cnt1++;
        else if (num == el2) cnt2++;
    }

    vector<int> ans;
    if (cnt1 > n / 3) ans.push_back(el1);
    if (cnt2 > n / 3) ans.push_back(el2);
    return ans;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {1, 1, 1, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2};
    vector<int> res = majorityElement2Optimal(nums);
    for (int x : res) cout << x << " ";
    cout << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 28 • Hard FAQ

Find the Repeating and Missing Number

Core Problem
Problem Statement Difficulty: Hard / Core

Given an unsorted array of size n with numbers from 1 to n. One number A occurs twice (repeating) and one number B is missing. Find and return [A, B].

Example 1:
Input: arr = [3, 1, 2, 5, 3]
Output: Repeating: 3, Missing: 4
Example 2:
Input: arr = [4, 3, 6, 2, 1, 1]
Output: Repeating: 1, Missing: 5
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Mathematics Method (2 Equations):
• Equation 1: S - Sn = A - B (Sum of array elements minus sum of 1..n).
• Equation 2: S2 - S2n = A² - B² = (A - B)(A + B).
Divide Eq 2 by Eq 1: A + B = (S2 - S2n) / (A - B).
Ab do simple linear equations hain: A - B = val1 aur A + B = val2. A = (val1 + val2) / 2, aur B = A - val1! $O(N)$ time aur $O(1)$ space without extra memory!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Math Equations) [3, 1, 2, 5, 3], n=5
Sum S: 3+1+2+5+3 = 14; Sn: 5(6)/2 = 15 → A - B = -1
Sum S2: 9+1+4+25+9 = 48; S2n: 5(6)(11)/6 = 55 → A² - B² = -7
A + B: -7 / (-1) = 7
Solve: A = (-1 + 7)/2 = 3, B = 3 - (-1) = 4. Result: [3, 4]
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Count occurrence of each number $1$ to $N$ with nested linear scans.
Time: O(N²) • Space: O(1)
🟡 Better Approach:
Frequency array of size $N+1$ to record counts in a single pass.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Mathematical sum equations ($S, S^2$) or Bitwise XOR bucket partitioning.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) in-place
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Nested Loop Scan) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

vector<int> findMissingRepeatingBrute(const vector<int>& arr) {
    int n = arr.size();
    int repeating = -1, missing = -1;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        int cnt = 0;
        for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
            if (arr[j] == i) cnt++;
        }
        if (cnt == 2) repeating = i;
        else if (cnt == 0) missing = i;
        if (repeating != -1 && missing != -1) break;
    }
    return {repeating, missing};
}

int main() {
    vector<int> arr = {3, 1, 2, 5, 3};
    vector<int> res = findMissingRepeatingBrute(arr);
    cout << "Repeating: " << res[0] << ", Missing: " << res[1] << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Frequency Array) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

vector<int> findMissingRepeatingBetter(const vector<int>& arr) {
    int n = arr.size();
    vector<int> freq(n + 1, 0);
    for (int x : arr) freq[x]++;
    int repeating = -1, missing = -1;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        if (freq[i] == 2) repeating = i;
        else if (freq[i] == 0) missing = i;
    }
    return {repeating, missing};
}

int main() {
    vector<int> arr = {3, 1, 2, 5, 3};
    vector<int> res = findMissingRepeatingBetter(arr);
    cout << "Repeating: " << res[0] << ", Missing: " << res[1] << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Math Equations O(1) Space) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

vector<int> findMissingRepeatingOptimal(const vector<int>& arr) {
    long long n = arr.size();
    long long sn = (n * (n + 1)) / 2;
    long long s2n = (n * (n + 1) * (2 * n + 1)) / 6;

    long long s = 0, s2 = 0;
    for (long long x : arr) {
        s += x;
        s2 += (x * x);
    }

    long long val1 = s - sn; // A - B
    long long val2 = s2 - s2n; // A^2 - B^2 = (A-B)(A+B)
    val2 = val2 / val1; // A + B

    long long A = (val1 + val2) / 2; // Repeating
    long long B = A - val1;          // Missing

    return {(int)A, (int)B};
}

int main() {
    vector<int> arr = {3, 1, 2, 5, 3};
    vector<int> res = findMissingRepeatingOptimal(arr);
    cout << "Repeating: " << res[0] << ", Missing: " << res[1] << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 29 • Hard FAQ

Count Inversions in an Array

Pro Problem
Problem Statement Difficulty: Hard / Pro

Given an integer array arr, find the Inversion Count. Two elements arr[i] and arr[j] form an inversion if i < j and arr[i] > arr[j].

Example 1:
Input: arr = [5, 3, 2, 4, 1]
Output: 8
Explanation: Inversions: (5,3), (5,2), (5,4), (5,1), (3,2), (3,1), (2,1), (4,1).
Example 2:
Input: arr = [2, 4, 1, 3, 5]
Output: 3
Explanation: Inversions: (2,1), (4,1), (4,3).
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Modified Merge Sort! Jab hum do sorted subarrays [low..mid] aur [mid+1..high] ko merge kar rahe hote hain: Agar arr[left] > arr[right], to kyunki left half already sorted hai, arr[left] se lekar arr[mid] tak ke sabhi elements arr[right] se bade honge! Isliye hum direct count += (mid - left + 1) add kar lete hain! Divide and conquer se pure array ka inversion count $O(N log N)$ me calculate ho jata hai.
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Merge Inversion Count) Left=[2, 4], Right=[1, 3]
left=0 (val 2), right=0 (val 1): 2 > 1 → arr[left..mid] all > 1! count += (1 - 0 + 1) = 2. Pairs: (2,1), (4,1). right++
left=0 (val 2), right=1 (val 3): 2 ≤ 3 → no inversion. left++
left=1 (val 4), right=1 (val 3): 4 > 3 → count += (1 - 1 + 1) = 1. Pair: (4,3). right++
Total inversions for this merge = 3.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Check all pairs $(i, j)$ with $i < j$ and increment count if $arr[i] > arr[j]$.
Time: O(N²) • Space: O(1)
🟡 Better Approach:
Binary Indexed Tree (Fenwick Tree) with coordinate compression.
Time: O(N log N) • Space: O(N)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Modified Divide-and-Conquer Merge Sort counting cross-inversions in $O(N log N)$.
Time: O(N log N) • Space: O(N)
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (All Pairs) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

long long countInversionsBrute(const vector<int>& arr) {
    long long cnt = 0;
    int n = arr.size();
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) {
            if (arr[i] > arr[j]) cnt++;
        }
    }
    return cnt;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> arr = {5, 3, 2, 4, 1};
    cout << countInversionsBrute(arr) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Recursive Tree) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

long long mergeCount(vector<int>& arr, int low, int mid, int high) {
    vector<int> temp;
    int left = low, right = mid + 1;
    long long cnt = 0;

    while (left <= mid && right <= high) {
        if (arr[left] <= arr[right]) {
            temp.push_back(arr[left++]);
        } else {
            temp.push_back(arr[right++]);
            cnt += (mid - left + 1);
        }
    }
    while (left <= mid) temp.push_back(arr[left++]);
    while (right <= high) temp.push_back(arr[right++]);
    for (int i = low; i <= high; i++) arr[i] = temp[i - low];
    return cnt;
}

long long mergeSort(vector<int>& arr, int low, int high) {
    long long cnt = 0;
    if (low >= high) return cnt;
    int mid = low + (high - low) / 2;
    cnt += mergeSort(arr, low, mid);
    cnt += mergeSort(arr, mid + 1, high);
    cnt += mergeCount(arr, low, mid, high);
    return cnt;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> arr = {5, 3, 2, 4, 1};
    cout << mergeSort(arr, 0, arr.size() - 1) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Optimized Inversion Counter) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

long long merge(vector<int>& arr, int low, int mid, int high) {
    vector<int> temp;
    int left = low, right = mid + 1;
    long long cnt = 0;

    while (left <= mid && right <= high) {
        if (arr[left] <= arr[right]) {
            temp.push_back(arr[left++]);
        } else {
            temp.push_back(arr[right++]);
            cnt += (mid - left + 1);
        }
    }
    while (left <= mid) temp.push_back(arr[left++]);
    while (right <= high) temp.push_back(arr[right++]);
    for (int i = low; i <= high; i++) arr[i] = temp[i - low];
    return cnt;
}

long long countInversionsOptimal(vector<int>& arr, int low, int high) {
    long long cnt = 0;
    if (low >= high) return cnt;
    int mid = low + (high - low) / 2;
    cnt += countInversionsOptimal(arr, low, mid);
    cnt += countInversionsOptimal(arr, mid + 1, high);
    cnt += merge(arr, low, mid, high);
    return cnt;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> arr = {5, 3, 2, 4, 1};
    cout << countInversionsOptimal(arr, 0, arr.size() - 1) << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 30 • Hard FAQ

Reverse Pairs: nums[i] > 2 × nums[j]

Problem #493 • Pro
Problem Statement Difficulty: Hard / Pro

Given an integer array nums, return the number of reverse pairs. A reverse pair is defined as (i, j) such that 0 ≤ i < j < nums.length and nums[i] > 2 × nums[j].

Example 1:
Input: nums = [1, 3, 2, 3, 1]
Output: 2
Explanation: Reverse pairs: (1, 4) since 3 > 2(1), and (3, 4) since 3 > 2(1).
Example 2:
Input: nums = [2, 4, 3, 5, 1]
Output: 3
Explanation: Reverse pairs: (1, 4) [4 > 2], (2, 4) [3 > 2], (3, 4) [5 > 2].
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Count Inversions ki tarah Merge Sort hi use karenge, lekin condition me 2 × nums[j] hone ki wajah se count merge step ke sath mix nahi ho sakta. Key Technique (Pre-merge Two Pointers count): Merge karne se theek pehle, dono sorted halves [low..mid] aur [mid+1..high] par Two Pointers lagao:
• Pointer right = mid + 1.
• Loop i from low to mid: jab tak right ≤ high && nums[i] > 2LL * nums[right], tab tak right++ aage badhao.
• Har i ke liye count += (right - (mid + 1)) add karo! Kyunki dono arrays sorted hain, right pointer peeche kabhi nahi jata (monotonicity). Isliye counting $O(N)$ me hoti hai! Total time: $O(N log N)$.
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run Left=[3], Right=[1]
i = 0 (val 3): 3 > 2 × 1 (3 > 2) is True!
right advances past 1 → count += 1
Pairs found = 1. Then standard merge produces [1, 3].
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Nested loops checking $nums[i] > 2LL imes nums[j]$ for all $i < j$.
Time: O(N²) • Space: O(1)
🟡 Better Approach:
Binary Indexed Tree with coordinate compression and frequency queries.
Time: O(N log N) • Space: O(N)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Modified Merge Sort with pre-merge Two Pointers monotonic counting scan.
Time: O(N log N) • Space: O(N)
Problem #493 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Nested Loop with 64-bit cast) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

int reversePairsBrute(const vector<int>& nums) {
    int cnt = 0, n = nums.size();
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) {
            if ((long long)nums[i] > 2LL * nums[j]) {
                cnt++;
            }
        }
    }
    return cnt;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {1, 3, 2, 3, 1};
    cout << reversePairsBrute(nums) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Binary Search Counting) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

int countPairs(vector<int>& nums, int low, int mid, int high) {
    int right = mid + 1;
    int cnt = 0;
    for (int i = low; i <= mid; i++) {
        while (right <= high && (long long)nums[i] > 2LL * nums[right]) {
            right++;
        }
        cnt += (right - (mid + 1));
    }
    return cnt;
}

void merge(vector<int>& nums, int low, int mid, int high) {
    vector<int> temp;
    int left = low, right = mid + 1;
    while (left <= mid && right <= high) {
        if (nums[left] <= nums[right]) temp.push_back(nums[left++]);
        else temp.push_back(nums[right++]);
    }
    while (left <= mid) temp.push_back(nums[left++]);
    while (right <= high) temp.push_back(nums[right++]);
    for (int i = low; i <= high; i++) nums[i] = temp[i - low];
}

int mergeSortHelper(vector<int>& nums, int low, int high) {
    if (low >= high) return 0;
    int mid = low + (high - low) / 2;
    int cnt = mergeSortHelper(nums, low, mid);
    cnt += mergeSortHelper(nums, mid + 1, high);
    cnt += countPairs(nums, low, mid, high);
    merge(nums, low, mid, high);
    return cnt;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {1, 3, 2, 3, 1};
    cout << mergeSortHelper(nums, 0, nums.size() - 1) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Merge Sort Pre-Count) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

int countPairsOptimal(vector<int>& nums, int low, int mid, int high) {
    int right = mid + 1;
    int cnt = 0;
    for (int i = low; i <= mid; i++) {
        while (right <= high && (long long)nums[i] > 2LL * nums[right]) {
            right++;
        }
        cnt += (right - (mid + 1));
    }
    return cnt;
}

void mergeOptimal(vector<int>& nums, int low, int mid, int high) {

    while (left <= mid && right <= high) {

        else temp.push_back(nums[right++]);

int reversePairsOptimal(vector<int>& nums, int low, int high) {

    cnt += reversePairsOptimal(nums, mid + 1, high);
    cnt += countPairsOptimal(nums, low, mid, high);
    mergeOptimal(nums, low, mid, high);

}

Problem 31 • Hard FAQ

Maximum Product Subarray in an Array

Problem #152 • Core
Problem Statement Difficulty: Hard / Core

Given an integer array nums, find a contiguous non-empty subarray that has the largest product, and return that maximum product.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [2, 3, -2, 4]
Output: 6
Explanation: [2, 3] has the largest product 6.
Example 2:
Input: nums = [-2, 0, -1]
Output: 0
Explanation: The result cannot be 2, because [-2, -1] is not a contiguous subarray.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Product me negative numbers tricky hote hain: do negative numbers milkar positive product bana dete hain! Prefix & Suffix Observation:
• Agar negatives even hain, to pure array ka product maximum hoga.
• Agar negatives odd hain, to kisi ek negative ko exclude karke answer ya to prefix part me hoga ya suffix part me!
• Agar 0 aaye, to product 0 ban jata hai, isliye 0 ke baad product ko wapas 1 reset karna hota hai. Isliye ek pass left-to-right (pref) aur ek pass right-to-left (suff) chalao. max(pref, suff) hamesha correct maximum product dega! $O(N)$ time, $O(1)$ space.
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Prefix & Suffix) [2, 3, -2, 4]
i = 0: pref = 2, suff = 4 → maxi = max(2, 4) = 4
i = 1: pref = 2*3 = 6, suff = 4*(-2) = -8 → maxi = max(4, 6, -8) = 6
i = 2: pref = 6*(-2) = -12, suff = -8*3 = -24 → maxi = 6
i = 3: pref = -12*4 = -48, suff = -24*2 = -48 → maxi = 6
Final Answer: 6
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Calculate products of all possible subarrays using 2 nested loops.
Time: O(N²) • Space: O(1)
🟡 Better Approach:
Modified Kadane's algorithm maintaining both currMax and currMin simultaneously.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Prefix and Suffix simultaneous linear scan with instantaneous zero-reset.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) in-place
Problem #152 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (All Subarrays) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
#include <climits>
using namespace std;

int maxProductBrute(const vector<int>& nums) {
    int n = nums.size();
    long long maxi = LLONG_MIN;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        long long prod = 1;
        for (int j = i; j < n; j++) {
            prod *= nums[j];
            maxi = max(maxi, prod);
        }
    }
    return (int)maxi;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {2, 3, -2, 4};
    cout << maxProductBrute(nums) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Modified Kadane) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

int maxProductBetter(const vector<int>& nums) {
    int n = nums.size();
    int prod1 = nums[0], prod2 = nums[0], result = nums[0];
    for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) {
        int temp = max({nums[i], prod1 * nums[i], prod2 * nums[i]});
        prod2 = min({nums[i], prod1 * nums[i], prod2 * nums[i]});
        prod1 = temp;
        result = max(result, prod1);
    }
    return result;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {2, 3, -2, 4};
    cout << maxProductBetter(nums) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Prefix & Suffix Dual Scan) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
#include <climits>
using namespace std;

int maxProductOptimal(const vector<int>& nums) {
    int n = nums.size();
    long long pref = 1, suff = 1;
    long long ans = INT_MIN;

    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (pref == 0) pref = 1;
        if (suff == 0) suff = 1;

        pref *= nums[i];
        suff *= nums[n - i - 1];

        ans = max({ans, pref, suff});
    }
    return (int)ans;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {2, 3, -2, 4};
    cout << maxProductOptimal(nums) << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 32 • Hard FAQ

Merge Two Sorted Arrays Without Extra Space

Problem #88 • Core
Problem Statement Difficulty: Hard / Core

Given two sorted arrays arr1 of size n and arr2 of size m, merge them in-place such that after merging, arr1 contains the first n smallest elements in sorted order, and arr2 contains the remaining m elements in sorted order. No extra array allowed!

Example 1:
Input: arr1 = [1, 4, 7, 8, 10], arr2 = [2, 3, 9]
Output: arr1 = [1, 2, 3, 4, 7], arr2 = [8, 9, 10]
Example 2:
Input: arr1 = [1, 5, 9], arr2 = [2, 3, 8]
Output: arr1 = [1, 2, 3], arr2 = [5, 8, 9]
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Gap Method (Shell Sort intuition): Dono arrays ko ek continuous virtual array of size n + m imagine karo.
1. Initial gap = ceil((n + m) / 2.0).
2. Pointers left = 0 aur right = gap.
3. Dono pointers ke elements compare karo: agar element[left] > element[right] to unhe swap kar do!
4. Dono pointers aage badhao jab tak right < n + m.
5. Har pass ke baad gap = ceil(gap / 2.0) karo. Jab gap == 1 par pass ho jaye, to array naturally perfectly sorted ho jata hai in $O((n+m) log(n+m))$ time and $O(1)$ space!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Gap Method) n=5, m=3, total=8
Initial gap: ceil(8 / 2) = 4
left=0 (arr1[0]=1), right=4 (arr1[4]=10) → 1 ≤ 10 ok
left=1 (arr1[1]=4), right=5 (arr2[0]=2) → 4 > 2 → swap!
left=2 (arr1[2]=7), right=6 (arr2[1]=3) → 7 > 3 → swap!
Next gap: ceil(4 / 2) = 2, then gap: 1 → All sorted in-place!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Merge both into a temporary buffer of size $N+M$, then copy back into arr1 and arr2.
Time: O(N + M) • Space: O(N + M) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Compare from end of arr1 and start of arr2, swap if out-of-order, then independently sort both.
Time: O(min(N, M) + N log N + M log M) • Space: O(1)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Gap Method (Shell Sort partitioning) directly comparing and swapping across arrays in-place.
Time: O((N + M) log(N + M)) • Space: O(1) in-place
Problem #88 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Auxiliary Array of size N+M) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

void mergeBrute(vector<int>& a, vector<int>& b) {
    int n = a.size(), m = b.size();
    vector<int> temp(n + m);
    int i = 0, j = 0, k = 0;
    while (i < n && j < m) {
        if (a[i] <= b[j]) temp[k++] = a[i++];
        else temp[k++] = b[j++];
    }
    while (i < n) temp[k++] = a[i++];
    while (j < m) temp[k++] = b[j++];

    for (int idx = 0; idx < n; idx++) a[idx] = temp[idx];
    for (int idx = 0; idx < m; idx++) b[idx] = temp[n + idx];
}

int main() {
    vector<int> a = {1, 4, 7, 8, 10}, b = {2, 3, 9};
    mergeBrute(a, b);
    for (int x : a) cout << x << " ";
    cout << "| ";
    for (int x : b) cout << x << " ";
    cout << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Swap & Sort) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

void mergeBetter(vector<int>& a, vector<int>& b) {
    int n = a.size(), m = b.size();
    int left = n - 1, right = 0;
    while (left >= 0 && right < m) {
        if (a[left] > b[right]) {
            swap(a[left], b[right]);
            left--;
            right++;
        } else {
            break;
        }
    }
    sort(a.begin(), a.end());
    sort(b.begin(), b.end());
}

int main() {
    vector<int> a = {1, 4, 7, 8, 10}, b = {2, 3, 9};
    mergeBetter(a, b);
    for (int x : a) cout << x << " ";
    cout << "| ";
    for (int x : b) cout << x << " ";
    cout << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Shell Sort Gap Method) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
using namespace std;

void swapIfGreater(vector<int>& a, vector<int>& b, int ind1, int ind2) {
    if (a[ind1] > b[ind2]) {
        swap(a[ind1], b[ind2]);
    }
}

void mergeOptimal(vector<int>& a, vector<int>& b) {
    int n = a.size(), m = b.size();
    int len = n + m;
    int gap = (len / 2) + (len % 2);

    while (gap > 0) {
        int left = 0, right = left + gap;
        while (right < len) {
            // Case 1: left in a, right in b
            if (left < n && right >= n) {
                swapIfGreater(a, b, left, right - n);
            }
            // Case 2: both in b
            else if (left >= n) {
                swapIfGreater(b, b, left - n, right - n);
            }
            // Case 3: both in a
            else {
                swapIfGreater(a, a, left, right);
            }
            left++;
            right++;
        }
        if (gap == 1) break;
        gap = (gap / 2) + (gap % 2);
    }
}

int main() {
    vector<int> a = {1, 4, 7, 8, 10}, b = {2, 3, 9};
    mergeOptimal(a, b);
    for (int x : a) cout << x << " ";
    cout << "| ";
    for (int x : b) cout << x << " ";
    cout << endl;
    return 0;
}

Module 1: Theory

1/1

Hashing Theory, Hash Functions, Collision Resolution (Chaining & Open Addressing) & STL Maps

Standard Interview Roadmap • C++ Optimal
Theory • Foundations

Basic Hashing: Architecture, Collision Resolution & STL Maps

Core Theory • Basic
Core Concept Time Complexity: O(1) Avg Lookup

Hashing ek technique hai jo kisi bhi arbitrary key ko ek fixed-size integer index me convert karti hai using a Hash Function. Iska primary objective linear search ke $O(N)$ lookup ko constant time $O(1)$ average lookup me optimize karna hai.

1. Common Hash Functions:
• Division Method: h(k) = k mod m (jahan m usually ek prime number hota hai taaki collisions minimize ho sakein).
• Mid-Square Method: k ka square nikalo aur middle digits ko index select karo.
• Folding Method: Key ko equal parts me divide karke add karo.
2. Collision Resolution Techniques:
• Separate Chaining (Open Hashing): Har table bucket ek linked list maintain karti hai. Collision aane par naye node ko list me append karte hain.
• Open Addressing (Closed Hashing): Table ke andar hi next available slot search karte hain:
  - Linear Probing: h'(k, i) = (h(k) + i) mod m (creates primary clustering)
  - Quadratic Probing: h'(k, i) = (h(k) + c1*i + c2*i²) mod m
  - Double Hashing: h'(k, i) = (h1(k) + i * h2(k)) mod m
💡 Map vs Unordered Map (C++ STL Decision Matrix):
std::map: Self-balancing Red-Black BST par implemented hota hai. Keys hamesha sorted order me rehti hain. Lookup, Insert, Delete guaranteed $O(log N)$ hoti hain.
std::unordered_map: Hash table + separate chaining par based hota hai. Average case $O(1)$ hota hai, lekin worst-case me collisions hone par $O(N)$ ho sakta hai (TLE risk on large adversarial test cases).
🔍 Direct Array Hashing (Number vs Character) Direct Indexing
• Integer Array Hashing: Max element agar $M le 10^7$ ho, to global array int hash[10000001] = {0}; banake index hash[nums[i]]++ karte hain. Inside main() max limit $10^6$ hoti hai.
• Character Array Hashing: Lowercase English letters ke liye hash[s[i] - 'a']++ (size 26). All ASCII characters ke liye hash[s[i]]++ (size 256). Lookup strictly $O(1)$ aur memory strictly $O(1)$!
Time Complexity: Direct Array: O(1) | Unordered Map: O(1) Avg, O(N) Worst | Map: O(log N)
Space Complexity: O(U) jahan U unique elements ya alphabet size hai.
⚪ 1. Integer Array Hashing (Direct Addressing) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

const int MAX_VAL = 1000000;
int hashArr[MAX_VAL + 1] = {0};

void precomputeFrequencies(const vector<int>& nums) {
    for (int x : nums) {
        if (x >= 0 && x <= MAX_VAL) {
            hashArr[x]++;
        }
    }
}

int queryFrequency(int number) {
    if (number >= 0 && number <= MAX_VAL) {
        return hashArr[number];
    }
    return 0;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {1, 3, 2, 1, 3, 4, 3};
    precomputeFrequencies(nums);
    cout << "Freq of 3: " << queryFrequency(3) << endl;
    cout << "Freq of 1: " << queryFrequency(1) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Character Array Hashing (ASCII Direct Map) 
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

vector<int> computeCharFreq(const string& s) {
    vector<int> charHash(256, 0);
    for (char c : s) {
        charHash[(unsigned char)c]++;
    }
    return charHash;
}

int main() {
    string s = "abracadabra";
    vector<int> freq = computeCharFreq(s);
    cout << "Count of 'a': " << freq['a'] << endl;
    cout << "Count of 'b': " << freq['b'] << endl;
    cout << "Count of 'r': " << freq['r'] << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. STL std::unordered_map (Hash Table Frequency Map) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <unordered_map>
using namespace std;

unordered_map<int, int> buildFrequencyMap(const vector<int>& nums) {
    unordered_map<int, int> freqMap;
    for (int x : nums) {
        freqMap[x]++;
    }
    return freqMap;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {10, -5, 10, 20, -5, 10};
    unordered_map<int, int> freq = buildFrequencyMap(nums);
    for (auto& [key, count] : freq) {
        cout << key << " -> " << count << endl;
    }
    return 0;
}

Problem 2 • FAQs

Longest Consecutive Sequence in an Array

Problem #128 • Core
Problem Statement Difficulty: Medium / Core

Given an unsorted array of integers nums, return the length of the longest consecutive elements sequence. You must write an algorithm that runs in O(n) time. Elements do not need to be contiguous in the original array.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [100, 4, 200, 1, 3, 2]
Output: 4
Explanation: Longest consecutive sequence is [1, 2, 3, 4], length = 4.
Example 2:
Input: nums = [0, 3, 7, 2, 5, 8, 4, 6, 0, 1]
Output: 9
Explanation: Longest sequence is [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8], length = 9.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Sabhi elements ko ek unordered_set me insert karo taaki $O(1)$ lookup mile.
• Kisi element x ke liye, agar x - 1 set me present hai, to iska matlab x sequence ka starting point nahi ho sakta! Use skip karo.
• Agar x - 1 set me nahi hai, tabhi x sequence ka START hai. Tab x + 1, x + 2... check karte hue streak count karo. Is filter se har element at most 2 times visit hota hai → Total time strictly $O(N)$!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Hash Set Filter) [100, 4, 200, 1, 3, 2]
Num (Num - 1) in Set? Is Start? Streak Count Max Streak
10099 not in setYes (Start)100 → 11
43 is in setNo (Skip)-1
200199 not in setYes (Start)200 → 11
10 not in setYes (Start)1 → 2 → 3 → 4 (Length 4)4
32 is in setNo (Skip)-4
21 is in setNo (Skip)-4
Time Complexity: Brute: O(N²) | Sorting: O(N log N) | Set: O(N)
Space Complexity: O(N) for the unordered_set.
⚪ 1. Brute Force (Linear Scan for Next Elements) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

bool linearSearch(const vector<int>& nums, int target) {
    for (int x : nums) {
        if (x == target) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

int longestConsecutiveBrute(vector<int>& nums) {
    int n = nums.size();
    if (n == 0) return 0;
    int longest = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        int x = nums[i];
        int count = 1;
        while (linearSearch(nums, x + 1)) {
            x++;
            count++;
        }
        longest = max(longest, count);
    }
    return longest;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {100, 4, 200, 1, 3, 2};
    cout << longestConsecutiveBrute(nums) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Sorting + Duplicate Handling) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

int longestConsecutiveBetter(vector<int>& nums) {
    int n = nums.size();
    if (n == 0) return 0;
    sort(nums.begin(), nums.end());
    int longest = 1, currStreak = 0, lastSmaller = -1e9;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (nums[i] - 1 == lastSmaller) {
            currStreak++;
            lastSmaller = nums[i];
        } else if (nums[i] != lastSmaller) {
            currStreak = 1;
            lastSmaller = nums[i];
        }
        longest = max(longest, currStreak);
    }
    return longest;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {100, 4, 200, 1, 3, 2};
    cout << longestConsecutiveBetter(nums) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Hash Set Start Filter - O(N)) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <unordered_set>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

int longestConsecutiveOptimal(vector<int>& nums) {
    int n = nums.size();
    if (n == 0) return 0;
    unordered_set<int> st(nums.begin(), nums.end());
    int longest = 1;

    for (int it : st) {
        if (st.find(it - 1) == st.end()) {
            int cnt = 1;
            int x = it;
            while (st.find(x + 1) != st.end()) {
                x++;
                cnt++;
            }
            longest = max(longest, cnt);
        }
    }
    return longest;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {100, 4, 200, 1, 3, 2};
    cout << longestConsecutiveOptimal(nums) << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 3 • FAQs

Longest Subarray with Sum K (Positives & Negatives)

Standard / Problem #325 • Core
Problem Statement Difficulty: Medium / Core

Given an array nums of size n containing both positive, negative, and zero integers, and an integer k, find the length of the longest continuous subarray whose elements sum to k. If no such subarray exists, return 0.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [10, 5, 2, 7, 1, 9], k = 15
Output: 4
Explanation: Subarray [5, 2, 7, 1] sums to 5+2+7+1 = 15, length = 4.
Example 2:
Input: nums = [-1, 2, 3], k = 6
Output: 0
Explanation: No subarray exists whose sum equals 6.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Prefix Sum Principle: Agar index i tak running prefix sum S hai, aur pehle kisi index j par prefix sum S - k tha, to index j + 1 se i tak ka subarray sum guaranteed k hoga!
• unordered_map<long long, int> me prefix_sum → first_index store karo.
• Agar sum == k ho, to length direct i + 1 hogi.
• Agar (sum - k) map me pehle se hai, to maxLen = max(maxLen, i - map[sum - k]).
• Crucial Note: Agar sum pehle se map me hai to use dobara update mat karo taaki sabse pehla (leftmost) index persist kare aur subarray length maximize ho sake!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Prefix Map) [10, 5, 2, 7, 1, 9], k=15
i nums[i] Prefix Sum rem = (Sum - 15) rem in Map? Max Len
01010-5No0
15150Sum == k!2
22172No2
37249No2
412510Yes at idx 0!4 (4 - 0)
593419No4
Time Complexity: Brute: O(N²) | Hash Map (All): O(N) | Two Pointers (Positives): O(N)
Space Complexity: Hash Map: O(N) | Two Pointers: O(1)
🔴 1. Brute Force (All Subarrays Sum Check) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

int longestSubarrayBrute(const vector<int>& nums, int k) {
    int n = nums.size();
    int maxLen = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        long long sum = 0;
        for (int j = i; j < n; j++) {
            sum += nums[j];
            if (sum == k) {
                maxLen = max(maxLen, j - i + 1);
            }
        }
    }
    return maxLen;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {10, 5, 2, 7, 1, 9};
    cout << longestSubarrayBrute(nums, 15) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Prefix Sum Map - Positives & Negatives) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

int longestSubarrayWithSumKMap(const vector<int>& nums, int k) {
    int n = nums.size();
    unordered_map<long long, int> preMap;
    long long sum = 0;
    int maxLen = 0;

    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        sum += nums[i];

        if (sum == k) {
            maxLen = max(maxLen, i + 1);
        }

        long long rem = sum - k;
        if (preMap.find(rem) != preMap.end()) {
            int len = i - preMap[rem];
            maxLen = max(maxLen, len);
        }

        if (preMap.find(sum) == preMap.end()) {
            preMap[sum] = i;
        }
    }
    return maxLen;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {10, 5, 2, 7, 1, 9};
    cout << longestSubarrayWithSumKMap(nums, 15) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (2 Pointers Greedy - Positives Only) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

int longestSubarrayPositivesTwoPointers(const vector<int>& nums, int k) {
    int n = nums.size();
    int left = 0, right = 0;
    long long sum = nums[0];
    int maxLen = 0;

    while (right < n) {
        while (left <= right && sum > k) {
            sum -= nums[left];
            left++;
        }
        if (sum == k) {
            maxLen = max(maxLen, right - left + 1);
        }
        right++;
        if (right < n) sum += nums[right];
    }
    return maxLen;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {10, 5, 2, 7, 1, 9};
    cout << longestSubarrayPositivesTwoPointers(nums, 15) << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 4 • FAQs

Largest Subarray with Sum 0

Core • High Frequency
Problem Statement Difficulty: Medium / Core

Given an array nums of size n containing both positive and negative integers, return the length of the longest continuous subarray with sum equal to 0.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [15, -2, 2, -8, 1, 7, 10, 23]
Output: 5
Explanation: Subarray [-2, 2, -8, 1, 7] sums to 0, length = 5.
Example 2:
Input: nums = [1, 2, 3]
Output: 0
Explanation: No subarray has sum equal to 0.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Prefix Sum Equality Property: Agar index j par prefix sum S tha, aur aage chalke index i par bhi prefix sum S hi rehta hai, to iska guaranteed matlab hai ki index j + 1 se i ke beech ke sabhi elements ka net sum 0 hai!
• Har prefix sum ki first occurrence index ko unordered_map<int, int> me store karo.
• Agar sum == 0 ho, to length direct i + 1 hai.
• Agar sum pehle dekha ja chuka hai, to maxLen = max(maxLen, i - map[sum]).
• Same sum dobara aane par map me overwrite nahi karte!

i val Sum Action / Map State Subarray Len Max Len
01515Insert (15 → 0)-0
1-213Insert (13 → 1)-0
2215Seen 15 at idx 0!2 - 0 = 22
3-87Insert (7 → 3)-2
418Insert (8 → 4)-2
5715Seen 15 at idx 0!5 - 0 = 55
61025Insert (25 → 6)-5
72348Insert (48 → 7)-5
Time Complexity: Brute: O(N²) | Hash Map: O(N)
Space Complexity: O(N) for prefix sum map.
⚪ 1. Brute Force (Nested Loops O(N^2)) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

int maxLenZeroSumBrute(const vector<int>& nums) {
    int n = nums.size();
    int maxLen = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        int sum = 0;
        for (int j = i; j < n; j++) {
            sum += nums[j];
            if (sum == 0) {
                maxLen = max(maxLen, j - i + 1);
            }
        }
    }
    return maxLen;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {15, -2, 2, -8, 1, 7, 10, 23};
    cout << maxLenZeroSumBrute(nums) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Prefix Sum Array Comparison) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

int maxLenZeroSumBetter(const vector<int>& nums) {
    int n = nums.size();
    vector<int> pre(n);
    pre[0] = nums[0];
    for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) pre[i] = pre[i - 1] + nums[i];

    int maxLen = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (pre[i] == 0) maxLen = max(maxLen, i + 1);
        for (int j = 0; j < i; j++) {
            if (pre[i] == pre[j]) {
                maxLen = max(maxLen, i - j);
            }
        }
    }
    return maxLen;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {15, -2, 2, -8, 1, 7, 10, 23};
    cout << maxLenZeroSumBetter(nums) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Hash Map First Index O(N)) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

int maxLenZeroSumOptimal(const vector<int>& nums) {
    int n = nums.size();
    unordered_map<int, int> firstSeen;
    int sum = 0;
    int maxLen = 0;

    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        sum += nums[i];

        if (sum == 0) {
            maxLen = i + 1;
        } else if (firstSeen.find(sum) != firstSeen.end()) {
            maxLen = max(maxLen, i - firstSeen[sum]);
        } else {
            firstSeen[sum] = i;
        }
    }
    return maxLen;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {15, -2, 2, -8, 1, 7, 10, 23};
    cout << maxLenZeroSumOptimal(nums) << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 5 • FAQs

Count Subarrays with Given Sum K

Problem #560 • Core
Problem Statement Difficulty: Medium / Core

Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, return the total number of continuous subarrays whose sum equals to k.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [1, 1, 1], k = 2
Output: 2
Explanation: Subarrays [1, 1] at indices [0, 1] and [1, 2] both sum to 2.
Example 2:
Input: nums = [1, 2, 3], k = 3
Output: 2
Explanation: Subarrays [1, 2] and [3] sum to 3.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Prefix Sum Frequency Map: Yahan hume sirf maximum length nahi, balki total count nikalna hai.
• Agar index i tak running sum prefixSum hai, to koi bhi pichla prefix sum jo prefixSum - k ke barabar ho, ek valid subarray banata hai!
• Isliye hum ek unordered_map<int, int> prefixFreq maintain karte hain jo har prefix sum ki frequency track karta hai.
• Base Case: Start me prefixFreq[0] = 1 set karna zaroori hai, taaki jab koi prefix sum direct k ke barabar ho, to wo count ho sake!
• Har step par: ans += prefixFreq[prefixSum - k], then prefixFreq[prefixSum]++.
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (Frequency Accumulator) [1, 1, 1], k=2
i val Prefix Sum Target (Sum - 2) Map[Target] Total Count
Init-0-Map: {0: 1}0
0111 - 2 = -10 (Not found)0
1122 - 2 = 01 (from Map[0])1
2133 - 2 = 11 (from Map[1])2
Time Complexity: Brute: O(N²) | Hash Map: O(N)
Space Complexity: O(N) for frequency hash map.
⚪ 1. Brute Force (All Subarrays Summation) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

int subarraySumBrute(const vector<int>& nums, int k) {
    int n = nums.size();
    int count = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        int sum = 0;
        for (int j = i; j < n; j++) {
            sum += nums[j];
            if (sum == k) count++;
        }
    }
    return count;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {1, 1, 1};
    cout << subarraySumBrute(nums, 2) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Prefix Cumulative Sum Array) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

int subarraySumBetter(const vector<int>& nums, int k) {
    int n = nums.size();
    vector<int> prefix(n + 1, 0);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i];
    }

    int count = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int j = i; j < n; j++) {
            if (prefix[j + 1] - prefix[i] == k) {
                count++;
            }
        }
    }
    return count;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {1, 1, 1};
    cout << subarraySumBetter(nums, 2) << endl;
    return 0;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Prefix Sum + Frequency Map - O(N)) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <unordered_map>
using namespace std;

int subarraySumOptimal(const vector<int>& nums, int k) {
    int n = nums.size();
    unordered_map<int, int> prefixFreq;
    prefixFreq[0] = 1;
    int runningSum = 0;
    int count = 0;

    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        runningSum += nums[i];
        int target = runningSum - k;
        if (prefixFreq.find(target) != prefixFreq.end()) {
            count += prefixFreq[target];
        }
        prefixFreq[runningSum]++;
    }
    return count;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {1, 1, 1};
    cout << subarraySumOptimal(nums, 2) << endl;
    return 0;
}
Problem 6 • FAQs

Count Subarrays with Given XOR K

InterviewBit • Pro
Problem Statement Difficulty: Pro / Hard

Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, find the total number of continuous subarrays having bitwise XOR of their elements equal to k.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [4, 2, 2, 6, 4], k = 6
Output: 4
Explanation: Subarrays are [4, 2], [4, 2, 2, 6, 4], [2, 2, 6], and [6]. Each XORs to 6.
Example 2:
Input: nums = [5, 6, 7, 8, 9], k = 5
Output: 2
Explanation: Subarrays are [5] and [5, 6, 7, 8, 9] (5^6^7^8^9 = 5).
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
XOR Cancellation Equation: Maan lijiye index i tak running prefix XOR XR hai. Hume ek pehla prefix XOR X chahiye taaki beech ka subarray XOR k ban sake:
XR ^ X = k ⇔ X = XR ^ k (dono sides me k se XOR karne par).
• Matlab current running XOR XR ke liye, agar pichle kisi prefix ka XOR XR ^ k tha, to wo subarray answer me count hoga!
• unordered_map<int, int> xorFreq me har prefix XOR ka count maintain karo.
• Base Case: Start me xorFreq[0] = 1 karo (empty prefix XOR is 0).
• Target: x = xr ^ k. count += xorFreq[x], then xorFreq[xr]++. Time $O(N)$!
🔍 Step-by-Step Dry Run (XOR Map) [4, 2, 2, 6, 4], k=6
i val Running XR Target X = (XR ^ 6) Map[Target] Total Count
Init-0-Map: {0: 1}0
0444 ^ 6 = 200
126 (4^2)6 ^ 6 = 01 (from Map[0])1
224 (6^2)4 ^ 6 = 201
362 (4^6)2 ^ 6 = 42 (from Map[4])3
446 (2^4)6 ^ 6 = 01 (from Map[0])4
Time Complexity: Brute: O(N²) | Hash Map: O(N)
Space Complexity: O(N) for frequency hash map.
⚪ 1. Brute Force (All Subarrays XOR Computation) 
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

int subarraysWithXorKBrute(const vector<int>& nums, int k) {
    int n = nums.size();
    int count = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        int xr = 0;
        for (int j = i; j < n; j++) {
            xr ^= nums[j];
            if (xr == k) count++;
        }
    }
    return count;
}

int main() {
    vector<int> nums = {4, 2, 2, 6, 4};
    cout << subarraysWithXorKBrute(nums, 6) << endl;
    return 0;
}

    int n = nums.size();

    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        prefXor[i + 1] = prefXor[i] ^ nums[i];
    }

    int count = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int j = i; j < n; j++) {
            if ((prefXor[j + 1] ^ prefXor[i]) == k) {

            }
        }

    return count;
}

Fundamentals (3 Problems)

3 Problems
Problem 1 • Fundamentals

Search X in Sorted Array (Binary Search)

Easy Problem #704
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

Given an array of integers nums sorted in ascending order, and an integer target, write a function to search target in nums. If target exists, return its index. Otherwise, return -1. You must write an algorithm with O(log n) runtime complexity.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [-1, 0, 3, 5, 9, 12], target = 9
Output: 4
Explanation: 9 exists in nums and its index is 4.
Example 2:
Input: nums = [-1, 0, 3, 5, 9, 12], target = 2
Output: -1
Explanation: 2 does not exist in nums, so return -1.
Example 3:
Input: nums = [5], target = 5
Output: 0
Explanation: Target found at index 0.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Sorted array me binary search ki search space har step par aadhi ho jati hai. Pointers low = 0 aur high = n - 1 lo. mid = low + (high - low) / 2 calculate karo. Agar nums[mid] == target, answer mil gaya! Agar nums[mid] < target, target right half me hai (low = mid + 1). Warna left half me hai (high = mid - 1).
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Scan array elements left to right comparing each element with target.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Divide and conquer recursive function passing low and high bounds.
Time: O(log N) • Space: O(log N) recursion call stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Standard in-place iterative while loop with mid overflow protection. O(log N) time and O(1) space.
Time: O(log N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Problem #704 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Linear Search Traversal) 
int searchBrute(vector<int>& nums, int target) {
    for (int i = 0; i < (int)nums.size(); i++) {
        if (nums[i] == target) return i;
    }
    return -1;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Recursive Binary Search) 
int bsRec(const vector<int>& nums, int low, int high, int target) {
    if (low > high) return -1;
    int mid = low + (high - low) / 2;
    if (nums[mid] == target) return mid;
    if (nums[mid] < target) return bsRec(nums, mid + 1, high, target);
    return bsRec(nums, low, mid - 1, target);
}
int searchBetter(vector<int>& nums, int target) {
    return bsRec(nums, 0, (int)nums.size() - 1, target);
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Iterative Two-Pointer Binary Search) 
int searchOptimal(vector<int>& nums, int target) {
    int low = 0;
    int high = (int)nums.size() - 1;
    while (low <= high) {
        int mid = low + (high - low) / 2;
        if (nums[mid] == target) {
            return mid;
        } else if (nums[mid] < target) {
            low = mid + 1;
        } else {
            high = mid - 1;
        }
    }
    return -1;
}
Problem 2 • Fundamentals

Implement Lower Bound

Easy Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

Given a sorted array of integers arr and an integer x, find the lower bound of x. The lower bound is the smallest index ind such that arr[ind] >= x. If no such element exists, return the size of the array N.

Example 1:
Input: arr = [1, 2, 8, 10, 11, 12, 19], x = 5
Output: 2
Explanation: Smallest element >= 5 is 8, which is at index 2.
Example 2:
Input: arr = [1, 2, 8, 10, 11, 12, 19], x = 20
Output: 7
Explanation: No element >= 20. Array length 7 is returned.
Example 3:
Input: arr = [3, 5, 8, 15, 19], x = 8
Output: 2
Explanation: arr[2] == 8 >= 8.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Lower bound matlab pehla index jaha element $\ge x$ ho. Agar arr[mid] >= x hai, to mid ek probable answer hai (ans = mid), aur hume aur chhota index mil sakta hai isliye left half me search karo (high = mid - 1). Agar arr[mid] < x ho, to answer right me hi hoga (low = mid + 1).
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Iterate from index 0 to n-1. Return first index where arr[i] >= x.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Use C++ standard library lower_bound function returning iterator offset.
Time: O(log N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Record ans = mid whenever arr[mid] >= x and search left. Runs in O(log N) time and O(1) space.
Time: O(log N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Linear Scan from Left) 
int lowerBoundBrute(vector<int>& arr, int n, int x) {
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (arr[i] >= x) return i;
    }
    return n;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (STL std::lower_bound) 
int lowerBoundBetter(vector<int>& arr, int n, int x) {
    return lower_bound(arr.begin(), arr.end(), x) - arr.begin();
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Custom Binary Search with Answer Recording) 
int lowerBoundOptimal(vector<int>& arr, int n, int x) {
    int low = 0, high = n - 1;
    int ans = n;
    while (low <= high) {
        int mid = low + (high - low) / 2;
        if (arr[mid] >= x) {
            ans = mid;
            high = mid - 1;
        } else {
            low = mid + 1;
        }
    }
    return ans;
}
Problem 3 • Fundamentals

Implement Upper Bound

Easy Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

Given a sorted array of integers arr and an integer x, find the upper bound of x. The upper bound is the smallest index ind such that arr[ind] > x. If no such element exists, return N.

Example 1:
Input: arr = [2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 8, 11, 11, 12], x = 6
Output: 3
Explanation: Smallest element strictly > 6 is 7, at index 3.
Example 2:
Input: arr = [2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 8, 11, 11, 12], x = 12
Output: 9
Explanation: No element > 12. Returns size 9.
Example 3:
Input: arr = [1, 2, 5], x = 0
Output: 0
Explanation: arr[0] = 1 > 0.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Upper bound lower bound jaisa hi hai, bas difference ye hai ki yaha condition strictly greater than hai: arr[mid] > x. Agar condition satisfy hoti hai, to ans = mid note karo aur left half me jao (high = mid - 1). Warna right half me jao (low = mid + 1).
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Iterate from index 0 to n-1. Return first index where arr[i] > x.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Call std::upper_bound to find iterator pointing strictly greater than x.
Time: O(log N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Check arr[mid] > x; update ans = mid and move high = mid - 1. O(log N) time and O(1) space.
Time: O(log N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Linear Scan from Left)

int upperBoundBetter(vector<int>& arr, int n, int x) {

🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Custom Binary Search with Answer Recording) 
int upperBoundOptimal(vector<int>& arr, int n, int x) {
    int low = 0, high = n - 1;
    int ans = n;
    while (low <= high) {
        int mid = low + (high - low) / 2;
        if (arr[mid] > x) {
            ans = mid;
            high = mid - 1;
        } else {
            low = mid + 1;
        }
    }
    return ans;
}

Problem 4 • Logic Building

Search Insert Position

Easy Problem #35
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

Given a sorted array of distinct integers and a target value, return the index if the target is found. If not, return the index where it would be if it were inserted in order. You must write an algorithm with O(log n) runtime complexity.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [1, 3, 5, 6], target = 5
Output: 2
Explanation: 5 is found at index 2.
Example 2:
Input: nums = [1, 3, 5, 6], target = 2
Output: 1
Explanation: 2 would be inserted between 1 and 3, which is index 1.
Example 3:
Input: nums = [1, 3, 5, 6], target = 7
Output: 4
Explanation: 7 is inserted at the end of the array, index 4.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Search Insert Position basically wahi index hai jaha par pehla element $\ge target$ milta hai—yani Lower Bound of target! Jab binary search loop low <= high terminate hota hai aur element nahi milta, to low hamesha correct insertion index par point kar raha hota hai!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Scan array from 0 to n-1. Return first index i where nums[i] >= target; if none, return n.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Call std::lower_bound to find iterator offset in logarithmic time.
Time: O(log N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Run while low <= high. If found return mid, otherwise return low at loop termination. O(log N) time and O(1) space.
Time: O(log N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary

        if (nums[mid] == target) {
