Problem 3 • String Conversions

Roman to Integer

Easy Problem #13
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

Given a Roman numeral string s, convert it to an integer. The symbols and values are: I=1, V=5, X=10, L=50, C=100, D=500, M=1000.

Example 1:
Input: s = "III"
Output: 3
Explanation: III = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.
Example 2:
Input: s = "LVIII"
Output: 58
Explanation: L = 50, V = 5, III = 3. Sum = 58.
Example 3:
Input: s = "MCMXCIV"
Output: 1994
Explanation: M=1000, CM=900, XC=90, IV=4. Total = 1994.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Roman numbers me rule hota hai: Agar current symbol apne agle symbol se chhota ho (jaise 'I' before 'V' = 4, 'X' before 'L' = 40), to subtract hota hai total -= curr. Warna add hota hai total += curr.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Replace 6 subtraction instances (IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM) with single characters, then accumulate values.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) string copy
🟡 Better Approach:
Look up each symbol in unordered_map. If curr < next, subtract curr, else add curr.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) hash map space
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Eliminate hash map hashing overhead using direct helper switch function. Runs in O(N) time and strictly O(1) space.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Problem #13 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Subtractive Substring Replacement) 
int romanToIntBrute(string s) {
    vector<pair<string, int>> specials = {
        {"IV", 4}, {"IX", 9}, {"XL", 40}, {"XC", 90}, {"CD", 400}, {"CM", 900}
    };
    int total = 0;
    for (auto& p : specials) {
        size_t pos;
        while ((pos = s.find(p.first)) != string::npos) {
            total += p.second;
            s.replace(pos, 2, " ");
        }
    }
    unordered_map<char, int> m = {{'I',1},{'V',5},{'X',10},{'L',50},{'C',100},{'D',500},{'M',1000}};
    for (char c : s) if (m.count(c)) total += m[c];
    return total;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Hash Map Lookahead Comparison) 
int romanToIntBetter(string s) {
    unordered_map<char, int> m = {
        {'I', 1}, {'V', 5}, {'X', 10}, {'L', 50},
        {'C', 100}, {'D', 500}, {'M', 1000}
    };
    int total = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < (int)s.size(); i++) {
        if (i + 1 < (int)s.size() && m[s[i]] < m[s[i + 1]]) {
            total -= m[s[i]];
        } else {
            total += m[s[i]];
        }
    }
    return total;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Direct Switch-Case Array Lookup) 
inline int charVal(char c) {
    switch(c) {
        case 'I': return 1;
        case 'V': return 5;
        case 'X': return 10;
        case 'L': return 50;
        case 'C': return 100;
        case 'D': return 500;
        case 'M': return 1000;
        default: return 0;
    }
}
int romanToIntOptimal(string s) {
    int total = 0;
    int n = s.size();
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        int curr = charVal(s[i]);
        if (i + 1 < n && curr < charVal(s[i + 1])) {
            total -= curr;
        } else {
            total += curr;
        }
    }
    return total;
}
Problem 4 • String Conversions

String to Integer (atoi)

Medium Problem #8
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Implement the myAtoi(string s) function, which converts a string to a 32-bit signed integer. Follow the 4-step algorithm: 1) Ignore leading whitespace. 2) Check '+' or '-' sign. 3) Read integer digits until non-digit. 4) Clamp to [INT_MIN, INT_MAX] if overflow.

Example 1:
Input: s = "42"
Output: 42
Explanation: Digits 4 and 2 form integer 42.
Example 2:
Input: s = " -042"
Output: -42
Explanation: Leading spaces ignored, negative sign applied, leading zero dropped: -42.
Example 3:
Input: s = "1337c0d3"
Output: 1337
Explanation: Parsing stops at non-digit character 'c'.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Overflow protection interview me critical hoti hai! long long accumulator har environment me allow nahi hota. 32-bit safe math ke liye check karo: agar res > INT_MAX / 10 ho ya res == INT_MAX / 10 && digit > 7 ho, to overflow guaranteed hai, sign ke hisab se INT_MAX ya INT_MIN return kar do.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Trim leading whitespace, use std::stringstream to extract candidate integer, check bounds.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) stream space
🟡 Better Approach:
Accumulate in 64-bit integer, clamp to [INT_MIN, INT_MAX] on each digit iteration.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Strictly 32-bit math. Check overflow condition before multiplying by 10. O(N) time and O(1) space.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Problem #8 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Stringstream Parsing with Manual Validation) 
int myAtoiBrute(string s) {
    int i = 0;
    while (i < (int)s.size() && s[i] == ' ') i++;
    if (i == (int)s.size()) return 0;
    int sign = 1;
    if (s[i] == '+' || s[i] == '-') {
        if (s[i] == '-') sign = -1;
        i++;
    }
    long long num = 0;
    while (i < (int)s.size() && isdigit(s[i])) {
        num = num * 10 + (s[i] - '0');
        if (sign == 1 && num > INT_MAX) return INT_MAX;
        if (sign == -1 && -num < INT_MIN) return INT_MIN;
        i++;
    }
    return (int)(num * sign);
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Long Long Accumulator with Clamp) 
int myAtoiBetter(string s) {
    int i = 0, n = s.size();
    while (i < n && s[i] == ' ') i++;
    int sign = 1;
    if (i < n && (s[i] == '+' || s[i] == '-')) {
        if (s[i] == '-') sign = -1;
        i++;
    }
    long long res = 0;
    while (i < n && isdigit(s[i])) {
        res = res * 10 + (s[i] - '0');
        if (sign == 1 && res >= INT_MAX) return INT_MAX;
        if (sign == -1 && -res <= INT_MIN) return INT_MIN;
        i++;
    }
    return (int)(res * sign);
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (32-Bit Proactive Overflow Guard) 
int myAtoiOptimal(string s) {
    int i = 0, n = s.size();
    while (i < n && s[i] == ' ') i++;
    int sign = 1;
    if (i < n && (s[i] == '+' || s[i] == '-')) {
        if (s[i] == '-') sign = -1;
        i++;
    }
    int res = 0;
    while (i < n && isdigit(s[i])) {
        int digit = s[i] - '0';
        if (res > INT_MAX / 10 || (res == INT_MAX / 10 && digit > 7)) {
            return (sign == 1) ? INT_MAX : INT_MIN;
        }
        res = res * 10 + digit;
        i++;
    }
    return res * sign;
}

Module 3: Substring Problems (3 Problems)

3 Problems
Problem 5 • Substring Search

Count Number of Substrings with Exactly K Distinct Characters

Medium Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given a string s consisting of lowercase English alphabets and an integer k, count the total number of substrings that contain exactly k distinct characters.

Example 1:
Input: s = "pqpqs", k = 2
Output: 7
Explanation: Substrings with 2 distinct chars: "pq", "pqp", "pqpq", "qp", "qpq", "pq", "qs". Total = 7.
Example 2:
Input: s = "aabacbebebe", k = 3
Output: 10
Explanation: 10 substrings contain exactly 3 distinct characters.
Example 3:
Input: s = "abc", k = 1
Output: 3
Explanation: "a", "b", "c" each have exactly 1 distinct character.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Sliding window se 'exactly k' nikalna mushkil hota hai kyunki window expand karte waqt distinct count increase hota hai aur shrink par decrease. Lekin standard trick hai: exactly(k) = atMost(k) - atMost(k - 1)! 'At most k' distinct characters wali substrings O(N) two-pointer sliding window se bahut aasani se nikal aati hain!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Generate all O(N^2) substrings, insert into unordered_set to check if set.size() == k.
Time: O(N^3) • Space: O(N) set space
🟡 Better Approach:
Fix start index i, expand j maintaining freq[26] and distinct counter.
Time: O(N^2) • Space: O(26) = O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Compute count of substrings with at most k distinct characters using two pointers, then subtract atMost(k - 1). O(N) time and O(1) space.
Time: O(2N) = O(N) • Space: O(26) = O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (All Substrings Generation with Set) 
long long countSubstringsBrute(string s, int k) {
    long long count = 0;
    int n = s.size();
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int j = i; j < n; j++) {
            unordered_set<char> distinct;
            for (int l = i; l <= j; l++) distinct.insert(s[l]);
            if ((int)distinct.size() == k) count++;
        }
    }
    return count;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Nested Loops with Frequency Array) 
long long countSubstringsBetter(string s, int k) {
    long long ans = 0;
    int n = s.size();
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        int freq[26] = {0};
        int distinct = 0;
        for (int j = i; j < n; j++) {
            if (freq[s[j] - 'a'] == 0) distinct++;
            freq[s[j] - 'a']++;
            if (distinct == k) ans++;
            else if (distinct > k) break;
        }
    }
    return ans;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Sliding Window: atMost(k) - atMost(k - 1)) 
long long atMostK(string& s, int k) {
    if (k <= 0) return 0;
    int left = 0, distinct = 0;
    int freq[26] = {0};
    long long count = 0;
    for (int right = 0; right < (int)s.size(); right++) {
        if (freq[s[right] - 'a'] == 0) distinct++;
        freq[s[right] - 'a']++;
        while (distinct > k) {
            freq[s[left] - 'a']--;
            if (freq[s[left] - 'a'] == 0) distinct--;
            left++;
        }
        count += (right - left + 1);
    }
    return count;
}
long long countSubstringsOptimal(string s, int k) {
    return atMostK(s, k) - atMostK(s, k - 1);
}
Problem 6 • Palindromes

Longest Palindromic Substring

Medium Problem #5
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given a string s, return the longest palindromic substring in s.

Example 1:
Input: s = "babad"
Output: "bab"
Explanation: "aba" is also a valid answer of maximum length 3.
Example 2:
Input: s = "cbbd"
Output: "bb"
Explanation: Longest palindromic substring is "bb" of length 2.
Example 3:
Input: s = "a"
Output: "a"
Explanation: Single character is a palindrome.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Ek palindrome apne center se dono taraf symmetric hota hai. String me 2N - 1 centers ho sakte hain: N single-character centers (odd length jaise 'aba') aur N - 1 two-character centers (even length jaise 'abba'). Har center se outward expand karo expandAroundCenter(i, i) aur expandAroundCenter(i, i+1). Max length record kar lo!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Generate all O(N^2) substrings, check each with two pointers in O(N).
Time: O(N^3) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
dp[i][j] is true if s[i..j] is palindrome. Build from length 1 to n.
Time: O(N^2) • Space: O(N^2) DP table space
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Expand outwards from every index i as odd center (i, i) and even center (i, i+1). O(N^2) time and O(1) space.
Time: O(N^2) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Problem #5 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (All Substrings Palindrome Check) 
bool isPalin(const string& s, int i, int j) {
    while (i < j) { if (s[i++] != s[j--]) return false; }
    return true;
}
string longestPalindromeBrute(string s) {
    int maxLen = 0, start = 0, n = s.size();
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int j = i; j < n; j++) {
            if (isPalin(s, i, j) && (j - i + 1) > maxLen) {
                maxLen = j - i + 1;
                start = i;
            }
        }
    }
    return s.substr(start, maxLen);
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Dynamic Programming Table O(N^2) Space) 
string longestPalindromeBetter(string s) {
    int n = s.size();
    if (n <= 1) return s;
    vector<vector<bool>> dp(n, vector<bool>(n, false));
    int start = 0, maxLen = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) dp[i][i] = true;
    for (int i = 0; i < n - 1; i++) {
        if (s[i] == s[i + 1]) { dp[i][i + 1] = true; start = i; maxLen = 2; }
    }
    for (int len = 3; len <= n; len++) {
        for (int i = 0; i <= n - len; i++) {
            int j = i + len - 1;
            if (s[i] == s[j] && dp[i + 1][j - 1]) {
                dp[i][j] = true;
                if (len > maxLen) { start = i; maxLen = len; }
            }
        }
    }
    return s.substr(start, maxLen);
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Expand Around Center (Odd & Even)) 
int expand(const string& s, int l, int r) {
    while (l >= 0 && r < (int)s.size() && s[l] == s[r]) {
        l--; r++;
    }
    return r - l - 1;
}
string longestPalindromeOptimal(string s) {
    int start = 0, maxLen = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < (int)s.size(); i++) {
        int len1 = expand(s, i, i);
        int len2 = expand(s, i, i + 1);
        int len = max(len1, len2);
        if (len > maxLen) {
            maxLen = len;
            start = i - (len - 1) / 2;
        }
    }
    return s.substr(start, maxLen);
}
Problem 7 • Substring Search

Sum of Beauty of All Substrings

Medium Problem #1781
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

The beauty of a string is the difference between the most frequent character frequency and the least frequent non-zero character frequency. Given a string s, return the sum of beauty of all its substrings.

Example 1:
Input: s = "aabcb"
Output: 5
Explanation: Substrings with non-zero beauty: "aab"(1), "aabc"(1), "aabcb"(1), "abcb"(1), "bcb"(1). Sum = 5.
Example 2:
Input: s = "aabcbaa"
Output: 17
Explanation: Sum of beauties over all valid substrings is 17.
Example 3:
Input: s = "aaa"
Output: 0
Explanation: All substrings have equal min and max frequencies (beauty = 0).
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Har substring s[i..j] ke liye beauty calculate karni hai: beauty = maxFreq - minFreq (sirf non-zero frequencies ka min). Agar hum outer loop i = 0 to n-1 chalayein aur inner loop j = i to n-1 chalayein, to frequency array freq[26] ko incrementally update kar sakte hain bina substring ko bar-bar re-scan kiye!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Generate all substrings, populate unordered_map, find min and max frequency.
Time: O(N^3) • Space: O(26) map space
🟡 Better Approach:
Fix start i, expand j updating freq[26], scan 26 entries for min and max.
Time: O(26 * N^2) • Space: O(26) = O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Maintain maxFreq dynamically on each character insertion, evaluate minFreq across active characters. O(26 * N^2) time and O(1) space.
Time: O(26 * N^2) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Problem #1781 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (All Substrings Generation with Map) 
int beautySumBrute(string s) {
    int total = 0, n = s.size();
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int j = i; j < n; j++) {
            unordered_map<char, int> freq;
            for (int k = i; k <= j; k++) freq[s[k]]++;
            int maxF = 0, minF = INT_MAX;
            for (auto& p : freq) {
                maxF = max(maxF, p.second);
                minF = min(minF, p.second);
            }
            if (minF != INT_MAX) total += (maxF - minF);
        }
    }
    return total;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Incremental Frequency Array 26-Scan) 
int beautySumBetter(string s) {
    int total = 0, n = s.size();
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        int freq[26] = {0};
        for (int j = i; j < n; j++) {
            freq[s[j] - 'a']++;
            int maxF = 0, minF = INT_MAX;
            for (int k = 0; k < 26; k++) {
                if (freq[k] > 0) {
                    maxF = max(maxF, freq[k]);
                    minF = min(minF, freq[k]);
                }
            }
            if (minF != INT_MAX) total += (maxF - minF);
        }
    }
    return total;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Optimized Inner Loop Frequency Evaluation) 
int beautySumOptimal(string s) {
    int total = 0;
    int n = s.size();
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        int freq[26] = {0};
        int maxF = 0;
        for (int j = i; j < n; j++) {
            int idx = s[j] - 'a';
            freq[idx]++;
            if (freq[idx] > maxF) maxF = freq[idx];
            int minF = INT_MAX;
            for (int k = 0; k < 26; k++) {
                if (freq[k] > 0 && freq[k] < minF) {
                    minF = freq[k];
                }
            }
            total += (maxF - minF);
        }
    }
    return total;
}

Module 1: Implementation Problems (5 Problems)

5 Problems
Problem 1 • Implementation

Pow(x, n) — Binary Exponentiation

Medium Problem #50
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Implement pow(x, n), which calculates x raised to the power n (i.e., x^n). Must run in O(log n) algorithmic complexity and handle negative powers and integer overflows (n = -2^31).

Example 1:
Input: x = 2.00000, n = 10
Output: 1024.00000
Explanation: 2^10 = 1024.
Example 2:
Input: x = 2.10000, n = 3
Output: 9.26100
Explanation: 2.1 * 2.1 * 2.1 = 9.261.
Example 3:
Input: x = 2.00000, n = -2
Output: 0.25000
Explanation: 2^(-2) = 1 / (2^2) = 1/4 = 0.25.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Linear loop O(N) dega jo 2*10^9 ke liye TLE ho jayega. Divide and Conquer property: Agar n even hai to x^n = (x*x)^(n/2). Agar n odd hai to x^n = x * x^(n-1). Isse power har step me aadhi hoti jati hai aur O(log N) me answer mil jata hai. Negative power me base ko 1/x kar do aur n ko long long me cast karo taaki -(-2^31) overflow na kare.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Multiply x by itself in a loop n times. Gives TLE for large n.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Recursively compute half = myPow(x, n / 2). If n is even return half * half, else return x * half * half.
Time: O(log N) • Space: O(log N) recursion call stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Bitwise loop: while exp > 0, if exp is odd result *= x; x *= x; exp /= 2. Runs in O(log N) time and strictly O(1) space.
Time: O(log N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Problem #50 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Linear Multiplication Loop) 
double myPowBrute(double x, int n) {
    long long exp = n;
    if (exp < 0) { x = 1.0 / x; exp = -exp; }
    double ans = 1.0;
    for (long long i = 0; i < exp; i++) {
        ans *= x;
    }
    return ans;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Recursive Divide & Conquer) 
double powHelper(double x, long long n) {
    if (n == 0) return 1.0;
    double half = powHelper(x, n / 2);
    if (n % 2 == 0) return half * half;
    else return x * half * half;
}
double myPowBetter(double x, int n) {
    long long exp = n;
    if (exp < 0) { x = 1.0 / x; exp = -exp; }
    return powHelper(x, exp);
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Iterative Binary Exponentiation) 
double myPowOptimal(double x, int n) {
    long long exp = n;
    if (exp < 0) {
        x = 1.0 / x;
        exp = -exp;
    }
    double result = 1.0;
    while (exp > 0) {
        if (exp % 2 == 1) {
            result *= x;
            exp--;
        } else {
            x *= x;
            exp /= 2;
        }
    }
    return result;
}
Problem 2 • Backtracking

Generate Parentheses

Medium Problem #22
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given n pairs of parentheses, write a function to generate all combinations of well-formed parentheses.

Example 1:
Input: n = 3
Output: ["((()))","(()())","(())()","()(())","()()()"]
Explanation: Total 5 valid combinations of length 6 (Catalan number C_3 = 5).
Example 2:
Input: n = 1
Output: ["()"]
Explanation: Only 1 valid combination of length 2.
Example 3:
Input: n = 2
Output: ["(())","()()"]
Explanation: C_2 = 2 combinations.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Sabse naive tarika 2^(2N) strings bana kar stack se check karna hai. Lekin Backtracking me hum invalid branch par jate hi nahi hain: 1) '(' tabhi lagao jab open < n ho. 2) ')' tabhi lagao jab close < open ho. Jab current.length() == 2*n ho jaye to valid result mil gaya!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Recursively build all 2^(2N) combinations of '(' and ')', validate with balance counter.
Time: O(2^(2N) * N) • Space: O(2^(2N) * N) space
🟡 Better Approach:
Branch only when valid (open < n or close < open) passing string by value.
Time: O(4^N / sqrt(N)) • Space: O(N) recursion call stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Maintain single string reference with push_back and pop_back. Runs in O(4^N / sqrt(N)) Catalan time with O(N) auxiliary space.
Time: O(4^N / sqrt(N)) • Space: O(N) recursion depth
Problem #22 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Generate All 2^(2N) Strings and Validate) 
bool isValid(const string& s) {
    int bal = 0;
    for (char c : s) {
        if (c == '(') bal++;
        else bal--;
        if (bal < 0) return false;
    }
    return bal == 0;
}
void generateAll(string cur, int n, vector<string>& res) {
    if ((int)cur.size() == 2 * n) {
        if (isValid(cur)) res.push_back(cur);
        return;
    }
    generateAll(cur + "(", n, res);
    generateAll(cur + ")", n, res);
}
vector<string> generateParenthesisBrute(int n) {
    vector<string> res;
    generateAll("", n, res);
    return res;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Pruned Recursion with String Passing) 
void backtrackBetter(string cur, int open, int close, int n, vector<string>& res) {
    if ((int)cur.size() == 2 * n) {
        res.push_back(cur);
        return;
    }
    if (open < n) backtrackBetter(cur + "(", open + 1, close, n, res);
    if (close < open) backtrackBetter(cur + ")", open, close + 1, n, res);
}
vector<string> generateParenthesisBetter(int n) {
    vector<string> res;
    backtrackBetter("", 0, 0, n, res);
    return res;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Backtracking with Pass-by-Reference & Pop-Back) 
void backtrackOptimal(string& current, int open, int close, int n, vector<string>& result) {
    if ((int)current.length() == 2 * n) {
        result.push_back(current);
        return;
    }
    if (open < n) {
        current.push_back('(');
        backtrackOptimal(current, open + 1, close, n, result);
        current.pop_back();
    }
    if (close < open) {
        current.push_back(')');
        backtrackOptimal(current, open, close + 1, n, result);
        current.pop_back();
    }
}
vector<string> generateParenthesisOptimal(int n) {
    vector<string> result;
    string current = "";
    backtrackOptimal(current, 0, 0, n, result);
    return result;
}
Problem 3 • Subsequences

Power Set (Subsets Generation)

Medium Problem #78
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given an integer array nums of unique elements, return all possible subsets (the power set). The solution set must not contain duplicate subsets. Return the solution in any order.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [1, 2, 3]
Output: [[], [1], [2], [1,2], [3], [1,3], [2,3], [1,2,3]]
Explanation: Total 2^3 = 8 subsets.
Example 2:
Input: nums = [0]
Output: [[], [0]]
Explanation: Total 2^1 = 2 subsets.
Example 3:
Input: nums = [1, 2]
Output: [[], [1], [2], [1, 2]]
Explanation: Total 2^2 = 4 subsets.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Har element ke paas 2 choices hain: ya to wo subset ka hissa banega (Pick), ya nahi banega (Don't Pick). Total subsets 2^N hote hain. Bitmasking se 0 to 2^N - 1 tak iterate karke set bits check kar sakte hain, ya recursion se pick/not-pick tree bana sakte hain.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Loop from 0 to (1 << n) - 1. If i-th bit of mask is set, include nums[j].
Time: O(N * 2^N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
At index i, recurse without nums[i], then recurse with nums[i].
Time: O(2^N) • Space: O(N) recursion stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Standard loop-based DFS backtracking adding current snapshot on every call. O(2^N) time and O(N) space.
Time: O(2^N) • Space: O(N) auxiliary recursion depth
Problem #78 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Bit Manipulation (Bitmasking)) 
vector<vector<int>> subsetsBrute(vector<int>& nums) {
    int n = nums.size();
    int total = 1 << n;
    vector<vector<int>> res;
    for (int mask = 0; mask < total; mask++) {
        vector<int> sub;
        for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
            if (mask & (1 << j)) sub.push_back(nums[j]);
        }
        res.push_back(sub);
    }
    return res;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Pick / Don't Pick Binary Tree Recursion) 
void generateSubsets(int idx, vector<int>& nums, vector<int>& current, vector<vector<int>>& result) {
    if (idx == (int)nums.size()) {
        result.push_back(current);
        return;
    }
    current.push_back(nums[idx]);
    generateSubsets(idx + 1, nums, current, result);
    current.pop_back();
    generateSubsets(idx + 1, nums, current, result);
}
vector<vector<int>> subsetsBetter(vector<int>& nums) {
    vector<vector<int>> result;
    vector<int> current;
    generateSubsets(0, nums, current, result);
    return result;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Backtracking DFS with Choice Loop) 
void backtrackSubsets(int start, vector<int>& nums, vector<int>& current, vector<vector<int>>& result) {
    result.push_back(current);
    for (int i = start; i < (int)nums.size(); i++) {
        current.push_back(nums[i]);
        backtrackSubsets(i + 1, nums, current, result);
        current.pop_back();
    }
}
vector<vector<int>> subsetsOptimal(vector<int>& nums) {
    vector<vector<int>> result;
    vector<int> current;
    backtrackSubsets(0, nums, current, result);
    return result;
}
Problem 4 • Math Recursion

Count Good Numbers

Medium Problem #1922
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

A digit string is good if the digits (0-indexed) at even indices are even (0, 2, 4, 6, 8) and the digits at odd indices are prime (2, 3, 5, 7). Given an integer n, return the total number of good digit strings of length n modulo 10^9 + 7.

Example 1:
Input: n = 1
Output: 5
Explanation: Single digit at index 0 (even index): can be 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 (5 choices).
Example 2:
Input: n = 4
Output: 400
Explanation: Indices 0, 2 have 5 choices each; indices 1, 3 have 4 choices each. 5 * 4 * 5 * 4 = 400.
Example 3:
Input: n = 50
Output: 564908303
Explanation: Computed with modulo 10^9 + 7.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Even indices par 5 choices hain (0, 2, 4, 6, 8) aur odd indices par 4 choices hain (2, 3, 5, 7). Length n me even positions = (n + 1)/2 aur odd positions = n / 2 hoti hain. Total answer = (5^evenPos * 4^oddPos) % MOD. Modular Binary Exponentiation se O(log N) me calculate karo.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Multiply 5 for even positions and 4 for odd positions one by one in O(N). TLE for N = 10^15.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Recursively compute modPow(5, evens) and modPow(4, odds) with divide and conquer.
Time: O(log N) • Space: O(log N) recursion stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Compute 5^evens and 4^odds using iterative bitwise power algorithm. O(log N) time and O(1) space.
Time: O(log N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Problem #1922 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Iterative Multiplication Loop) 
int countGoodNumbersBrute(long long n) {
    long long MOD = 1e9 + 7;
    long long ans = 1;
    for (long long i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (i % 2 == 0) ans = (ans * 5) % MOD;
        else ans = (ans * 4) % MOD;
    }
    return ans;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Recursive Modular Exponentiation) 
long long modPowRec(long long base, long long exp, long long mod) {
    if (exp == 0) return 1;
    long long half = modPowRec(base, exp / 2, mod);
    long long res = (half * half) % mod;
    if (exp % 2 == 1) res = (res * base) % mod;
    return res;
}
int countGoodNumbersBetter(long long n) {
    long long MOD = 1e9 + 7;
    long long evens = (n + 1) / 2;
    long long odds = n / 2;
    long long p1 = modPowRec(5, evens, MOD);
    long long p2 = modPowRec(4, odds, MOD);
    return (p1 * p2) % MOD;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Iterative Binary Exponentiation (O(log N))) 
long long modPow(long long base, long long exp, long long mod) {
    long long res = 1;
    base %= mod;
    while (exp > 0) {
        if (exp % 2 == 1) res = (res * base) % mod;
        base = (base * base) % mod;
        exp /= 2;
    }
    return res;
}
int countGoodNumbersOptimal(long long n) {
    long long MOD = 1e9 + 7;
    long long evens = (n + 1) / 2;
    long long odds = n / 2;
    long long p1 = modPow(5, evens, MOD);
    long long p2 = modPow(4, odds, MOD);
    return (p1 * p2) % MOD;
}
Problem 5 • Stack Recursion

Reverse a Stack using Recursion

Medium Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

You are given a stack st of integers. Reverse the stack using recursion. You are not allowed to use any loop constructs or additional data structures (like arrays, queues, or another stack).

Example 1:
Input: st = [3, 2, 1, 7, 6] (top is 6)
Output: [6, 7, 1, 2, 3] (top is 3)
Explanation: All elements in the stack are inverted in-place.
Example 2:
Input: st = [4, 3, 9, 6]
Output: [6, 9, 3, 4]
Explanation: Order of elements is completely reversed.
Example 3:
Input: st = [1]
Output: [1]
Explanation: Single element remains unchanged.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Hume do recursive functions chahiye: 1) reverse() jo top element ko pop karke function call stack me hold karta hai aur baki stack ko reverse karta hai. 2) insertAtBottom() jo element ko stack ke sabse neeche (bottom par) insert karta hai.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Pop all elements into a vector, then push them back into stack in reversed order.
Time: O(2N) • Space: O(N) vector space
🟡 Better Approach:
Transfer all elements from stack to queue (FIFO), then back to stack.
Time: O(2N) • Space: O(N) queue auxiliary space
🟢 Optimal Approach:
insertAtBottom recursively pops to empty stack then pushes. reverse() pops top, calls reverse(), then insertAtBottom(). O(N^2) time and O(N) recursion stack.
Time: O(N^2) • Space: O(N) recursion call stack
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Auxiliary Vector Buffering) 
void reverseStackBrute(stack<int>& st) {
    vector<int> v;
    while (!st.empty()) { v.push_back(st.top()); st.pop(); }
    for (int x : v) st.push(x);
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Queue-Based Reversal) 
void reverseStackBetter(stack<int>& st) {
    queue<int> q;
    while (!st.empty()) { q.push(st.top()); st.pop(); }
    while (!q.empty()) { st.push(q.front()); q.pop(); }
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Two-Function Pure Recursion (In-Place)) 
void insertAtBottom(stack<int>& st, int element) {
    if (st.empty()) {
        st.push(element);
        return;
    }
    int topElement = st.top();
    st.pop();
    insertAtBottom(st, element);
    st.push(topElement);
}
void reverseStackOptimal(stack<int>& st) {
    if (st.empty()) return;
    int topElement = st.top();
    st.pop();
    reverseStackOptimal(st);
    insertAtBottom(st, topElement);
}

Module 2: Subsequence Pattern Problems (4 Problems)

4 Problems
Problem 6 • Subsequences

Generate All Subsequences (Power Set Recursion)

Medium Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given an array nums of size N, generate and return all possible subsequences of the array using recursion. A subsequence is formed by deleting zero or more elements without changing the order of the remaining elements.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [1, 2]
Output: [[], [1], [2], [1, 2]]
Explanation: 4 subsequences.
Example 2:
Input: nums = [3, 1, 2]
Output: [[], [3], [1], [2], [3, 1], [3, 2], [1, 2], [3, 1, 2]]
Explanation: Total 2^3 = 8 subsequences.
Example 3:
Input: nums = [5]
Output: [[], [5]]
Explanation: 2 subsequences.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Core recursion pattern: Har index par 2 options hote hain: Element ko path me shamil karo (Pick: path.push_back(nums[i])) aur aage badho. Wapas aate waqt element ko hatao (Backtrack: path.pop_back()) aur bina element ke aage badho (Don't Pick).
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Loop from 0 to 2^N - 1, checking set bits in O(N * 2^N).
Time: O(N * 2^N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Pass path by value on both branches (pick and not pick).
Time: O(2^N) • Space: O(N) recursion stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Maintain single reference path with push_back and pop_back. O(2^N) time and O(N) recursion space.
Time: O(2^N) • Space: O(N) recursion call stack
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Bitmasking Generation) 
vector<vector<int>> genSubseqBrute(vector<int>& nums) {
    int n = nums.size();
    vector<vector<int>> res;
    for (int mask = 0; mask < (1 << n); mask++) {
        vector<int> sub;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (mask & (1 << i)) sub.push_back(nums[i]);
        res.push_back(sub);
    }
    return res;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Binary Tree Recursion) 
void recurseSubseq(int i, vector<int>& nums, vector<int> path, vector<vector<int>>& res) {
    if (i == (int)nums.size()) { res.push_back(path); return; }
    recurseSubseq(i + 1, nums, path, res);
    path.push_back(nums[i]);
    recurseSubseq(i + 1, nums, path, res);
}
vector<vector<int>> genSubseqBetter(vector<int>& nums) {
    vector<vector<int>> res;
    recurseSubseq(0, nums, {}, res);
    return res;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Backtracking with Pass-by-Reference & Pop-Back) 
void backtrackSubseq(int ind, vector<int>& path, vector<int>& nums, vector<vector<int>>& result) {
    if (ind == (int)nums.size()) {
        result.push_back(path);
        return;
    }
    path.push_back(nums[ind]);
    backtrackSubseq(ind + 1, path, nums, result);
    path.pop_back();
    backtrackSubseq(ind + 1, path, nums, result);
}
vector<vector<int>> genSubseqOptimal(vector<int>& nums) {
    vector<vector<int>> result;
    vector<int> path;
    backtrackSubseq(0, path, nums, result);
    return result;
}
Problem 7 • Subsequences

Check if there exists a Subsequence with Sum K

Medium Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given an array nums of integers and an integer k, return true if there exists at least one subsequence whose sum equals k, otherwise return false.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [1, 2, 1], k = 2
Output: true
Explanation: Subsequence [1, 1] has sum 1 + 1 = 2.
Example 2:
Input: nums = [1, 2, 3], k = 7
Output: false
Explanation: Maximum possible sum is 1+2+3 = 6, so 7 is impossible.
Example 3:
Input: nums = [5], k = 5
Output: true
Explanation: Single element matches k.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Hume saari subsequences dhundne ki zaroorat nahi hai! Jaise hi koi branch true return kare, recursion ko turant short-circuit (early exit) kar do: if (checkSum(i+1, sum + nums[i])) return true; taaki baki branches bina wajah explore na hon.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Generate all 2^N subsequences and sum elements of each to check if any equals k.
Time: O(N * 2^N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Traverse entire recursion tree accumulating bool result.
Time: O(2^N) • Space: O(N) recursion stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Return true immediately when pick branch succeeds without exploring notPick branch. O(2^N) worst-case, fast early exit in practice, O(N) stack.
Time: O(2^N) worst case, O(1) best case • Space: O(N) recursion stack
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (All Subsequences Exhaustive Check) 
bool checkSubsequenceSumBrute(vector<int>& nums, int k) {
    int n = nums.size();
    for (int mask = 0; mask < (1 << n); mask++) {
        int sum = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (mask & (1 << i)) sum += nums[i];
        if (sum == k) return true;
    }
    return false;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Full Recursion Tree without Early Exit) 
bool helperBetter(int ind, int sum, int k, vector<int>& nums) {
    if (ind == (int)nums.size()) return sum == k;
    bool pick = helperBetter(ind + 1, sum + nums[ind], k, nums);
    bool notPick = helperBetter(ind + 1, sum, k, nums);
    return pick || notPick;
}
bool checkSubsequenceSumBetter(vector<int>& nums, int k) {
    return helperBetter(0, 0, k, nums);
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Short-Circuiting Boolean Backtracking) 
bool checkSubsequenceSumOptimal(int ind, int currentSum, int target, vector<int>& nums) {
    if (ind == (int)nums.size()) {
        return currentSum == target;
    }
    if (checkSubsequenceSumOptimal(ind + 1, currentSum + nums[ind], target, nums)) {
        return true;
    }
    if (checkSubsequenceSumOptimal(ind + 1, currentSum, target, nums)) {
        return true;
    }
    return false;
}
Problem 8 • Subsequences

Count All Subsequences with Sum K

Medium Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given an array nums of integers and a target integer k, count the total number of subsequences whose sum is equal to k.

Example 1:
Input: nums = [1, 2, 1], k = 2
Output: 2
Explanation: Two subsequences: [1, 1] and [2].
Example 2:
Input: nums = [1, 1, 1], k = 2
Output: 3
Explanation: Choosing any 2 out of 3 elements gives sum 2: C(3, 2) = 3.
Example 3:
Input: nums = [2, 3, 5], k = 8
Output: 1
Explanation: Only [3, 5] sums to 8.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Functional Recursion technique: Har node par base case me check karo: agar currentSum == k to return 1, warna return 0. Left branch (Pick) ka count l lo, Right branch (Not Pick) ka count r lo, aur function se return l + r kar do!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Iterate all 2^N bitmasks, calculate sum, increment count if sum == k.
Time: O(N * 2^N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Pass global count by reference, incrementing count whenever sum == k at base case.
Time: O(2^N) • Space: O(N) recursion stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Base case returns 1 or 0. Function returns pickCount + notPickCount directly. O(2^N) time and O(N) stack space.
Time: O(2^N) • Space: O(N) recursion call stack
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Power Set Exhaustive Counting) 
int countSubsequencesBrute(vector<int>& nums, int k) {
    int n = nums.size(), cnt = 0;
    for (int mask = 0; mask < (1 << n); mask++) {
        int sum = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (mask & (1 << i)) sum += nums[i];
        if (sum == k) cnt++;
    }
    return cnt;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Global Counter Accumulator Recursion) 
void countHelper(int ind, int sum, int k, vector<int>& nums, int& count) {
    if (ind == (int)nums.size()) {
        if (sum == k) count++;
        return;
    }
    countHelper(ind + 1, sum + nums[ind], k, nums, count);
    countHelper(ind + 1, sum, k, nums, count);
}
int countSubsequencesBetter(vector<int>& nums, int k) {
    int count = 0;
    countHelper(0, 0, k, nums, count);
    return count;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Functional Recursion: return left + right) 
int countSubsequencesOptimal(int ind, int currentSum, int target, vector<int>& nums) {
    if (ind == (int)nums.size()) {
        return (currentSum == target) ? 1 : 0;
    }
    int pick = countSubsequencesOptimal(ind + 1, currentSum + nums[ind], target, nums);
    int notPick = countSubsequencesOptimal(ind + 1, currentSum, target, nums);
    return pick + notPick;
}
Problem 9 • Binary Strings

Generate Binary Strings Without Consecutive 1s

Medium Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given an integer N, generate all valid binary strings of length N such that no two '1's are consecutive. Return the strings in sorted order.

Example 1:
Input: N = 3
Output: ["000", "001", "010", "100", "101"]
Explanation: Total 5 valid strings (Fibonacci F_5 = 5).
Example 2:
Input: N = 2
Output: ["00", "01", "10"]
Explanation: Three valid strings.
Example 3:
Input: N = 1
Output: ["0", "1"]
Explanation: Both 0 and 1 are valid.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Sabse naive me 2^N strings generate karke '11' check karo. Lekin Backtracking me hum invalid branch par jate hi nahi: 1) '0' hamesha append ho sakta hai (no restriction). 2) '1' sirf tabhi append ho sakta hai jab previous character '0' tha ya string empty ho. Total valid strings Fibonacci numbers follow karti hain!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Generate all binary strings of length N, check if string contains '11', filter out.
Time: O(N * 2^N) • Space: O(N * 2^N) space
🟡 Better Approach:
Only append '1' if last char != '1', passing string by value.
Time: O(phi^N) approx O(1.618^N) • Space: O(N) recursion stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Branch with '0' always. Branch with '1' only when last is '0'. Backtrack in O(Fibonacci(N)) time and O(N) space.
Time: O(1.618^N) (Golden Ratio Fibonacci growth) • Space: O(N) recursion call stack

🔴 1. Brute Force (All 2^N Binary Strings Generation & Filter) 
bool hasConsecutiveOnes(const string& s) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i + 1 < s.size(); i++) {
        if (s[i] == '1' && s[i + 1] == '1') return true;
    }
    return false;
}
void genAll(string cur, int n, vector<string>& res) {
    if ((int)cur.size() == n) {
        if (!hasConsecutiveOnes(cur)) res.push_back(cur);
        return;
    }
    genAll(cur + "0", n, res);
    genAll(cur + "1", n, res);
}

    genAll("", n, res);
    return res;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Pruned Recursion with String by Value) 
void buildStrings(string cur, int n, vector<string>& res) {
    if ((int)cur.size() == n) { res.push_back(cur); return; }
    buildStrings(cur + "0", n, res);
    if (cur.empty() || cur.back() != '1') {
        buildStrings(cur + "1", n, res);
    }
}
vector<string> generateBinaryStringsBetter(int n) {
    vector<string> res;
    buildStrings("", n, res);
    return res;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Backtracking with Pass-by-Reference & In-Place Pop) 
void backtrackBinary(string& current, int n, vector<string>& result) {
    if ((int)current.length() == n) {
        result.push_back(current);
        return;
    }
    current.push_back('0');
    backtrackBinary(current, n, result);
    current.pop_back();

    if (current.empty() || current.back() != '1') {
        current.push_back('1');
        backtrackBinary(current, n, result);
        current.pop_back();
    }
}
vector<string> generateBinaryStringsOptimal(int n) {
    vector<string> result;
    string current = "";
    backtrackBinary(current, n, result);
    return result;
}

Problem 10 • Combinations

Combination Sum (Unlimited Pick)

Medium Problem #39
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given an array of distinct integers candidates and a target integer target, return a list of all unique combinations of candidates where the chosen numbers sum to target. You may return the combinations in any order. The same number may be chosen from candidates an unlimited number of times.

Example 1:
Input: candidates = [2, 3, 6, 7], target = 7
Output: [[2, 2, 3], [7]]
Explanation: 2 + 2 + 3 = 7 and 7 = 7.
Example 2:
Input: candidates = [2, 3, 5], target = 8
Output: [[2, 2, 2, 2], [2, 3, 3], [3, 5]]
Explanation: Three valid combinations.
Example 3:
Input: candidates = [2], target = 1
Output: []
Explanation: Cannot sum to 1 using 2.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Unlimited pick ka matlab: jab hum element candidates[ind] ko pick karte hain, to index ko aage nahi badhate (index ind par hi rehte hain) aur target me se subtract karte hain: target - candidates[ind]. Jab pick nahi karte (not pick), to index ko ind + 1 badha dete hain.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Generate all permutations up to target / minElement depth, sort each combination, insert into std::set.
Time: O(N^(T/M)) where T=target, M=minVal • Space: O(S) set space
🟡 Better Approach:
Binary decision tree: Pick stays at ind with target - candidates[ind]. Don't pick moves to ind + 1.
Time: O(2^T * K) • Space: O(K) recursion stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Sort candidates first. Loop from start index i; if candidates[i] > target break early. Extremely fast execution.
Time: O(2^T * K) • Space: O(K) where K is target / minCandidate

🔴 1. Brute Force (Bounded Depth Permutations with Set Dedup) 
void permuteSum(vector<int>& c, int target, vector<int>& cur, set<vector<int>>& s) {
    if (target == 0) {
        vector<int> sorted = cur;
        sort(sorted.begin(), sorted.end());
        s.insert(sorted);
        return;
    }
    if (target < 0) return;
    for (int x : c) {
        cur.push_back(x);
        permuteSum(c, target - x, cur, s);
        cur.pop_back();
    }
}
vector<vector<int>> combinationSumBrute(vector<int>& candidates, int target) {
    set<vector<int>> s;
    vector<int> cur;
    permuteSum(candidates, target, cur, s);
    return vector<vector<int>>(s.begin(), s.end());
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Pick / Don't Pick Recursion) 
void findCombinations(int ind, int target, vector<int>& arr, vector<int>& ds, vector<vector<int>>& ans) {
    if (ind == (int)arr.size()) {
        if (target == 0) ans.push_back(ds);
        return;
    }
    if (arr[ind] <= target) {
        ds.push_back(arr[ind]);
        findCombinations(ind, target - arr[ind], arr, ds, ans);
        ds.pop_back();
    }
    findCombinations(ind + 1, target, arr, ds, ans);
}
vector<vector<int>> combinationSumBetter(vector<int>& candidates, int target) {
    vector<vector<int>> ans;
    vector<int> ds;
    findCombinations(0, target, candidates, ds, ans);
    return ans;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Sorted Backtracking Loop with Early Break) 
void backtrackComb(int start, int target, vector<int>& candidates, vector<int>& current, vector<vector<int>>& result) {
    if (target == 0) {
        result.push_back(current);
        return;
    }
    for (int i = start; i < (int)candidates.size(); i++) {
        if (candidates[i] > target) break;
        current.push_back(candidates[i]);
        backtrackComb(i, target - candidates[i], candidates, current, result);
        current.pop_back();
    }
}
vector<vector<int>> combinationSumOptimal(vector<int>& candidates, int target) {
    sort(candidates.begin(), candidates.end());
    vector<vector<int>> result;
    vector<int> current;
    backtrackComb(0, target, candidates, current, result);
    return result;
}

Duplicates se bachne ke liye do cheezein karo: 1) Array ko pehle sort kar lo sort(candidates.begin(), candidates.end()). 2) For loop me same recursive depth par agar i > start && candidates[i] == candidates[i - 1] ho, to us element ko skip (continue) kar do! Isse bina kisi std::set ke O(1) space me strictly unique combinations milte hain!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:

Pick element, then for not-pick advance index while candidates[ind] == candidates[ind + 1].

Sort candidates. In loop: if i > start && arr[i] == arr[i - 1] continue. Eliminates set overhead completely. O(2^N * K) time and O(K) space.

    return result;
}
Problem 14 • Combinations

Combination Sum III (K Digits Sum to N)

Medium Problem #216
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Find all valid combinations of k numbers that sum up to n such that only numbers 1 through 9 are used and each number is used at most once. Return a list of all possible valid combinations.

Example 1:
Input: k = 3, n = 7
Output: [[1, 2, 4]]
Explanation: 1 + 2 + 4 = 7. No other 3 numbers from 1-9 sum to 7.
Example 2:
Input: k = 3, n = 9
Output: [[1, 2, 6], [1, 3, 5], [2, 3, 4]]
Explanation: Three valid sets of 3 distinct digits summing to 9.
Example 3:
Input: k = 4, n = 1
Output: []
Explanation: Minimum sum of 4 distinct positive digits is 1+2+3+4 = 10 > 1.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Digits 1 se 9 tak hi allow hain aur strictly increasing order me pick karne se duplicates automatically prevent ho jaate hain. Base case: jab current.size() == k ho, to check karo target == 0 hai ya nahi. Loop for (int i = start; i <= 9; i++) chalao, agar i > target to break kar do.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Check all subsets of digits {1, 2, ..., 9} using bitmasking, filter for size k and sum n.
Time: O(9 * 2^9) = O(4608) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Binary decision tree on digits 1 through 9 tracking remaining k and remaining n.
Time: O(2^9) • Space: O(K) recursion stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Loop from start to 9 with immediate break when i > target. Maximum C(9, k) states. O(C(9, k)) time and O(K) space.
Time: O(C(9, K)) • Space: O(K) auxiliary recursion stack

vector<vector<int>> combinationSum3Brute(int k, int n) {
    vector<vector<int>> ans;
    for (int mask = 0; mask < (1 << 9); mask++) {
        vector<int> cur;
        int sum = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < 9; i++) {
            if (mask & (1 << i)) { cur.push_back(i + 1); sum += (i + 1); }
        }
        if ((int)cur.size() == k && sum == n) ans.push_back(cur);
    }
    return ans;
}

void comb3Helper(int digit, int k, int n, vector<int>& ds, vector<vector<int>>& ans) {
    if (k == 0) { if (n == 0) ans.push_back(ds); return; }
    if (digit > 9 || n < 0) return;
    ds.push_back(digit);
    comb3Helper(digit + 1, k - 1, n - digit, ds, ans);
    ds.pop_back();
    comb3Helper(digit + 1, k, n, ds, ans);
}

void backtrackComb3(int start, int k, int target, vector<int>& current, vector<vector<int>>& result) {
    if ((int)current.size() == k) {
        if (target == 0) result.push_back(current);
        return;
    }
    for (int i = start; i <= 9; i++) {
        if (i > target) break;
        current.push_back(i);
        backtrackComb3(i + 1, k, target - i, current, result);
        current.pop_back();
    }
}

    vector<vector<int>> result;
    vector<int> current;
    backtrackComb3(1, k, n, current, result);

}

🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Use a queue to iteratively dequeue partial combinations and enqueue new strings for each mapped character.

🟡 Better Approach:
Recursively build string passing current combination by value.
Time: O(4^N * N) • Space: O(N) recursion stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:

Problem 16 • Partitioning

Palindrome Partitioning

Medium Problem #131
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given a string s, partition s such that every substring of the partition is a palindrome. Return all possible palindrome partitioning of s.

Example 1:
Input: s = "aab"
Output: [["a","a","b"],["aa","b"]]
Explanation: "a","a","b" are all palindromes; "aa" and "b" are palindromes.
Example 2:
Input: s = "a"
Output: [["a"]]
Explanation: Single partition.
Example 3:
Input: s = "aba"
Output: [["a","b","a"],["aba"]]
Explanation: Two valid palindrome partitions.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Index start se aage har possible cut position i check karo. Agar substring s[start..i] palindrome hai, to us substring ko path me push karo aur baki bache hisse par recursively i + 1 par partition call karo. Wapas aate waqt path se pop_back karo.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Generate all 2^(N-1) possible partition boundaries, validate each substring for palindrome property.
Time: O(2^N * N^2) • Space: O(2^N * N) space
🟡 Better Approach:
Only recurse when substring s[start..i] is verified palindrome using two pointers.
Time: O(2^N * N) • Space: O(N) recursion stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Precompute isPalin[i][j] in O(N^2) time. Backtrack cuts with O(1) palindrome verification. O(N^2 + 2^N * N) time and O(N^2) space.
Time: O(N^2 + 2^N * N) • Space: O(N^2) DP table + O(N) recursion depth

bool checkPalin(const string& str) {
    int l = 0, r = str.size() - 1;
    while (l < r) if (str[l++] != str[r--]) return false;
    return true;
}
void generatePartitions(int start, const string& s, vector<string>& cur, vector<vector<string>>& res) {
    if (start == (int)s.size()) {
        bool allPalin = true;
        for (auto& str : cur) if (!checkPalin(str)) { allPalin = false; break; }
        if (allPalin) res.push_back(cur);

    for (int i = start; i < (int)s.size(); i++) {
        cur.push_back(s.substr(start, i - start + 1));
        generatePartitions(i + 1, s, cur, res);
        cur.pop_back();
    }
}

    while (l < r) { if (s[l++] != s[r--]) return false; }

}
void backtrackPalin(int start, const string& s, vector<string>& path, vector<vector<string>>& res) {
    if (start == (int)s.size()) { res.push_back(path); return; }
    for (int i = start; i < (int)s.size(); i++) {
        if (isPalindrome(s, start, i)) {
            path.push_back(s.substr(start, i - start + 1));
            backtrackPalin(i + 1, s, path, res);
            path.pop_back();
        }
    }

void dfsPartition(int start, const string& s, const vector<vector<bool>>& isPalin, vector<string>& current, vector<vector<string>>& result) {
    if (start == (int)s.length()) {
        result.push_back(current);
        return;
    }
    for (int i = start; i < (int)s.length(); i++) {
        if (isPalin[start][i]) {
            current.push_back(s.substr(start, i - start + 1));
            dfsPartition(i + 1, s, isPalin, current, result);
            current.pop_back();
        }
    }

vector<vector<string>> partitionOptimal(string s) {
    int n = s.length();
    vector<vector<bool>> isPalin(n, vector<bool>(n, false));
    for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        for (int j = i; j < n; j++) {
            if (s[i] == s[j] && (j - i <= 2 || isPalin[i + 1][j - 1])) {
                isPalin[i][j] = true;
            }
        }
    }
    vector<vector<string>> result;
    vector<string> current;
    dfsPartition(0, s, isPalin, current, result);
    return result;
}
Problem 17 • Hard Backtracking

Word Search in 2D Grid

Medium Problem #79
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given an m x n grid of characters board and a string word, return true if word exists in the grid. The word can be constructed from letters of sequentially adjacent cells (horizontally or vertically neighboring). The same letter cell may not be used more than once in a word.

Example 1:
Input: board = [["A","B","C","E"],["S","F","C","S"],["A","D","E","E"]], word = "ABCCED"
Output: true
Explanation: Word ABCCED is found along the top row and right downward turns.
Example 2:
Input: board = [["A","B","C","E"],["S","F","C","S"],["A","D","E","E"]], word = "SEE"
Output: true
Explanation: Word SEE is found.
Example 3:
Input: board = [["A","B","C","E"],["S","F","C","S"],["A","D","E","E"]], word = "ABCB"
Output: false
Explanation: Cell 'B' cannot be reused.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Grid ke har cell (r, c) se DFS shuru karo. Agar board[r][c] == word[k] match ho, to us cell ko temporarily mask karo char temp = board[r][c]; board[r][c] = '#'; taaki same path me reuse na ho. Fir charo directions (Up, Down, Left, Right) me recurse karo. Wapas aate waqt original character restore karo board[r][c] = temp;.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Use queue storing current coordinate and set of visited coordinates. Exponential state explosion.
Time: O(N * M * 4^L) • Space: O(4^L * L) queue space
🟡 Better Approach:
DFS using separate visited[m][n] table avoiding cell re-visitation.
Time: O(N * M * 4^L) • Space: O(N * M) auxiliary matrix space
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Mask board[r][c] = '#' during traversal, restore after return. O(N * M * 4^L) time and O(L) stack space with zero extra matrix overhead.
Time: O(N * M * 4^L) • Space: O(L) recursion depth where L is word length

🔴 1. Brute Force (BFS Path Expansion with Set Visited) 
bool existBrute(vector<vector<char>>& board, string word) {
    int m = board.size(), n = board[0].size(), L = word.size();
    int dr[] = {-1, 1, 0, 0}, dc[] = {0, 0, -1, 1};
    for (int r = 0; r < m; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < n; c++) {
            if (board[r][c] != word[0]) continue;
            queue<tuple<int, int, int, set<pair<int,int>>>> q;
            set<pair<int,int>> initSet = {{r, c}};
            q.push({r, c, 0, initSet});
            while (!q.empty()) {
                auto [cr, cc, idx, vis] = q.front(); q.pop();
                if (idx == L - 1) return true;
                for (int d = 0; d < 4; d++) {
                    int nr = cr + dr[d], nc = cc + dc[d];
                    if (nr >= 0 && nr < m && nc >= 0 && nc < n && !vis.count({nr, nc}) && board[nr][nc] == word[idx + 1]) {
                        auto nvis = vis;
                        nvis.insert({nr, nc});
                        q.push({nr, nc, idx + 1, nvis});
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return false;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (DFS with 2D Visited Boolean Matrix) 
bool dfsVisited(int r, int c, int k, const vector<vector<char>>& b, const string& w, vector<vector<bool>>& vis) {
    if (k == (int)w.size()) return true;
    if (r < 0 || r >= (int)b.size() || c < 0 || c >= (int)b[0].size() || vis[r][c] || b[r][c] != w[k]) return false;
    vis[r][c] = true;
    bool found = dfsVisited(r + 1, c, k + 1, b, w, vis) ||
                 dfsVisited(r - 1, c, k + 1, b, w, vis) ||
                 dfsVisited(r, c + 1, k + 1, b, w, vis) ||
                 dfsVisited(r, c - 1, k + 1, b, w, vis);
    vis[r][c] = false;
    return found;
}

    int m = board.size(), n = board[0].size();
    vector<vector<bool>> vis(m, vector<bool>(n, false));
    for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
            if (board[i][j] == word[0] && dfsVisited(i, j, 0, board, word, vis)) return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (In-Place Character Masking Backtracking) 
bool dfsWord(vector<vector<char>>& board, const string& word, int r, int c, int k) {
    if (k == (int)word.length()) return true;
    if (r < 0 || r >= (int)board.size() || c < 0 || c >= (int)board[0].size() || board[r][c] != word[k]) {
        return false;
    }
    char temp = board[r][c];
    board[r][c] = '#';
    bool found = dfsWord(board, word, r + 1, c, k + 1) ||
                 dfsWord(board, word, r - 1, c, k + 1) ||
                 dfsWord(board, word, r, c + 1, k + 1) ||
                 dfsWord(board, word, r, c - 1, k + 1);
    board[r][c] = temp;
    return found;
}

    for (int i = 0; i < m; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {

                if (dfsWord(board, word, i, j, 0)) return true;

}
Problem 18 • Hard Backtracking

N-Queens Problem

Hard Problem #51
Problem Statement Standard • Hard

The n-queens puzzle is the problem of placing n queens on an n x n chessboard such that no two queens attack each other (no two queens share the same row, column, or diagonal). Return all distinct solutions.

Example 1:
Input: n = 4
Output: [[".Q..","...Q","Q...","..Q."],["..Q.","Q...","...Q",".Q.."]]
Explanation: Two distinct 4x4 non-attacking configurations.
Example 2:
Input: n = 1
Output: [["Q"]]
Explanation: Single queen board.
Example 3:
Input: n = 2
Output: []
Explanation: No valid placement exists for 2x2 board.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Column by column queens place karo: har column col me row row = 0 to n-1 try karo. Agar safe hai, to place karo aur agle column col + 1 par jao. Safety check O(N) me loop se ho sakta hai, lekin 3 Hash Vectors (`leftRow`, `lowerDiagonal: row + col`, `upperDiagonal: (n - 1) + (col - row)`) maintain karne se safety check direct O(1) me ho jata hai!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Generate all permutations of column indices (N!), validate diagonal collisions in O(N^2).
Time: O(N! * N^2) • Space: O(N^2) board space
🟡 Better Approach:
Check left horizontal row, upper-left diagonal, and lower-left diagonal with while loops.
Time: O(N! * N) • Space: O(N^2) board space
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Hash row, row + col (lower diag), and (n - 1) + (col - row) (upper diag). Reduces safety check to strictly O(1). O(N!) time and O(N) space.
Time: O(N!) • Space: O(N) auxiliary hash vectors

🔴 1. Brute Force (Generate All Permutations and Validate) 
bool isValidBoard(const vector<string>& b, int n) {
    for (int r = 0; r < n; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < n; c++) {
            if (b[r][c] == 'Q') {
                for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) {
                    if (r + i < n && c + i < n && b[r + i][c + i] == 'Q') return false;
                    if (r - i >= 0 && c + i < n && b[r - i][c + i] == 'Q') return false;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return true;
}
vector<vector<string>> solveNQueensBrute(int n) {
    vector<int> p(n);
    iota(p.begin(), p.end(), 0);
    vector<vector<string>> ans;
    do {
        vector<string> b(n, string(n, '.'));
        for (int r = 0; r < n; r++) b[r][p[r]] = 'Q';
        if (isValidBoard(b, n)) ans.push_back(b);
    } while (next_permutation(p.begin(), p.end()));
    return ans;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Backtracking with O(N) isSafe Helper) 
bool isSafe(int r, int c, const vector<string>& b, int n) {
    int dr = r, dc = c;
    while (dc >= 0) if (b[dr][dc--] == 'Q') return false;
    dr = r; dc = c;
    while (dr >= 0 && dc >= 0) if (b[dr--][dc--] == 'Q') return false;
    dr = r; dc = c;
    while (dr < n && dc >= 0) if (b[dr++][dc--] == 'Q') return false;
    return true;
}
void solveSafe(int c, vector<string>& b, vector<vector<string>>& ans, int n) {
    if (c == n) { ans.push_back(b); return; }
    for (int r = 0; r < n; r++) {
        if (isSafe(r, c, b, n)) {
            b[r][c] = 'Q';
            solveSafe(c + 1, b, ans, n);
            b[r][c] = '.';
        }
    }
}
vector<vector<string>> solveNQueensBetter(int n) {
    vector<vector<string>> ans;
    vector<string> b(n, string(n, '.'));
    solveSafe(0, b, ans, n);
    return ans;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (O(1) Hashing Vectors for Rows and Diagonals) 
void solveNQueensDfs(int col, vector<string>& board, vector<vector<string>>& result,
                       vector<int>& leftRow, vector<int>& lowerDiag, vector<int>& upperDiag, int n) {
    if (col == n) {
        result.push_back(board);
        return;
    }
    for (int row = 0; row < n; row++) {
        if (leftRow[row] == 0 && lowerDiag[row + col] == 0 && upperDiag[n - 1 + col - row] == 0) {
            board[row][col] = 'Q';
            leftRow[row] = 1;
            lowerDiag[row + col] = 1;
            upperDiag[n - 1 + col - row] = 1;

            solveNQueensDfs(col + 1, board, result, leftRow, lowerDiag, upperDiag, n);

            board[row][col] = '.';
            leftRow[row] = 0;
            lowerDiag[row + col] = 0;
            upperDiag[n - 1 + col - row] = 0;
        }
    }
}
vector<vector<string>> solveNQueensOptimal(int n) {
    vector<vector<string>> result;
    vector<string> board(n, string(n, '.'));
    vector<int> leftRow(n, 0);
    vector<int> lowerDiag(2 * n - 1, 0);
    vector<int> upperDiag(2 * n - 1, 0);
    solveNQueensDfs(0, board, result, leftRow, lowerDiag, upperDiag, n);
    return result;
}
Problem 19 • Hard Backtracking

Rat in a Maze Problem

Medium Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Consider a rat placed at (0, 0) in an N x N square matrix mat. The rat has to reach the destination at (N - 1, N - 1). The rat can move in 4 directions: 'D' (Down), 'L' (Left), 'R' (Right), 'U' (Up). Value 0 means blocked and 1 means open cell. Find all valid paths in lexicographical order.

Example 1:
Input: mat = [[1, 0, 0, 0], [1, 1, 0, 1], [1, 1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 1, 1]], N = 4
Output: ["DDRDRR", "DRDDRR"]

Example 2:
Input: mat = [[1, 0], [1, 0]], N = 2
Output: ["-1"]
Explanation: Destination (1, 1) is 0 (blocked); no path exists.
Example 3:
Input: mat = [[1, 1], [1, 1]], N = 2
Output: ["DR", "RD"]
Explanation: Two paths.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Lexicographical order guarantee karne ke liye directions ka order hamesha 'D', 'L', 'R', 'U' rakho. Delta arrays di = {1, 0, 0, -1} aur dj = {0, -1, 1, 0} banao. Cell par aate hi usse visited mark karo, charo direction me loop chalao, aur backtrack karte waqt unmark karo.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Queue BFS storing coordinate, path string, and visited 2D boolean grid.
Time: O(4^(N^2)) • Space: O(4^(N^2) * N^2) queue space
🟡 Better Approach:
Explicit if conditions for Down, Left, Right, Up with visited[n][n] matrix.
Time: O(4^(N^2)) • Space: O(N^2) auxiliary matrix
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Direction array {di, dj} and 'DLRU' order with in-place cell marking mat[i][j] = 0. O(4^(N^2)) time and O(N^2) stack space.
Time: O(4^(N^2)) • Space: O(N^2) recursion call stack

🔴 1. Brute Force (BFS Queue with Path and Visited History) 
vector<string> findPathBrute(vector<vector<int>>& mat, int n) {
    if (mat[0][0] == 0 || mat[n - 1][n - 1] == 0) return {};
    vector<string> ans;
    queue<tuple<int, int, string, vector<vector<bool>>>> q;
    vector<vector<bool>> v(n, vector<bool>(n, false));
    v[0][0] = true;
    q.push({0, 0, "", v});
    int di[] = {1, 0, 0, -1}, dj[] = {0, -1, 1, 0};
    char dir[] = {'D', 'L', 'R', 'U'};
    while (!q.empty()) {
        auto [r, c, p, vis] = q.front(); q.pop();
        if (r == n - 1 && c == n - 1) { ans.push_back(p); continue; }
        for (int d = 0; d < 4; d++) {
            int nr = r + di[d], nc = c + dj[d];
            if (nr >= 0 && nr < n && nc >= 0 && nc < n && !vis[nr][nc] && mat[nr][nc] == 1) {
                auto nvis = vis;
                nvis[nr][nc] = true;
                q.push({nr, nc, p + dir[d], nvis});
            }
        }
    }
    sort(ans.begin(), ans.end());
    return ans;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (4 Separate Recursive Calls with Visited Array) 
void solveMaze(int r, int c, vector<vector<int>>& m, int n, string path, vector<string>& ans, vector<vector<bool>>& vis) {
    if (r == n - 1 && c == n - 1) { ans.push_back(path); return; }
    vis[r][c] = true;
    if (r + 1 < n && !vis[r + 1][c] && m[r + 1][c] == 1) solveMaze(r + 1, c, m, n, path + "D", ans, vis);
    if (c - 1 >= 0 && !vis[r][c - 1] && m[r][c - 1] == 1) solveMaze(r, c - 1, m, n, path + "L", ans, vis);
    if (c + 1 < n && !vis[r][c + 1] && m[r][c + 1] == 1) solveMaze(r, c + 1, m, n, path + "R", ans, vis);
    if (r - 1 >= 0 && !vis[r - 1][c] && m[r - 1][c] == 1) solveMaze(r - 1, c, m, n, path + "U", ans, vis);
    vis[r][c] = false;
}
vector<string> findPathBetter(vector<vector<int>>& mat, int n) {
    if (mat[0][0] == 0 || mat[n - 1][n - 1] == 0) return {};
    vector<string> ans;
    vector<vector<bool>> vis(n, vector<bool>(n, false));
    solveMaze(0, 0, mat, n, "", ans, vis);
    return ans;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Loop-Based Backtracking with Delta Arrays in 'D-L-R-U') 
void findPathsDfs(int r, int c, vector<vector<int>>& mat, int n, string& path, vector<string>& result) {
    if (r == n - 1 && c == n - 1) {
        result.push_back(path);
        return;
    }
    string dir = "DLRU";
    int di[] = {1, 0, 0, -1};
    int dj[] = {0, -1, 1, 0};
    mat[r][c] = 0;
    for (int idx = 0; idx < 4; idx++) {
        int nextR = r + di[idx];
        int nextC = c + dj[idx];
        if (nextR >= 0 && nextR < n && nextC >= 0 && nextC < n && mat[nextR][nextC] == 1) {
            path.push_back(dir[idx]);
            findPathsDfs(nextR, nextC, mat, n, path, result);
            path.pop_back();
        }
    }
    mat[r][c] = 1;
}
vector<string> findPathOptimal(vector<vector<int>>& mat, int n) {
    vector<string> result;
    if (mat[0][0] == 0 || mat[n - 1][n - 1] == 0) return result;
    string path = "";
    findPathsDfs(0, 0, mat, n, path, result);
    return result;
}
Problem 20 • Hard Backtracking

M-Coloring Problem (Graph Vertex Coloring)

Medium Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given an undirected graph represented by an adjacency matrix graph and an integer M, determine if the graph can be colored with at most M colors such that no two adjacent vertices share the same color. Return true if possible, else false.

Example 1:
Input: N = 4, M = 3, Edges = (0,1), (1,2), (2,3), (3,0), (0,2)
Output: true
Explanation: Valid 3-coloring exists: Vertex 0: color 1, Vertex 1: color 2, Vertex 2: color 3, Vertex 3: color 2.
Example 2:
Input: N = 3, M = 2, Edges = (0,1), (1,2), (0,2) (Triangle K3)
Output: false
Explanation: Triangle requires at least 3 colors. Cannot be colored with 2 colors.
Example 3:
Input: N = 1, M = 1
Output: true
Explanation: Single vertex colored with color 1.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Vertex node = 0 to N-1 par recursive DFS chalao. Har vertex par color = 1 to M try karo. Safety check karo: agar koi adjacent neighbor pehle se wahi color rakhta hai to color invalid hai. Agar valid mila, to assign karo aur agle node node + 1 par jao. Agar node N tak bina conflict pahuch gaye to return true!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Generate all M^V possible vertex colorings, verify each edge in graph.
Time: O(M^V * V^2) • Space: O(V) space
🟡 Better Approach:
Convert graph to adjacency list, check neighbors during assignment.
Time: O(M^V) • Space: O(V + E) list space
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Check neighbors in O(V) time. Recurse node-by-node with immediate true propagation. O(M^V) time and O(V) space.
Time: O(M^V) • Space: O(V) auxiliary recursion depth
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (All M^V Color Configurations Generation) 
bool isValidColoring(int v, int color[], bool graph[101][101]) {
    for (int i = 0; i < v; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < v; j++) {
            if (graph[i][j] && color[i] == color[j]) return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}
bool genColors(int node, int v, int m, int color[], bool graph[101][101]) {
    if (node == v) return isValidColoring(v, color, graph);
    for (int c = 1; c <= m; c++) {
        color[node] = c;
        if (genColors(node + 1, v, m, color, graph)) return true;
        color[node] = 0;
    }
    return false;
}
bool graphColoringBrute(bool graph[101][101], int m, int n) {
    int color[101] = {0};
    return genColors(0, n, m, color, graph);
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Adjacency List Backtracking) 
bool isSafeAdj(int node, int c, const vector<int> adj[], const vector<int>& col) {
    for (int neighbor : adj[node]) {
        if (col[neighbor] == c) return false;
    }
    return true;
}
bool solveAdj(int node, int v, int m, const vector<int> adj[], vector<int>& col) {
    if (node == v) return true;
    for (int c = 1; c <= m; c++) {
        if (isSafeAdj(node, c, adj, col)) {
            col[node] = c;
            if (solveAdj(node + 1, v, m, adj, col)) return true;
            col[node] = 0;
        }
    }
    return false;
}
bool graphColoringBetter(bool graph[101][101], int m, int n) {
    vector<int> adj[n];
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) if (graph[i][j]) adj[i].push_back(j);
    }
    vector<int> col(n, 0);
    return solveAdj(0, n, m, adj, col);
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (In-Place Backtracking with Short-Circuiting) 
bool isSafeColor(int node, int color[], bool graph[101][101], int n, int col) {
    for (int k = 0; k < n; k++) {
        if (k != node && graph[k][node] && color[k] == col) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}
bool solveMColoring(int node, int color[], int m, int n, bool graph[101][101]) {
    if (node == n) return true;
    for (int c = 1; c <= m; c++) {
        if (isSafeColor(node, color, graph, n, c)) {
            color[node] = c;
            if (solveMColoring(node + 1, color, m, n, graph)) return true;
            color[node] = 0;
        }
    }
    return false;
}
bool graphColoringOptimal(bool graph[101][101], int m, int n) {
    int color[101] = {0};
    return solveMColoring(0, color, m, n, graph);
}
Problem 21 • Hard Backtracking

Sudoku Solver

Hard Problem #37
Problem Statement Standard • Hard

Write a program to solve a Sudoku puzzle by filling the empty cells. A sudoku solution must satisfy: 1) Each digit 1-9 appears once per row. 2) Each digit 1-9 appears once per column. 3) Each digit 1-9 appears once per 3x3 sub-box. Empty cells are denoted by '.'.

Example 1:
Input: 9x9 board with standard partial clues
Output: Complete 9x9 board solved satisfying all constraints.
Explanation: Every row, column, and 3x3 block contains digits 1-9.
Example 2:
Input: Board with single empty cell
Output: Single empty cell filled with unique missing digit.
Explanation: Instant solution.
Example 3:
Input: Already valid full board
Output: Returns board as is.
Explanation: Already solved.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Board par empty cell '.' dhundo. Us cell ke liye digits '1' to '9' try karo. Ek single helper isValid(board, row, col, c) row, col, aur 3x3 block teeno ek hi loop for (int i = 0; i < 9; i++) me check kar leta hai! Formula: 3 * (row / 3) + i / 3 aur 3 * (col / 3) + i % 3. Agar valid digit mile to place karo aur recurse karo.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Try all 9^K combinations for K empty cells, validating whole board on each complete assignment.
Time: O(9^81) • Space: O(81) space
🟡 Better Approach:
Collect empty cells in vector>, check row, column, and box with 3 separate loops.
Time: O(9^emptyCells) • Space: O(emptyCells) auxiliary space
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Row, col, and 3x3 box checked simultaneously in a single 9-iteration loop. Solves in < 10ms with strictly O(1) space.
Time: O(9^emptyCells) (extremely pruned branch search) • Space: O(1) auxiliary space (81 recursion max depth)
Problem #37 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (All Combinations Generation and Validation) 
bool isValidSudokuFull(const vector<vector<char>>& b) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 9; i++) {
        unordered_set<char> row, col, box;
        for (int j = 0; j < 9; j++) {
            if (b[i][j] != '.' && !row.insert(b[i][j]).second) return false;
            if (b[j][i] != '.' && !col.insert(b[j][i]).second) return false;
            int r = 3 * (i / 3) + j / 3, c = 3 * (i % 3) + j % 3;
            if (b[r][c] != '.' && !box.insert(b[r][c]).second) return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Cell List Backtracking with 3 Separate Checks) 
bool checkValid3(vector<vector<char>>& b, int r, int c, char ch) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 9; i++) if (b[r][i] == ch) return false;
    for (int i = 0; i < 9; i++) if (b[i][c] == ch) return false;
    int sr = (r / 3) * 3, sc = (c / 3) * 3;
    for (int i = sr; i < sr + 3; i++) {
        for (int j = sc; j < sc + 3; j++) if (b[i][j] == ch) return false;
    }
    return true;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Single-Loop 3-Way Validity Backtracking) 
bool isValidSudoku(vector<vector<char>>& board, int row, int col, char c) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 9; i++) {
        if (board[row][i] == c) return false;
        if (board[i][col] == c) return false;
        if (board[3 * (row / 3) + i / 3][3 * (col / 3) + i % 3] == c) return false;
    }
    return true;
}
bool solveSudokuOptimal(vector<vector<char>>& board) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 9; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < 9; j++) {
            if (board[i][j] == '.') {
                for (char c = '1'; c <= '9'; c++) {
                    if (isValidSudoku(board, i, j, c)) {
                        board[i][j] = c;
                        if (solveSudokuOptimal(board)) return true;
                        board[i][j] = '.';
                    }
                }
                return false;
            }
        }
    }
    return true;
}
Problem 22 • Hard Backtracking

Expression Add Operators

Hard Problem #282
Problem Statement Standard • Hard

Given a string num that contains only digits and an integer target, return all possibilities to insert binary operators '+', '-', and/or '*' between the digits of num so that the resultant expression evaluates to target.

Example 1:
Input: num = "123", target = 6
Output: ["1*2*3","1+2+3"]
Explanation: 1*2*3 = 6 and 1+2+3 = 6.
Example 2:
Input: num = "232", target = 8
Output: ["2*3+2","2+3*2"]
Explanation: Both evaluate to 8 with operator precedence respected.
Example 3:
Input: num = "105", target = 5
Output: ["1*0+5","10-5"]
Explanation: Leading zeroes like '05' are invalid and excluded.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Multiplication operator '*' ki precedence addition aur subtraction se high hoti hai. Isliye recursive function me hume do values track karni padti hain: curVal (ab tak ka calculated sum) aur prevVal (pichhla term jo add ya subtract hua tha). Jab '*' aata hai, to (curVal - prevVal) + (prevVal * curNum) karke purani addition undo karte hain aur product jodte hain!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Insert all 4^(N-1) combinations of {'', '+', '-', '*'}, parse each using stack-based expression evaluator.
Time: O(4^N * N) • Space: O(4^N * N) space
🟡 Better Approach:
Track curVal and prevVal on each step, prune numbers with leading zeroes.
Time: O(4^N) • Space: O(N) recursion stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Formula: val - prev + prev * curNum for multiplication. Skips leading zeros immediately. O(4^N) time and O(N) space.
Time: O(4^N) • Space: O(N) recursion call stack
Problem #282 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Generate All Operator Strings & Shunting-Yard Parser) 
void generateExpressions(int ind, string expr, const string& num, int target, vector<string>& res) {
    if (ind == (int)num.size()) {
        // Evaluate expr using standard expression parsing stack
        return;
    }
    generateExpressions(ind + 1, expr + num[ind], num, target, res);
    generateExpressions(ind + 1, expr + "+" + num[ind], num, target, res);
    generateExpressions(ind + 1, expr + "-" + num[ind], num, target, res);
    generateExpressions(ind + 1, expr + "*" + num[ind], num, target, res);
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Backtracking with Dynamic Evaluation & Value Tracking) 
void addOpHelper(int ind, string path, long long val, long long prev, const string& num, int target, vector<string>& res) {
    if (ind == (int)num.size()) {
        if (val == target) res.push_back(path);
        return;
    }
    for (int i = ind; i < (int)num.size(); i++) {
        if (i > ind && num[ind] == '0') break;
        string part = num.substr(ind, i - ind + 1);
        long long cur = stoll(part);
        if (ind == 0) {
            addOpHelper(i + 1, part, cur, cur, num, target, res);
        } else {
            addOpHelper(i + 1, path + "+" + part, val + cur, cur, num, target, res);
            addOpHelper(i + 1, path + "-" + part, val - cur, -cur, num, target, res);
            addOpHelper(i + 1, path + "*" + part, val - prev + prev * cur, prev * cur, num, target, res);
        }
    }
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Optimized Backtracking with Operator Precedence Undo) 
void dfsOperators(int ind, const string& num, int target, string path, long long val, long long prev, vector<string>& result) {
    if (ind == (int)num.length()) {
        if (val == target) result.push_back(path);
        return;
    }
    for (int i = ind; i < (int)num.length(); i++) {
        if (i > ind && num[ind] == '0') break;
        string part = num.substr(ind, i - ind + 1);
        long long cur = stoll(part);
        if (ind == 0) {
            dfsOperators(i + 1, num, target, part, cur, cur, result);
        } else {
            dfsOperators(i + 1, num, target, path + "+" + part, val + cur, cur, result);
            dfsOperators(i + 1, num, target, path + "-" + part, val - cur, -cur, result);
            dfsOperators(i + 1, num, target, path + "*" + part, val - prev + prev * cur, prev * cur, result);
        }
    }
}
vector<string> addOperatorsOptimal(string num, int target) {
    vector<string> result;
    if (num.empty()) return result;
    dfsOperators(0, num, target, "", 0, 0, result);
    return result;
}
