Module 1: Fundamentals (Single LL) (14 Problems)

14 Problems
Problem 1 • Single LL

Introduction to Singly Linked List (Convert Array to LL)

Easy Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

Given an integer array arr of size N, construct a singly linked list where the elements of the list appear in the same order as in the array, and return the head pointer of the newly created linked list.

Example 1:
Input: arr = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
Output: 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> NULL
Explanation: Node 1 creates the head. Each subsequent element is chained to the next pointer in order.
Example 2:
Input: arr = [42]
Output: 42 -> NULL
Explanation: Array with a single item produces a single node linked list whose next pointer is NULL.
Example 3:
Input: arr = [10, 20]
Output: 10 -> 20 -> NULL
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Array elements contiguous memory me hote hain, jabki linked list nodes heap me random addresses par bante hain. Pehle element se head allocate karo, aur ek pointer mover ko head par rakho. Baaki elements par loop chala kar naya node allocate karo aur mover->next se bind karke mover ko aage badhaate jao.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Store each newly allocated node pointer in an auxiliary vector, then run a secondary loop to wire up all adjacent pointers.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) auxiliary vector
🟡 Better Approach:
Instantiate head with arr[0], then sequentially append each new node using a mover/tail pointer in a single pass.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Use a dummy head sentinel to unify node creation loop without branching conditions for the head element.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Vector of Node Pointers Linking) 
Node* constructLLBrute(vector<int>& arr) {
    if (arr.empty()) return nullptr;
    vector<Node*> nodes;
    for (int val : arr) {
        nodes.push_back(new Node(val));
    }
    for (size_t i = 0; i + 1 < nodes.size(); i++) {
        nodes[i]->next = nodes[i + 1];
    }
    return nodes[0];
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Iterative Direct Mover Pointer) 
Node* constructLLBetter(vector<int>& arr) {
    if (arr.empty()) return nullptr;
    Node* head = new Node(arr[0]);
    Node* mover = head;
    for (size_t i = 1; i < arr.size(); i++) {
        Node* temp = new Node(arr[i]);
        mover->next = temp;
        mover = temp;
    }
    return head;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Dummy Sentinel Node Chaining) 
Node* constructLLOptimal(vector<int>& arr) {
    Node dummy(0);
    Node* tail = &dummy;
    for (int val : arr) {
        tail->next = new Node(val);
        tail = tail->next;
    }
    return dummy.next;
}
Problem 2 • Single LL

Traversal in Linked List

Easy Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

Given the head of a singly linked list, print or collect each node's value in order from head to tail until reaching the terminating NULL pointer.

Example 1:
Input: head = 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> NULL
Output: [1, 2, 3]
Explanation: Pointer traverses node 1, then node 2, then node 3 before encountering NULL.
Example 2:
Input: head = 5 -> NULL
Output: [5]
Explanation: Only single node is visited, then pointer stops at NULL.
Example 3:
Input: head = NULL
Output: []
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Linked list me array ki tarah index based jump arr[i] allowed nahi hota. Traversing ke liye current pointer temp = head rakhte hain aur jab tak temp != nullptr ho, data access karte hain aur temp = temp->next aage shift karte hain.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Traverse list pushing every node's value into a vector, then iterate over vector to process values.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) vector space
🟡 Better Approach:
Print current node value and recursively invoke function on temp->next until reaching base case nullptr.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) recursion stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Single pointer linear scan using while loop with zero auxiliary space overhead.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Vector Value Buffer Collection) 
void printLLBrute(Node* head) {
    vector<int> res;
    Node* temp = head;
    while (temp != nullptr) {
        res.push_back(temp->data);
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    for (int v : res) cout << v << " ";
    cout << endl;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Recursive Function Call Stack Traversal) 
void printLLBetter(Node* head) {
    if (head == nullptr) return;
    cout << head->data << " ";
    printLLBetter(head->next);
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Standard In-Place Iterative Traversal) 
void printLLOptimal(Node* head) {
    Node* temp = head;
    while (temp != nullptr) {
        cout << temp->data << " ";
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    cout << endl;
}
Problem 3 • Single LL

Deletion in Linked List (4 Core Archetypes)

Medium Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Implement generalized deletion operations on a singly linked list across 4 core cases: deleting head, deleting tail, deleting k-th element, or deleting node with value X.

Example 1:
Input: head = 10 -> 20 -> 30, delete position 2
Output: 10 -> 30 -> NULL
Explanation: Node 20 at position 2 is unlinked and deleted. Node 10 points directly to 30.
Example 2:
Input: head = 5 -> 15, delete position 1 (head)
Output: 15 -> NULL
Explanation: Old head is deallocated and head pointer shifts to 15.
Example 3:
Input: head = 1 -> 2, delete position 2 (tail)
Output: 1 -> NULL
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Deletion me sabse important baat pointer rewire karna aur deleted node ki memory ko explicitly delete karna hota hai taaki C++ me memory leaks na hon. Preceding node prev->next = temp->next link karega.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Dump all nodes into an array, erase target index, then allocate and rebuild an entire new linked list.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) auxiliary space
🟡 Better Approach:
Traverse list tracking previous node and current node. Rewire prev->next to curr->next and free curr.
Time: O(K) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Attach dummy node before head so that head deletion and internal deletions share identical single-pointer logic.
Time: O(K) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Array Reconstruction Deletion) 
Node* deleteNodeBrute(Node* head, int k) {
    if (!head) return nullptr;
    vector<int> vals;

        vals.push_back(temp->data);

        delete temp;
        return head;
    }
    Node* prev = nullptr;
    Node* curr = head;
    int count = 1;
    while (curr && count < k) {
        prev = curr;
        curr = curr->next;
        count++;

        delete curr;

    return head;

        prev = prev->next;

    if (prev->next) {
        Node* target = prev->next;
        prev->next = target->next;
        delete target;
    }
    return dummy.next;
}

Input: head = 42 -> NULL
Output: 1
Explanation: Only 1 node is present.
Example 3:
Input: head = NULL
Output: 0
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Ek counter cnt = 0 initialize karo aur pointer temp = head lo. Loop while (temp != nullptr) me har step par cnt++ karo aur pointer ko temp = temp->next aage badhao.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Insert every node pointer into an unordered_set or vector, return set size.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) hash set space
🟡 Better Approach:
Recursively count nodes: 1 + getLength(head->next) with base case head == null returning 0.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) recursion stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Standard single loop traversal with a single integer counter.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Unordered Set Pointer Buffering) 
int getLengthBrute(Node* head) {
    unordered_set<Node*> visited;
    Node* temp = head;
    while (temp) {
        visited.insert(temp);
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    return visited.size();
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Recursive Call Stack Counting) 
int getLengthBetter(Node* head) {
    if (!head) return 0;
    return 1 + getLengthBetter(head->next);
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Iterative Single Counter Traversal) 
int getLengthOptimal(Node* head) {
    int cnt = 0;
    Node* temp = head;
    while (temp != nullptr) {
        cnt++;
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    return cnt;
}
Problem 14 • Single LL

Search in Linked List

Easy Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

Given the head of a singly linked list and an integer key, determine whether key is present in the linked list. Return true (or 1) if present, else false (or 0).

Example 1:
Input: head = 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4, key = 3
Output: true
Explanation: Node 3 is present in the list at position 3.
Example 2:
Input: head = 10 -> 20 -> 30, key = 50
Output: false
Explanation: Value 50 is not present in any node.
Example 3:
Input: head = NULL, key = 1
Output: false
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Head se shuru karke linear search lagao. Har node par check karo if (temp->data == key) return true;. Agar pointer nullptr tak pahuch gaya aur match nahi mila, to return false.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Dump all linked list values into a std::vector, then call std::find.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) vector space
🟡 Better Approach:
Check head->data == key, else recurse on head->next until base case nullptr.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) recursion stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
While loop scanning node values with immediate return on match.
Time: O(N) worst case, O(1) best case • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Vector Linear Search with STL find) 
bool searchLLBrute(Node* head, int key) {
    vector<int> vals;
    Node* temp = head;
    while (temp) {
        vals.push_back(temp->data);
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    return find(vals.begin(), vals.end(), key) != vals.end();
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Recursive Search Traversal) 
bool searchLLBetter(Node* head, int key) {
    if (!head) return false;
    if (head->data == key) return true;
    return searchLLBetter(head->next, key);
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Iterative Linear Scan with Early Exit) 
bool searchLLOptimal(Node* head, int key) {
    Node* temp = head;
    while (temp != nullptr) {
        if (temp->data == key) return true;
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    return false;
}

Module 2: Fundamentals (Doubly LL) (13 Problems)

13 Problems
Problem 15 • Doubly LL

Introduction to Doubly Linked List

Easy Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

Understand Doubly Linked List structure where each node contains data, a next pointer to the subsequent node, and a prev pointer to the preceding node. Construct a DLL from a given array.

Example 1:
Input: arr = [1, 2, 3]
Output: NULL <- 1 <-> 2 <-> 3 -> NULL
Explanation: Node 1 has prev=NULL, next=2. Node 2 has prev=1, next=3. Node 3 has prev=2, next=NULL.
Example 2:
Input: arr = [10]
Output: NULL <- 10 -> NULL
Explanation: Single node has both prev and next pointing to NULL.
Example 3:
Input: arr = [4, 8]
Output: NULL <- 4 <-> 8 -> NULL
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Singly LL me hum sirf aage ja sakte the, peeche nahi. Doubly LL me har node ke paas prev pointer bhi hota hai jisse bidirectional traversal possible ho jata hai.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Instantiate all nodes in a vector, then loop to set both next and prev pointers.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) auxiliary vector
🟡 Better Approach:
Maintain prev pointer while creating nodes one by one in a single pass.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Use Node constructor Node(val, next, prev) directly to eliminate intermediate assignments.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Array of Node Pointers Linking) 
Node* constructDLLBrute(vector<int>& arr) {
    if (arr.empty()) return nullptr;
    vector<Node*> nodes;
    for (int x : arr) nodes.push_back(new Node(x));
    for (size_t i = 0; i < nodes.size(); i++) {
        if (i > 0) nodes[i]->prev = nodes[i - 1];
        if (i + 1 < nodes.size()) nodes[i]->next = nodes[i + 1];
    }
    return nodes[0];
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Iterative Prev-Tracking Builder) 
Node* constructDLLBetter(vector<int>& arr) {
    if (arr.empty()) return nullptr;
    Node* head = new Node(arr[0]);
    Node* prevNode = head;
    for (size_t i = 1; i < arr.size(); i++) {
        Node* curr = new Node(arr[i]);
        curr->prev = prevNode;
        prevNode->next = curr;
        prevNode = curr;
    }
    return head;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Direct Constructor 3-Arg Chaining) 
Node* constructDLLOptimal(vector<int>& arr) {
    if (arr.empty()) return nullptr;
    Node* head = new Node(arr[0], nullptr, nullptr);
    Node* prev = head;
    for (size_t i = 1; i < arr.size(); i++) {
        Node* temp = new Node(arr[i], nullptr, prev);
        prev->next = temp;
        prev = temp;
    }
    return head;
}
Problem 16 • Doubly LL

Deletion in Doubly Linked List (Bidirectional Unlinking)

Medium Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given a pointer to a target node in a doubly linked list, delete the node in O(1) time without having access to the head pointer. (Target is guaranteed not to be the head).

Example 1:
Input: 1 <-> 2 <-> 3, target = node 2
Output: 1 <-> 3 -> NULL
Explanation: Node 1 connects its next to 3, node 3 connects its prev to 1. Node 2 is safely freed.
Example 2:
Input: 10 <-> 20, target = node 20 (tail)
Output: 10 -> NULL
Explanation: Node 10's next becomes NULL, node 20 is freed.
Example 3:
Input: 5 <-> 6 <-> 7 <-> 8, target = node 7
Output: 5 <-> 6 <-> 8 -> NULL
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
DLL me target node ke paas target->prev aur target->next dono hote hain. Isliye bina head traverse kiye hum target->prev->next = target->next aur agar target->next != null ho to target->next->prev = target->prev karke node delete kar sakte hain.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Walk backwards using prev pointers to locate head, then search forward to delete.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Directly rewire surrounding neighbors using target's prev and next with null checks.
Time: O(1) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
In-place O(1) pointer bypass and memory deletion.
Time: O(1) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Head Back-Tracking Traversal) 
void deleteNodeBrute(Node* target) {
    if (!target) return;
    Node* head = target;
    while (head->prev) head = head->prev;
    Node* curr = head;
    while (curr && curr != target) curr = curr->next;
    if (curr) {
        if (curr->prev) curr->prev->next = curr->next;
        if (curr->next) curr->next->prev = curr->prev;
        delete curr;
    }
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Direct Unlink with Null Checking) 
void deleteNodeBetter(Node* target) {
    if (!target) return;
    Node* back = target->prev;
    Node* front = target->next;
    if (back) back->next = front;
    if (front) front->prev = back;
    target->next = nullptr;
    target->prev = nullptr;
    delete target;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Safe O(1) Memory Deallocation) 
void deleteNodeOptimal(Node* target) {
    if (!target) return;
    target->prev->next = target->next;
    if (target->next != nullptr) {
        target->next->prev = target->prev;
    }
    delete target;
}
Problem 17 • Doubly LL

Insertion in Doubly Linked List (4-Pointer Wiring)

Medium Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Insert a new node with data val after a given node target in a Doubly Linked List. All 4 pointer updates must be maintained.

Example 1:
Input: 1 <-> 3, insert 2 after node 1
Output: 1 <-> 2 <-> 3 -> NULL
Explanation: Node 2 is spliced between 1 and 3. Four pointer connections are updated.
Example 2:
Input: 5 -> NULL, insert 10 after node 5
Output: 5 <-> 10 -> NULL
Explanation: Node 10 becomes the new tail.
Example 3:
Input: 1 <-> 2, insert 99 after node 2
Output: 1 <-> 2 <-> 99 -> NULL
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Jab DLL me do nodes (A aur B) ke beech naya node (N) insert karte hain, to 4 links update hote hain: 1) N->next = B, 2) N->prev = A, 3) B->prev = N (agar B null na ho), 4) A->next = N.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Convert DLL to vector, splice new element after target data, rebuild entire DLL.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) auxiliary space
🟡 Better Approach:
Find target node starting from head, then perform 4-pointer assignment.
Time: O(N) to find, O(1) to splice • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
When given direct target pointer, update 4 links in O(1) time without list traversal.
Time: O(1) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Array Splice and DLL Reconstruction) 
Node* insertAfterBrute(Node* head, int targetVal, int val) {
    vector<int> v;
    Node* t = head;
    while (t) { v.push_back(t->data); t = t->next; }
    for (size_t i = 0; i < v.size(); i++) {
        if (v[i] == targetVal) {
            v.insert(v.begin() + i + 1, val);
            break;
        }
    }
    return constructDLLOptimal(v);
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Target Search then 4-Way Splice) 
void insertAfterBetter(Node* head, int targetVal, int val) {
    Node* curr = head;
    while (curr && curr->data != targetVal) curr = curr->next;
    if (!curr) return;
    Node* newNode = new Node(val);
    newNode->next = curr->next;
    newNode->prev = curr;
    if (curr->next) curr->next->prev = newNode;
    curr->next = newNode;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Direct O(1) 4-Pointer Splice) 
void insertAfterOptimal(Node* target, int val) {
    if (!target) return;
    Node* newNode = new Node(val, target->next, target);
    if (target->next != nullptr) {
        target->next->prev = newNode;
    }
    target->next = newNode;
}

🔴 1. Brute Force (Vector of Nodes Double-Link Loop) 
Node* arrayToDLLBrute(vector<int>& arr) {

Node* arrayToDLLBetter(vector<int>& arr) {

    for (size_t i = 1; i < arr.size(); i++) {

Node* arrayToDLLOptimal(vector<int>& arr) {

    for (size_t i = 1; i < arr.size(); i++) {

Problem 19 • Doubly LL

Delete Tail of Doubly Linked List

Easy Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

Given the head of a Doubly Linked List, remove the last node (tail) and return the head pointer. Safely deallocate the removed node.

Example 1:
Input: 1 <-> 2 <-> 3 -> NULL
Output: 1 <-> 2 -> NULL
Explanation: Node 3 is removed. Node 2 becomes new tail with next=NULL.
Example 2:
Input: 5 -> NULL
Output: NULL
Explanation: Single node list becomes empty after deletion.
Example 3:
Input: 10 <-> 20 -> NULL
Output: 10 -> NULL
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Tail delete karne ke liye list ke aakhiri node tak traverse karo while (tail->next != nullptr) tail = tail->next;. Phir uske previous node ko pakad kar newTail = tail->prev; newTail->next = nullptr; tail->prev = nullptr; delete tail;.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Collect all node pointers in vector, disconnect 2nd last, delete last.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) vector space
🟡 Better Approach:
Traverse to tail tracking prev, unlink prev's next and free tail.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Advance to tail node, decouple bidirectional links in-place and delete.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Vector Pointers Deletion) 
Node* deleteTailDLLBrute(Node* head) {
    if (!head || !head->next) { delete head; return nullptr; }
    vector<Node*> nodes;
    Node* t = head;
    while (t) { nodes.push_back(t); t = t->next; }
    Node* last = nodes.back();
    Node* secondLast = nodes[nodes.size() - 2];
    secondLast->next = nullptr;
    last->prev = nullptr;
    delete last;
    return head;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Two-Pointer (prev and curr) Scan) 
Node* deleteTailDLLBetter(Node* head) {
    if (!head || !head->next) { delete head; return nullptr; }
    Node* tail = head;
    while (tail->next) tail = tail->next;
    Node* prevNode = tail->prev;
    prevNode->next = nullptr;
    tail->prev = nullptr;
    delete tail;
    return head;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (In-Place Backward Unlink) 
Node* deleteTailDLLOptimal(Node* head) {
    if (!head || !head->next) { delete head; return nullptr; }
    Node* tail = head;
    while (tail->next != nullptr) {
        tail = tail->next;
    }
    Node* newTail = tail->prev;
    newTail->next = nullptr;
    tail->prev = nullptr;
    delete tail;
    return head;
}
Problem 20 • Doubly LL

Delete K-th Element of Doubly Linked List

Medium Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given the head of a Doubly Linked List and an integer k (1-based index), delete the k-th node from the list and return the head pointer.

Example 1:
Input: 1 <-> 2 <-> 3 <-> 4, k = 2
Output: 1 <-> 3 <-> 4 -> NULL
Explanation: Node 2 is unlinked. Node 1's next points to 3, and Node 3's prev points to 1.
Example 2:
Input: 10 <-> 20, k = 1
Output: 20 -> NULL
Explanation: Deleting 1st node shifts head to 20 with prev=NULL.
Example 3:
Input: 5 <-> 6 <-> 7, k = 3
Output: 5 <-> 6 -> NULL
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Agar k == 1 hai, to head delete hoga. Agar k-th node tail hai, to tail delete hoga. Agar beech me hai, to front = kNode->next aur back = kNode->prev ko apas me link karke kNode ko delete kar do.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Extract values to vector, erase index k - 1, rebuild new DLL.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) auxiliary space
🟡 Better Approach:
Advance counter to k, branch on whether target is head, tail, or middle node.
Time: O(K) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Locate k-th node and update back->next and front->prev directly with clean memory cleanup.
Time: O(K) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Array Filter and Rebuild DLL) 
Node* deleteKthDLLBrute(Node* head, int k) {
    vector<int> v;
    Node* t = head;
    while (t) { v.push_back(t->data); t = t->next; }
    if (k <= 0 || k > (int)v.size()) return head;
    v.erase(v.begin() + (k - 1));
    return constructDLLOptimal(v);
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Count Search with Conditional Edge Cases) 
Node* deleteKthDLLBetter(Node* head, int k) {
    if (!head) return nullptr;
    int cnt = 0;
    Node* kNode = head;
    while (kNode) {
        cnt++;
        if (cnt == k) break;
        kNode = kNode->next;
    }
    if (!kNode) return head;
    Node* prevNode = kNode->prev;
    Node* nextNode = kNode->next;
    if (!prevNode && !nextNode) { delete kNode; return nullptr; }
    if (!prevNode) { head = head->next; head->prev = nullptr; delete kNode; return head; }
    if (!nextNode) { prevNode->next = nullptr; delete kNode; return head; }
    prevNode->next = nextNode;
    nextNode->prev = prevNode;
    delete kNode;
    return head;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Standard In-Place 2-Sided Unlink) 
Node* deleteKthDLLOptimal(Node* head, int k) {
    if (!head) return nullptr;
    int cnt = 0;
    Node* kNode = head;
    while (kNode) {
        cnt++;
        if (cnt == k) break;
        kNode = kNode->next;
    }
    if (!kNode) return head;
    Node* back = kNode->prev;
    Node* front = kNode->next;
    if (back == nullptr && front == nullptr) { delete kNode; return nullptr; }
    if (back == nullptr) { head = front; front->prev = nullptr; delete kNode; return head; }
    if (front == nullptr) { back->next = nullptr; delete kNode; return head; }
    back->next = front;
    front->prev = back;
    delete kNode;
    return head;
}
Problem 21 • Doubly LL

Removing Given Node in Doubly Linked List

Easy Coding Platform & Standard
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

Given a direct pointer to a node in a Doubly Linked List, delete this node in-place. Note: The given node is guaranteed not to be the head node.

Example 1:
Input: 1 <-> 2 <-> 3, given node = 2
Output: 1 <-> 3 -> NULL
Explanation: Node 2's neighbors (1 and 3) are connected together directly.

💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Hume direct target node pointer diya hai, isliye list traverse karne ki zaroorat hi nahi hai. Target ke peeche wala node prev = target->prev aur aage wala node next = target->next pakdo. prev->next = next aur agar next null na ho to next->prev = prev.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Walk back to head pointer, linear search to confirm identity, then delete.

Store back = target->prev and front = target->next, rewire and delete target.

Coding Platform & Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++

void deleteGivenNodeBrute(Node* target) {

void deleteGivenNodeOptimal(Node* target) {

🟢 Optimal Approach:
Construct Node(val, head, nullptr) and link head->prev conditionally in 2 lines.

Problem 23 • Doubly LL

Insert Node Before Tail in Doubly Linked List

Given the head of a Doubly Linked List and an integer val, insert a new node with value val immediately before the tail node.

Output: 1 <-> 2 <-> 3 <-> 4 -> NULL
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Tail node tak traverse karo while (tail->next != nullptr) tail = tail->next;. Agar tail ka prev == nullptr hai, to ye single node list thi, direct head ke pehle insert karo. Warna prevNode = tail->prev pakad kar 4 links update karo.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Convert DLL to vector, insert before last element, rebuild DLL.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) auxiliary space
🟡 Better Approach:
Locate tail, cache tail->prev, insert newNode between tail->prev and tail.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Clean in-place splice before tail with Node constructor wiring next and prev directly.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Array Splicing Rebuild) 
Node* insertBeforeTailBrute(Node* head, int val) {
    vector<int> v;
    Node* t = head;
    while (t) { v.push_back(t->data); t = t->next; }
    if (v.empty()) v.push_back(val);
    else v.insert(v.end() - 1, val);
    return constructDLLOptimal(v);
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Traverse to Tail and Rewire 4 Links) 
Node* insertBeforeTailBetter(Node* head, int val) {
    if (!head->next) return insertBeforeHeadOptimal(head, val);
    Node* tail = head;
    while (tail->next) tail = tail->next;
    Node* prevNode = tail->prev;
    Node* newNode = new Node(val, tail, prevNode);
    prevNode->next = newNode;
    tail->prev = newNode;
    return head;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Direct Constructor 4-Way Splice) 
Node* insertBeforeTailOptimal(Node* head, int val) {
    if (!head || !head->next) {
        return insertBeforeHeadOptimal(head, val);
    }
    Node* tail = head;
    while (tail->next != nullptr) {
        tail = tail->next;
    }
    Node* prevNode = tail->prev;
    Node* newNode = new Node(val, tail, prevNode);
    prevNode->next = newNode;
    tail->prev = newNode;
    return head;
}
Problem 24 • Doubly LL

Insert Node Before K-th Node in Doubly Linked List

Medium Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given the head of a Doubly Linked List, an integer val, and a 1-based position k, insert a new node with data val before the k-th node.

Example 1:
Input: 1 <-> 3 <-> 4, val = 2, k = 2
Output: 1 <-> 2 <-> 3 <-> 4 -> NULL
Explanation: Node 2 is inserted before the 2nd node (3).
Example 2:
Input: 5 <-> 10, val = 1, k = 1
Output: 1 <-> 5 <-> 10 -> NULL
Explanation: Inserting before 1st node creates a new head.
Example 3:
Input: 10 <-> 30, val = 20, k = 2
Output: 10 <-> 20 <-> 30 -> NULL
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Agar k == 1 hai, to seedha head ke pehle insert hoga insertBeforeHead. Warna counter chala kar k-th node par pahucho. Uska prevNode = temp->prev lo, aur dono ke beech naya node splice kar do.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Dump DLL to vector, insert at k - 1, construct fresh DLL.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) auxiliary space
🟡 Better Approach:
Check k == 1 first, else traverse count to k and update 4 links.
Time: O(K) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Loop to k-th node and rewire pointers in O(1) auxiliary space.
Time: O(K) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Array Splicing Rebuild DLL) 
Node* insertBeforeKthBrute(Node* head, int val, int k) {
    vector<int> v;
    Node* t = head;
    while (t) { v.push_back(t->data); t = t->next; }
    if (k <= 1) v.insert(v.begin(), val);
    else if (k > (int)v.size()) v.push_back(val);
    else v.insert(v.begin() + (k - 1), val);
    return constructDLLOptimal(v);
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Counter Traversal with Head Condition) 
Node* insertBeforeKthBetter(Node* head, int val, int k) {
    if (k == 1) return insertBeforeHeadOptimal(head, val);
    Node* temp = head;
    int cnt = 0;
    while (temp) {
        cnt++;
        if (cnt == k) break;
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    Node* prevNode = temp->prev;
    Node* newNode = new Node(val, temp, prevNode);
    prevNode->next = newNode;
    temp->prev = newNode;
    return head;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Single-Scan In-Place 4-Link Insertion) 
Node* insertBeforeKthOptimal(Node* head, int val, int k) {
    if (k == 1) {
        return insertBeforeHeadOptimal(head, val);
    }
    Node* temp = head;
    int cnt = 0;
    while (temp != nullptr) {
        cnt++;
        if (cnt == k) break;
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    if (!temp) return head;
    Node* prevNode = temp->prev;
    Node* newNode = new Node(val, temp, prevNode);
    prevNode->next = newNode;
    temp->prev = newNode;
    return head;
}
Problem 25 • Doubly LL

Insert Before Given Node in Doubly Linked List

Easy Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

Given a direct pointer to a node target in a Doubly Linked List and an integer val, insert a new node with data val immediately before target. (target is guaranteed not to be head).

Example 1:
Input: 1 <-> 3, val = 2, target = node 3
Output: 1 <-> 2 <-> 3 -> NULL
Explanation: Node 2 is inserted before node 3.
Example 2:
Input: 10 <-> 30, val = 20, target = node 30
Output: 10 <-> 20 <-> 30 -> NULL
Explanation: Node 20 is placed between 10 and 30.
Example 3:
Input: 7 <-> 9, val = 8, target = node 9
Output: 7 <-> 8 <-> 9 -> NULL
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Direct target pointer milne ka fayda ye hai ki hum O(1) time me target->prev access kar sakte hain. prevNode = target->prev pakdo. newNode = new Node(val, target, prevNode) banao, aur prevNode->next = newNode; target->prev = newNode;.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Backtrack to head pointer, search forward to locate node, then insert.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Cache target->prev, instantiate node, update 4 links explicitly.
Time: O(1) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Construct Node(val, target, target->prev) and link adjacent pointers in O(1) time.
Time: O(1) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Trace to Head and Linear Search) 
void insertBeforeGivenBrute(Node* target, int val) {
    if (!target) return;
    Node* h = target;
    while (h->prev) h = h->prev;
    Node* curr = h;
    while (curr && curr != target) curr = curr->next;
    if (curr) {
        Node* p = curr->prev;
        Node* n = new Node(val, curr, p);
        if (p) p->next = n;
        curr->prev = n;
    }
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Direct 4-Link Rewiring with Temp) 
void insertBeforeGivenBetter(Node* target, int val) {
    if (!target) return;
    Node* prevNode = target->prev;
    Node* newNode = new Node(val);
    newNode->next = target;
    newNode->prev = prevNode;
    if (prevNode) prevNode->next = newNode;
    target->prev = newNode;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Constructor Inlined O(1) Insertion) 
void insertBeforeGivenOptimal(Node* target, int val) {
    if (!target) return;
    Node* prevNode = target->prev;
    Node* newNode = new Node(val, target, prevNode);
    prevNode->next = newNode;
    target->prev = newNode;
}
Problem 26 • Doubly LL

Delete Head of Doubly Linked List

Easy Coding Platform & Standard
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

Given the head of a Doubly Linked List, delete the first node (head) and return the updated head pointer. Prevent any memory leaks.

Example 1:
Input: 1 <-> 2 <-> 3 -> NULL
Output: 2 <-> 3 -> NULL
Explanation: Node 1 is removed. Node 2 becomes head with prev=NULL.
Example 2:
Input: 10 -> NULL
Output: NULL
Explanation: Deleting the only node leaves the list empty.
Example 3:
Input: 5 <-> 15 -> NULL
Output: 15 -> NULL
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Purane head ko temporary pointer prev = head me store karo. Head ko aage badhao head = head->next. Agar naya head exist karta hai, to uska head->prev = nullptr kar do taaki backward reference clean ho jaye. Phir delete prev.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Copy elements from index 1 onwards to vector, rebuild new DLL.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) auxiliary space
🟡 Better Approach:
Shift head forward and clear prev (causes memory leak of old head).
Time: O(1) • Space: O(1) (Leaked memory)
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Save old head in temp, update head->prev = nullptr, deallocate temp safely.
Time: O(1) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Coding Platform & Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Array Reconstruction DLL) 
Node* deleteHeadDLLBrute(Node* head) {
    if (!head || !head->next) { delete head; return nullptr; }
    vector<int> v;
    Node* t = head->next;
    while (t) { v.push_back(t->data); t = t->next; }
    return constructDLLOptimal(v);
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Pointer Shift without Deletion) 
Node* deleteHeadDLLBetter(Node* head) {
    if (!head || !head->next) return nullptr;
    head = head->next;
    head->prev = nullptr;
    return head;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Safe Memory Deallocation In-Place) 
Node* deleteHeadDLLOptimal(Node* head) {
    if (!head || !head->next) {
        delete head;
        return nullptr;
    }
    Node* prev = head;
    head = head->next;
    head->prev = nullptr;
    prev->next = nullptr;
    delete prev;
    return head;
}
Problem 27 • Doubly LL

Reverse a Doubly Linked List

Easy Coding Platform & Standard
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

Given the head of a Doubly Linked List, reverse the list in-place so that the old tail becomes the new head and all next and prev pointers are correctly swapped.

Example 1:
Input: 1 <-> 2 <-> 3 <-> 4 -> NULL
Output: 4 <-> 3 <-> 2 <-> 1 -> NULL
Explanation: All bidirectional links are swapped. Node 4 is the new head.
Example 2:
Input: 10 -> NULL
Output: 10 -> NULL
Explanation: Single node list remains unchanged.
Example 3:
Input: 5 <-> 10 -> NULL
Output: 10 <-> 5 -> NULL
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Har node par ja kar uska next aur prev pointers swap kar do! Pointer curr = head lo: swap(curr->next, curr->prev). Phir aage badhne ke liye curr = curr->prev karo (kyunki swap hone ke baad purana next ab prev ban chuka hai). Aakhiri swapped node naya head ban jayega.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Push all node values onto a stack, then traverse list again popping values into nodes.
Time: O(2N) • Space: O(N) stack space
🟡 Better Approach:
Recursively reach tail swapping next and prev pointers on call stack unwind.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) recursion stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
In-place single pass swapping current node's next and prev pointers with zero extra space.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Coding Platform & Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Stack Data Reversal) 
Node* reverseDLLBrute(Node* head) {
    if (!head || !head->next) return head;
    stack<int> st;
    Node* temp = head;
    while (temp) { st.push(temp->data); temp = temp->next; }
    temp = head;
    while (temp) {
        temp->data = st.top();
        st.pop();
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    return head;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Recursive Link Swapping) 
Node* reverseDLLBetter(Node* head) {
    if (!head || !head->next) {
        if (head) swap(head->next, head->prev);
        return head;
    }
    Node* newHead = reverseDLLBetter(head->next);
    swap(head->next, head->prev);
    return newHead;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Single Pass Pointer Swapping) 
Node* reverseDLLOptimal(Node* head) {
    if (!head || !head->next) return head;
    Node* last = nullptr;
    Node* current = head;
    while (current != nullptr) {
        last = current->prev;
        current->prev = current->next;
        current->next = last;
        current = current->prev;
    }
    return last->prev;
}

Problem 28 • Logic Building

Add Two Numbers in Linked List

Medium Problem #2
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

You are given two non-empty linked lists representing two non-negative integers. The digits are stored in reverse order, and each of their nodes contains a single digit. Add the two numbers and return the sum as a linked list in reverse order.

Example 1:
Input: l1 = 2 -> 4 -> 3, l2 = 5 -> 6 -> 4
Output: 7 -> 0 -> 8 -> NULL
Explanation: 342 + 465 = 807. Reversing 807 gives 7 -> 0 -> 8.
Example 2:
Input: l1 = 0, l2 = 0
Output: 0 -> NULL
Explanation: 0 + 0 = 0.
Example 3:
Input: l1 = 9 -> 9 -> 9, l2 = 1
Output: 0 -> 0 -> 0 -> 1 -> NULL
Explanation: 999 + 1 = 1000, so reverse is 0 -> 0 -> 0 -> 1.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Digits already reversed order me hain, jo school addition (units place se start) ke liye perfect hai! Ek dummy node aur carry variable carry = 0 banao. Loop chalao jab tak l1, l2 ya carry me se koi bhi bacha ho. Har step par sum nikaalo sum = carry + l1->val + l2->val, naya node sum % 10 banao aur carry update karo carry = sum / 10.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Convert both linked lists to large integer strings, perform manual string column addition, and convert the result back to a linked list.
Time: O(N + M) • Space: O(max(N, M)) string space
🟡 Better Approach:
Recursively advance both list pointers passing carry to next recursive frame, unwinding to construct nodes.
Time: O(max(N, M)) • Space: O(max(N, M)) recursion stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Single pass traversal using dummy node and carry variable. Runs in O(max(N, M)) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
Time: O(max(N, M)) • Space: O(max(N, M)) for result list, O(1) auxiliary
Problem #2 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (BigInt String Conversion & Addition) 
ListNode* addTwoNumbersBrute(ListNode* l1, ListNode* l2) {
    string s1 = "", s2 = "";
    while (l1) { s1 += to_string(l1->val); l1 = l1->next; }
    while (l2) { s2 += to_string(l2->val); l2 = l2->next; }
    int i = 0, j = 0, carry = 0;
    ListNode dummy(0);
    ListNode* curr = &dummy;
    while (i < (int)s1.size() || j < (int)s2.size() || carry) {
        int sum = carry;
        if (i < (int)s1.size()) sum += (s1[i++] - '0');
        if (j < (int)s2.size()) sum += (s2[j++] - '0');
        carry = sum / 10;
        curr->next = new ListNode(sum % 10);
        curr = curr->next;
    }
    return dummy.next;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Recursive Column Addition with Carry Passing) 
ListNode* addHelper(ListNode* l1, ListNode* l2, int carry) {
    if (!l1 && !l2 && carry == 0) return nullptr;
    int sum = carry;
    if (l1) { sum += l1->val; l1 = l1->next; }
    if (l2) { sum += l2->val; l2 = l2->next; }
    ListNode* node = new ListNode(sum % 10);
    node->next = addHelper(l1, l2, sum / 10);
    return node;
}
ListNode* addTwoNumbersBetter(ListNode* l1, ListNode* l2) {
    return addHelper(l1, l2, 0);
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Dummy Head Single-Pass Iterative Addition) 
ListNode* addTwoNumbersOptimal(ListNode* l1, ListNode* l2) {
    ListNode dummy(0);
    ListNode* curr = &dummy;
    int carry = 0;
    while (l1 != nullptr || l2 != nullptr || carry != 0) {
        int sum = carry;
        if (l1 != nullptr) {
            sum += l1->val;
            l1 = l1->next;
        }
        if (l2 != nullptr) {
            sum += l2->val;
            l2 = l2->next;
        }
        carry = sum / 10;
        curr->next = new ListNode(sum % 10);
        curr = curr->next;
    }
    return dummy.next;
}
Problem 29 • Logic Building

Segregate Odd and Even Nodes in Linked List

Medium Problem #328
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given the head of a singly linked list, group all the nodes with odd indices together followed by the nodes with even indices, and return the reordered list. The first node is considered odd, the second node even, and so on. Relative order within odd and even groups must be preserved.

Example 1:
Input: head = 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> NULL
Output: 1 -> 3 -> 5 -> 2 -> 4 -> NULL
Explanation: Odd-indexed nodes: [1, 3, 5], Even-indexed nodes: [2, 4]. Grouping gives 1 -> 3 -> 5 -> 2 -> 4.
Example 2:
Input: head = 2 -> 1 -> 3 -> 5 -> 6 -> 4 -> 7 -> NULL
Output: 2 -> 3 -> 6 -> 7 -> 1 -> 5 -> 4 -> NULL
Explanation: Odd positions: 1st(2), 3rd(3), 5th(6), 7th(7). Even positions: 2nd(1), 4th(5), 6th(4).
Example 3:
Input: head = 1 -> 2 -> NULL
Output: 1 -> 2 -> NULL
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Odd aur Even nodes ke pointers ko parallel chalao: odd = head, even = head->next, aur even ke head ko save kar lo evenHead = even. Har step par odd->next = even->next aur even->next = odd->next->next karte hue 2-2 step jump karo. Aakhir me odd->next = evenHead connect kar do.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Collect all odd-indexed values first into a vector, then even-indexed values, then overwrite node data.
Time: O(2N) • Space: O(N) auxiliary vector
🟡 Better Approach:
Maintain two separate chains oddDummy and evenDummy, detach each node and append to respective chain, then link oddTail->next = evenDummy.next.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Direct in-place rewiring: odd->next = even->next, odd advances; even->next = odd->next, even advances. Then odd->next = evenHead.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Problem #328 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Vector Array Re-ordering and Value Copy) 
ListNode* oddEvenListBrute(ListNode* head) {
    if (!head || !head->next) return head;
    vector<int> vals;
    ListNode* temp = head;
    while (temp) {
        vals.push_back(temp->val);
        if (temp->next) temp = temp->next->next;
        else break;
    }
    temp = head->next;
    while (temp) {
        vals.push_back(temp->val);
        if (temp->next) temp = temp->next->next;
        else break;
    }
    temp = head;
    int i = 0;
    while (temp) {
        temp->val = vals[i++];
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    return head;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Two Separate Dummy Lists and Merge) 
ListNode* oddEvenListBetter(ListNode* head) {
    if (!head || !head->next) return head;
    ListNode oddD(0), evenD(0);
    ListNode* o = &oddD, *e = &evenD;
    ListNode* curr = head;
    int idx = 1;
    while (curr) {
        if (idx % 2 != 0) { o->next = curr; o = o->next; }
        else { e->next = curr; e = e->next; }
        curr = curr->next;
        idx++;
    }
    e->next = nullptr;
    o->next = evenD.next;
    return oddD.next;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Two-Pointer In-Place Leapfrogging) 
ListNode* oddEvenListOptimal(ListNode* head) {
    if (head == nullptr || head->next == nullptr) return head;
    ListNode* odd = head;
    ListNode* even = head->next;
    ListNode* evenHead = even;
    while (even != nullptr && even->next != nullptr) {
        odd->next = even->next;
        odd = odd->next;
        even->next = odd->next;
        even = even->next;
    }
    odd->next = evenHead;
    return head;
}
Problem 30 • Logic Building

Sort a Linked List of 0's, 1's and 2's

Medium Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given a singly linked list where every node contains either 0, 1, or 2, sort the linked list so that all 0s appear first, followed by all 1s, followed by all 2s. The algorithm should ideally re-link nodes in-place rather than overwriting node values.

Example 1:
Input: head = 1 -> 2 -> 2 -> 1 -> 2 -> 0 -> 2 -> 2 -> NULL
Output: 0 -> 1 -> 1 -> 2 -> 2 -> 2 -> 2 -> 2 -> NULL
Explanation: All 0s are grouped first (one 0), followed by two 1s, followed by five 2s.
Example 2:
Input: head = 2 -> 1 -> 0 -> NULL
Output: 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> NULL
Explanation: List is rearranged into strictly ascending sorted order.
Example 3:
Input: head = 0 -> 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 0 -> NULL
Output: 0 -> 0 -> 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> NULL
Explanation: Three 0s, one 1, and one 2.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Sabse basic sochna ye hai ki saare data ko array me daal ke sort kar lo (Brute). Better approach me 0s, 1s aur 2s ka count count0, count1, count2 store karo aur 2nd pass me list values overwrite kar do. Lekin Optimal interview standard me interviewers node pointers ko rewire karne bolte hain: 3 dummy heads banao (zeroHead, oneHead, twoHead), nodes ko filter karke unme baanto, aur fir teeno chains ko O(1) me concatenate kar do!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Dump all node values into std::vector, sort using std::sort (O(N log N)), then overwrite node data in second pass.
Time: O(N log N) • Space: O(N) auxiliary vector
🟡 Better Approach:
Count frequency of 0, 1, and 2 in pass 1. In pass 2, overwrite node values according to frequencies in O(2N) time and O(1) space.
Time: O(2N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Maintain zeroHead, oneHead, and twoHead dummy nodes. Segregate nodes without value overwriting, then splice chains together in O(N) time and O(1) space.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Vector Array std::sort and Value Overwrite) 
Node* segregate012Brute(Node* head) {
    if (!head || !head->next) return head;
    vector<int> vals;
    Node* temp = head;
    while (temp) { vals.push_back(temp->data); temp = temp->next; }
    sort(vals.begin(), vals.end());
    temp = head;
    int i = 0;
    while (temp) { temp->data = vals[i++]; temp = temp->next; }
    return head;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Two-Pass Counting Sort (Value Overwrite)) 
Node* segregate012Better(Node* head) {
    int cnt0 = 0, cnt1 = 0, cnt2 = 0;
    Node* temp = head;
    while (temp) {
        if (temp->data == 0) cnt0++;
        else if (temp->data == 1) cnt1++;
        else cnt2++;
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    temp = head;
    while (temp) {
        if (cnt0 > 0) { temp->data = 0; cnt0--; }
        else if (cnt1 > 0) { temp->data = 1; cnt1--; }
        else { temp->data = 2; cnt2--; }
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    return head;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Three Dummy Chains In-Place Pointer Rewiring) 
Node* segregate012Optimal(Node* head) {
    if (!head || !head->next) return head;
    Node zeroDummy(0), oneDummy(0), twoDummy(0);
    Node* zero = &zeroDummy;
    Node* one = &oneDummy;
    Node* two = &twoDummy;
    Node* curr = head;
    while (curr != nullptr) {
        if (curr->data == 0) {
            zero->next = curr;
            zero = zero->next;
        } else if (curr->data == 1) {
            one->next = curr;
            one = one->next;
        } else {
            two->next = curr;
            two = two->next;
        }
        curr = curr->next;
    }
    zero->next = (oneDummy.next != nullptr) ? oneDummy.next : twoDummy.next;
    one->next = twoDummy.next;
    two->next = nullptr;
    return zeroDummy.next;
}
Problem 31 • Logic Building

Remove N-th Node From End of List

Medium Problem #19
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given the head of a linked list, remove the n-th node from the end of the list and return its head. The solution must handle edge cases like removing the head node cleanly.

Example 1:
Input: head = 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5, n = 2
Output: 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 5 -> NULL
Explanation: The 2nd node from the end is node 4. Unlinking it leaves 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 5.
Example 2:
Input: head = 1, n = 1
Output: NULL
Explanation: Removing the only node from the end leaves the list empty.
Example 3:
Input: head = 1 -> 2, n = 1
Output: 1 -> NULL
Explanation: The 1st node from the end is node 2 (tail).
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
End se n-th node matlab start se (Total Length - n + 1)-th node! Naive way me hum length count karte hain fir traverse karte hain. Lekin Single-Pass Optimal trick me Two Pointers (Fast & Slow) use karo: Fast pointer ko pehle n steps aage bhejo. Phir Slow aur Fast dono ko simultaneously ek-ek step chalao jab tak Fast last node par na pahuch jaye. Us moment par Slow theek target node ke pehle khada hoga! slow->next = slow->next->next.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Collect all node pointers in vector, find target index (size - n), unlink and delete target.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) pointer vector space
🟡 Better Approach:
Pass 1 counts total nodes L. Pass 2 traverses L - n steps to target predecessor and removes node.
Time: O(2N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Fast moves n steps ahead. Then Fast and Slow move in tandem until Fast reaches the end. Removes node in a single O(N) pass.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Problem #19 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Vector Pointer Buffering & Index Calculation) 
ListNode* removeNthFromEndBrute(ListNode* head, int n) {
    if (!head) return nullptr;
    vector<ListNode*> nodes;
    ListNode* curr = head;
    while (curr) { nodes.push_back(curr); curr = curr->next; }
    int targetIdx = (int)nodes.size() - n;
    if (targetIdx == 0) {
        ListNode* newHead = head->next;
        delete head;
        return newHead;
    }
    nodes[targetIdx - 1]->next = nodes[targetIdx]->next;
    delete nodes[targetIdx];
    return head;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Two-Pass Total Length Counting) 
ListNode* removeNthFromEndBetter(ListNode* head, int n) {
    int total = 0;
    ListNode* temp = head;
    while (temp) { total++; temp = temp->next; }
    if (total == n) {
        ListNode* newHead = head->next;
        delete head;
        return newHead;
    }
    int steps = total - n;
    temp = head;
    for (int i = 1; i < steps; i++) {
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    ListNode* toDelete = temp->next;
    temp->next = toDelete->next;
    delete toDelete;
    return head;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Fast & Slow Two-Pointer Single Pass) 
ListNode* removeNthFromEndOptimal(ListNode* head, int n) {
    ListNode dummy(0);
    dummy.next = head;
    ListNode* fast = &dummy;
    ListNode* slow = &dummy;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        fast = fast->next;
    }
    while (fast->next != nullptr) {
        fast = fast->next;
        slow = slow->next;
    }
    ListNode* toDelete = slow->next;
    slow->next = slow->next->next;
    delete toDelete;
    return dummy.next;
}
Problem 32 • Logic Building

Reverse a Singly Linked List (Iterative & Optimal)

Easy Problem #206
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list in-place and return the reversed list's head.

Example 1:
Input: head = 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> NULL
Output: 5 -> 4 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1 -> NULL
Explanation: The original head 1 becomes the tail, and 5 becomes the new head.
Example 2:
Input: head = 1 -> 2 -> NULL
Output: 2 -> 1 -> NULL
Explanation: Reversing two nodes simply inverts their link.
Example 3:
Input: head = NULL
Output: NULL
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
List ko reverse karte waqt pointers ka orientation palatna padta hai. Teen pointers maintain karo: prev = nullptr, curr = head, aur next = nullptr. Har step par agle node ko lose hone se bachane ke liye next = curr->next save karo, fir pointer palto curr->next = prev, aur dono ko ek-ek kadam aage shift karo: prev = curr; curr = next;. Jab curr null ho jayega, prev naya head hoga!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Push all node values onto a stack, then traverse list again popping values into nodes in O(2N) time and O(N) space.
Time: O(2N) • Space: O(N) stack auxiliary space
🟡 Better Approach:
Recurse to the last node. On return unwind, set head->next->next = head and head->next = nullptr.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) recursion call stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Standard in-place pointer reversal with prev, curr, and front. O(N) time and strictly O(1) space.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Problem #206 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Stack Data Reversal (Value Overwrite)) 
ListNode* reverseListBrute(ListNode* head) {
    if (!head || !head->next) return head;
    stack<int> st;
    ListNode* temp = head;
    while (temp) { st.push(temp->val); temp = temp->next; }
    temp = head;
    while (temp) {
        temp->val = st.top();
        st.pop();
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    return head;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Recursive Pointer Reversal) 
ListNode* reverseListBetter(ListNode* head) {
    if (head == nullptr || head->next == nullptr) {
        return head;
    }
    ListNode* newHead = reverseListBetter(head->next);
    ListNode* front = head->next;
    front->next = head;
    head->next = nullptr;
    return newHead;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (3-Pointer Iterative In-Place Reversal) 
ListNode* reverseListOptimal(ListNode* head) {
    ListNode* prev = nullptr;
    ListNode* curr = head;
    while (curr != nullptr) {
        ListNode* front = curr->next;
        curr->next = prev;
        prev = curr;
        curr = front;
    }
    return prev;
}

Problem 33 • FAQs (Medium)

Add One to a Number Represented by LL

Medium Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

A number is represented by a singly linked list where each node contains a single digit and the most significant digit is at the head. Add 1 to this number and return the head of the modified linked list.

Example 1:
Input: head = 1 -> 5 -> 9 -> NULL
Output: 1 -> 6 -> 0 -> NULL
Explanation: 159 + 1 = 160. Node 9 becomes 0, node 5 becomes 6.
Example 2:
Input: head = 9 -> 9 -> 9 -> NULL
Output: 1 -> 0 -> 0 -> 0 -> NULL
Explanation: 999 + 1 = 1000. All 9s become 0s with a new node 1 prepended at the head.
Example 3:
Input: head = 0 -> NULL
Output: 1 -> NULL
Explanation: 0 + 1 = 1.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Digits left-to-right hain (MSD to LSD), lekin addition hamesha right-most digit se hota hai. Ek tarika hai list reverse karke carry propagate karna aur wapas reverse karna. Dusra recursive approach: recursion call stack automatically tail tak jata hai aur wapas aate waqt carry propagate karta hai bina list ko reverse kiye!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Reverse the linked list, add 1 propagating carry, and reverse it back to original orientation.
Time: O(3N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Extract digits to vector, add 1 from back with carry handling, allocate new head if carry overflows, overwrite data.
Time: O(2N) • Space: O(N) vector space
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Recurse to the tail of the list. On the return path, carry is added to node data. If carry remains after head, a new node is attached.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) recursion call stack
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Reverse List, Add One, Re-Reverse) 
Node* reverse(Node* head) {
    Node* prev = nullptr; Node* curr = head;
    while (curr) { Node* nxt = curr->next; curr->next = prev; prev = curr; curr = nxt; }
    return prev;
}
Node* addOneBrute(Node* head) {
    head = reverse(head);
    Node* curr = head;
    int carry = 1;
    while (curr && carry) {
        int sum = curr->data + carry;
        curr->data = sum % 10;
        carry = sum / 10;
        if (!curr->next && carry) {
            curr->next = new Node(carry);
            carry = 0;
            break;
        }
        curr = curr->next;
    }
    return reverse(head);
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Vector Number Addition & Overwrite) 
Node* addOneBetter(Node* head) {
    vector<int> v;
    Node* t = head;
    while (t) { v.push_back(t->data); t = t->next; }
    int carry = 1;
    for (int i = (int)v.size() - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        int sum = v[i] + carry;
        v[i] = sum % 10;
        carry = sum / 10;
    }
    if (carry) v.insert(v.begin(), carry);
    Node dummy(0);
    Node* tail = &dummy;
    for (int x : v) { tail->next = new Node(x); tail = tail->next; }
    return dummy.next;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Recursive Backtracking Carry Propagation) 
int addHelper(Node* temp) {
    if (temp == nullptr) return 1;
    int carry = addHelper(temp->next);
    temp->data += carry;
    if (temp->data < 10) return 0;
    temp->data = 0;
    return 1;
}
Node* addOneOptimal(Node* head) {
    int carry = addHelper(head);
    if (carry == 1) {
        Node* newHead = new Node(1);
        newHead->next = head;
        return newHead;
    }
    return head;
}
Problem 34 • FAQs (Medium)

Find Middle of Linked List (Tortoise & Hare)

Easy Problem #876
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

Given the head of a singly linked list, return the middle node of the linked list. If there are two middle nodes (even number of nodes), return the second middle node.

Example 1:
Input: head = 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> NULL
Output: 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> NULL
Explanation: Odd length 5: exact middle node is node 3.
Example 2:
Input: head = 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> NULL
Output: 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> NULL
Explanation: Even length 6: two middle nodes are 3 and 4; returning second middle node 4.
Example 3:
Input: head = 1 -> NULL
Output: 1 -> NULL
Explanation: Single node is its own middle.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Tortoise and Hare (Slow & Fast Pointers) algorithm: Fast pointer do guna tez daudta hai (2 steps at a time) aur Slow pointer normal daudta hai (1 step at a time). Jab Fast pointer aakhiri node par ya list ke paar pahuchta hai, Slow pointer theek aadhi doori tay kar chuka hota hai!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Store every node pointer into a std::vector, return nodes[nodes.size() / 2].
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) auxiliary pointer vector
🟡 Better Approach:
First pass counts total length N. Second pass traverses N/2 steps to return the middle node.
Time: O(N + N/2) = O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Slow moves 1 step, fast moves 2 steps. When fast reaches end, slow is at the middle. Single-pass O(N) time and O(1) space.
Time: O(N/2) = O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary

    }

    return temp;
}

    ListNode* slow = head;
    ListNode* fast = head;
    while (fast != nullptr && fast->next != nullptr) {
        slow = slow->next;
        fast = fast->next->next;
    }
    return slow;
}
Problem 35 • FAQs (Medium)

Detect a Loop in Linked List (Floyd's Cycle Finding)

Easy Problem #141
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

Given head, the head of a linked list, determine if the linked list has a cycle in it. Return true if there is some node in the list that can be reached again by continuously following the next pointer. Otherwise, return false.

Example 1:
Input: head = [3, 2, 0, -4], pos = 1 (tail connects to node 2)
Output: true
Explanation: There is a cycle where tail connects to 2nd node (value 2).
Example 2:
Input: head = [1, 2], pos = 0 (tail connects to node 1)
Output: true
Explanation: Tail connects to head node 1, creating a loop of length 2.
Example 3:
Input: head = [1], pos = -1 (no loop)
Output: false
Explanation: Single node with next pointing to NULL.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Circular track race analogy: Agar ek circular track par do runners hain, ek fast runner (2 m/s) aur ek slow runner (1 m/s), to chahe track kitna bhi lamba ho, fast runner slow runner ko zaroor lap karke cross karega! Agar loop nahi hai to fast runner nullptr par pahuch kar terminate ho jayega.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Change visited node values to a sentinel value (e.g. 1e9 + 7). If sentinel is encountered again, loop detected.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) (Mutates input data)
🟡 Better Approach:
Insert every node pointer address into an unordered_set. If address already exists in set, cycle is present.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) hash set auxiliary space
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Slow moves 1 step, fast moves 2 steps. If pointers ever collide, cycle exists. Runs in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary

bool hasCycleBrute(ListNode* head) {
    const int SENTINEL = 1e9 + 7;
    ListNode* temp = head;
    while (temp) {
        if (temp->val == SENTINEL) return true;
        temp->val = SENTINEL;
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    return false;
}

bool hasCycleBetter(ListNode* head) {
    unordered_set<ListNode*> visited;
    ListNode* temp = head;
    while (temp != nullptr) {
        if (visited.count(temp)) return true;
        visited.insert(temp);
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    return false;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Floyd's Cycle-Finding Algorithm (Tortoise & Hare)) 
bool hasCycleOptimal(ListNode* head) {
    ListNode* slow = head;
    ListNode* fast = head;
    while (fast != nullptr && fast->next != nullptr) {
        slow = slow->next;
        fast = fast->next->next;
        if (slow == fast) return true;
    }
    return false;
}
Problem 36 • FAQs (Medium)

Check if Linked List is Palindrome

Easy Problem #234
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

Given the head of a singly linked list, return true if it is a palindrome or false otherwise.

Example 1:
Input: head = 1 -> 2 -> 2 -> 1 -> NULL
Output: true
Explanation: Reads 1, 2, 2, 1 forwards and backwards identically.
Example 2:
Input: head = 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> NULL
Output: false
Explanation: 1, 2, 3 reversed is 3, 2, 1 which does not match.
Example 3:
Input: head = 1 -> NULL
Output: true
Explanation: Single node is always a palindrome.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Palindrome check karne ke liye: 1) Slow & Fast pointer se list ka middle dhundo. 2) Middle ke baad wale second half ko reverse kar do. 3) First half aur reversed second half ko node-by-node compare karo. 4) (Best practice) Second half ko wapas reverse karke original list restore kar do!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Push all node values onto a stack. Traverse list again comparing current node data with stack.top() and pop.
Time: O(2N) • Space: O(N) stack auxiliary space
🟡 Better Approach:
Copy list values to vector, then use two pointers left = 0 and right = n - 1 moving inwards.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) vector space
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Find middle using slow & fast, reverse second half, compare halves, restore second half. O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Problem #234 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Stack Comparison) 
bool isPalindromeBrute(ListNode* head) {
    stack<int> st;
    ListNode* temp = head;
    while (temp) { st.push(temp->val); temp = temp->next; }
    temp = head;
    while (temp) {
        if (temp->val != st.top()) return false;
        st.pop();
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    return true;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Vector Two-Pointer Inward Scan) 
bool isPalindromeBetter(ListNode* head) {
    vector<int> v;
    ListNode* temp = head;
    while (temp) { v.push_back(temp->val); temp = temp->next; }
    int l = 0, r = (int)v.size() - 1;
    while (l < r) {
        if (v[l++] != v[r--]) return false;
    }
    return true;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Find Middle, Reverse Second Half, Compare) 
ListNode* reverseLL(ListNode* head) {
    ListNode* prev = nullptr; ListNode* curr = head;
    while (curr) { ListNode* nxt = curr->next; curr->next = prev; prev = curr; curr = nxt; }
    return prev;
}
bool isPalindromeOptimal(ListNode* head) {
    if (!head || !head->next) return true;
    ListNode* slow = head;
    ListNode* fast = head;
    while (fast->next != nullptr && fast->next->next != nullptr) {
        slow = slow->next;
        fast = fast->next->next;
    }
    ListNode* newHead = reverseLL(slow->next);
    ListNode* first = head;
    ListNode* second = newHead;
    bool isPalin = true;
    while (second != nullptr) {
        if (first->val != second->val) { isPalin = false; break; }
        first = first->next;
        second = second->next;
    }
    reverseLL(newHead);
    return isPalin;
}
Problem 37 • FAQs (Medium)

Find Intersection Point of Y Linked Lists

Medium Problem #160
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given the heads of two singly linked lists headA and headB, return the node at which the two lists intersect. If the two linked lists have no intersection at all, return NULL.

Example 1:
Input: intersectVal = 8, listA = [4,1,8,4,5], listB = [5,6,1,8,4,5]
Output: Intersected at '8'
Explanation: Both lists merge at node with value 8.
Example 2:
Input: intersectVal = 2, listA = [1,9,1,2,4], listB = [3,2,4]
Output: Intersected at '2'
Explanation: Both lists intersect at node 2.
Example 3:
Input: listA = [2,6,4], listB = [1,5], intersectVal = 0
Output: NULL
Explanation: Lists do not intersect.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Dono lists ki length alag ho sakti hai (L1 aur L2). Lekin intersection ke baad ka hissa common hota hai! Agar pointer A list A khatam karke list B ke head par switch ho jaye, aur pointer B list B khatam karke list A ke head par switch ho jaye, to dono exact (L1 + L2) steps chalte hain aur intersection point par ek sath meet karte hain!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
For each node in list A, traverse all nodes in list B checking if pointers match.
Time: O(N * M) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Store all node pointers of list A in unordered_set, traverse list B checking for set membership.
Time: O(N + M) • Space: O(N) hash set auxiliary space
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Pointers d1 and d2 traverse lists. Upon reaching null, they switch to the opposite list's head. Meets at intersection in O(N + M) time and O(1) space.
Time: O(N + M) • Space: O(1) auxiliary

    while (tempA) {
        ListNode* tempB = headB;
        while (tempB) {

        }
        tempA = tempA->next;

}

    while (temp) { visited.insert(temp); temp = temp->next; }
    temp = headB;

ListNode* getIntersectionNodeOptimal(ListNode* headA, ListNode* headB) {
    if (!headA || !headB) return nullptr;
    ListNode* d1 = headA;
    ListNode* d2 = headB;
    while (d1 != d2) {
        d1 = (d1 == nullptr) ? headB : d1->next;
        d2 = (d2 == nullptr) ? headA : d2->next;
    }
    return d1;
}

Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) auxiliary space

Pass 1 counts total N. Pass 2 moves (N / 2) - 1 steps to predecessor and removes target node.

ListNode* deleteMiddleBrute(ListNode* head) {
    if (!head || !head->next) return nullptr;

    while (temp) { count++; temp = temp->next; }
    int target = count / 2;
    temp = head;
    for (int i = 0; i < target - 1; i++) {
        temp = temp->next;

    ListNode* toDel = temp->next;
    temp->next = toDel->next;

    while (fast != nullptr && fast->next != nullptr) {
        slow = slow->next;
        fast = fast->next->next;
    }
    ListNode* toDelete = slow->next;
    slow->next = slow->next->next;
    delete toDelete;
    return head;
}
Problem 39 • FAQs (Medium)

Find the Starting Point of Loop in Linked List

Medium Problem #142
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given the head of a linked list, return the node where the cycle begins. If there is no cycle, return NULL.

Example 1:
Input: head = [3, 2, 0, -4], pos = 1 (tail connects to node index 1)
Output: Node with value 2
Explanation: The loop starts at the 2nd node with value 2.
Example 2:
Input: head = [1, 2], pos = 0
Output: Node with value 1
Explanation: Loop starts at head node 1.
Example 3:
Input: head = [1], pos = -1
Output: NULL
Explanation: No loop exists.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Mathematical proof: Suppose distance from head to cycle start is L1, and collision point is L2 inside loop of length C. Slow travels L1 + L2, Fast travels 2(L1 + L2). Difference is L1 + L2 = n*C, which means L1 = n*C - L2. Iska matlab collision hone ke baad agar ek pointer ko head par wapas bhej diya jaye aur dono ko 1-1 step chalaya jaye, to wo exact cycle ke entry gate (starting node) par meet karenge!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
For every node, iterate through subsequent nodes checking if any address repeats.
Time: O(N^2) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Traverse list inserting node pointers into unordered_set. The first node pointer that already exists in set is the start of loop.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) hash set auxiliary space
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Detect collision with slow and fast. Reset slow to head. Advance both 1 step at a time; their collision point is the cycle start. O(N) time and O(1) space.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary

    ListNode* temp = head;
    while (temp) {

            runner = runner->next;
        }
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    return nullptr;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Hash Set First Duplicate Lookup) 
ListNode* detectCycleBetter(ListNode* head) {
    unordered_set<ListNode*> visited;
    ListNode* temp = head;
    while (temp != nullptr) {
        if (visited.count(temp)) return temp;
        visited.insert(temp);
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    return nullptr;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Floyd's Algorithm with Head Reset Phase 2) 
ListNode* detectCycleOptimal(ListNode* head) {
    ListNode* slow = head;
    ListNode* fast = head;
    while (fast != nullptr && fast->next != nullptr) {
        slow = slow->next;
        fast = fast->next->next;
        if (slow == fast) {
            slow = head;
            while (slow != fast) {
                slow = slow->next;
                fast = fast->next;
            }
            return slow;
        }
    }
    return nullptr;
}
Problem 40 • FAQs (Medium)

Length of Loop in Linked List

Medium Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given the head of a linked list, find and return the length of the loop present in the list. If no loop exists, return 0.

Example 1:
Input: head = 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 2 (cycle of 4 nodes: 2->3->4->5->2)
Output: 4
Explanation: Loop consists of nodes [2, 3, 4, 5], so length is 4.
Example 2:
Input: head = 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> NULL
Output: 0
Explanation: No cycle exists, so return 0.
Example 3:
Input: head = 1 -> 1 (self-loop)
Output: 1
Explanation: Node connects to itself, loop length is 1.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Floyd's algorithm se Slow aur Fast ka meeting point nikalo. Jab dono collide karte hain, to meeting point loop ke andar hi hota hai! Ab Slow ko wahi roko aur ek runner pointer temp = slow->next chala kar count karte raho jab tak temp == slow wapas na aa jaye.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Store each visited node along with its step timer in unordered_map. If visited again, return timer - map[temp].
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) hash map auxiliary space
🟡 Better Approach:
Locate collision using Floyd's algorithm, freeze fast pointer, advance slow until returning to fast.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Find loop collision node in O(N). Traverse cycle with counter in O(C) where C <= N. Strictly O(1) space.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary

🔴 1. Brute Force (Hash Map Node to Step Index Mapping) 
int countNodesinLoopBrute(Node* head) {
    unordered_map<Node*, int> visited;
    Node* temp = head;
    int timer = 1;
    while (temp != nullptr) {
        if (visited.count(temp)) {
            return timer - visited[temp];
        }
        visited[temp] = timer++;
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    return 0;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Floyd's Collision Followed by Traversal)

    Node* fast = head;
    while (fast && fast->next) {
        slow = slow->next;
        fast = fast->next->next;
        if (slow == fast) {
            int len = 1;
            fast = fast->next;
            while (slow != fast) {
                len++;
                fast = fast->next;
            }
            return len;
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

    Node* fast = head;
    while (fast != nullptr && fast->next != nullptr) {
        slow = slow->next;
        fast = fast->next->next;
        if (slow == fast) {
            int count = 1;
            Node* temp = slow->next;
            while (temp != slow) {
                count++;
                temp = temp->next;
            }
            return count;
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

Problem 41 • FAQs (Hard)

Reverse Nodes in K-Group

Hard Problem #25
Problem Statement Standard • Hard

Given the head of a linked list, reverse the nodes of the list k at a time, and return the modified list. If the number of nodes is not a multiple of k, the leftover nodes at the end should remain in their original order.

Example 1:
Input: head = 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5, k = 2
Output: 2 -> 1 -> 4 -> 3 -> 5 -> NULL
Explanation: Groups of 2: [1,2] reversed to [2,1], [3,4] reversed to [4,3], leftover node 5 remains as is.
Example 2:
Input: head = 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5, k = 3
Output: 3 -> 2 -> 1 -> 4 -> 5 -> NULL
Explanation: Group of 3: [1,2,3] becomes [3,2,1], leftover [4,5] remain unchanged.
Example 3:
Input: head = 1 -> 2, k = 3
Output: 1 -> 2 -> NULL
Explanation: Length 2 is less than k=3, no modification.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Har block me k nodes dhundo getKthNode(temp, k). Agar k-th node exist karta hai, to agle group ka head nextNode = kthNode->next temporarily disconnect karo kthNode->next = nullptr. Current group ko reverse karo, purane group ke previous tail se connect karo, aur pointer ko nextNode par jump kara do.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Dump all nodes to vector, reverse blocks of size k in vector, rebuild the linked list.
Time: O(2N) • Space: O(N) vector space
🟡 Better Approach:
Check if k nodes exist. If yes, reverse them and recursively link head->next = reverseKGroup(nextNode, k).
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N/k) recursion call stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Locate k-th node, isolate segment, reverse in-place, connect prevLast and nextNode. O(N) time and O(1) space.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Problem #25 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Vector Slicing Reversal & Rebuild) 
ListNode* reverseKGroupBrute(ListNode* head, int k) {
    if (!head || k <= 1) return head;
    vector<int> v;
    ListNode* t = head;
    while (t) { v.push_back(t->val); t = t->next; }
    for (size_t i = 0; i + k <= v.size(); i += k) {
        std::reverse(v.begin() + i, v.begin() + i + k);
    }
    ListNode dummy(0);
    ListNode* tail = &dummy;
    for (int x : v) { tail->next = new ListNode(x); tail = tail->next; }
    return dummy.next;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Recursive K-Group Reversal) 
ListNode* reverseKGroupBetter(ListNode* head, int k) {
    ListNode* cursor = head;
    for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) {
        if (!cursor) return head;
        cursor = cursor->next;
    }
    ListNode* curr = head;
    ListNode* prev = nullptr;
    for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) {
        ListNode* nxt = curr->next;
        curr->next = prev;
        prev = curr;
        curr = nxt;
    }
    head->next = reverseKGroupBetter(curr, k);
    return prev;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Iterative K-Group In-Place Reversal) 
ListNode* reverseLinkedList(ListNode* head) {
    ListNode* prev = nullptr; ListNode* curr = head;
    while (curr) { ListNode* nxt = curr->next; curr->next = prev; prev = curr; curr = nxt; }
    return prev;
}
ListNode* getKthNode(ListNode* temp, int k) {
    k -= 1;
    while (temp != nullptr && k > 0) { k--; temp = temp->next; }
    return temp;
}
ListNode* reverseKGroupOptimal(ListNode* head, int k) {
    ListNode* temp = head;
    ListNode* prevLast = nullptr;
    while (temp != nullptr) {
        ListNode* kthNode = getKthNode(temp, k);
        if (kthNode == nullptr) {
            if (prevLast) prevLast->next = temp;
            break;
        }
        ListNode* nextNode = kthNode->next;
        kthNode->next = nullptr;
        reverseLinkedList(temp);
        if (temp == head) head = kthNode;
        else prevLast->next = kthNode;
        prevLast = temp;
        temp = nextNode;
    }
    return head;
}
Problem 42 • FAQs (Hard)

Rotate List

Medium Problem #61
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given the head of a linked list, rotate the list to the right by k places.

Example 1:
Input: head = 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5, k = 2
Output: 4 -> 5 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> NULL
Explanation: Rotate 1: 5->1->2->3->4. Rotate 2: 4->5->1->2->3.
Example 2:
Input: head = 0 -> 1 -> 2, k = 4
Output: 2 -> 0 -> 1 -> NULL
Explanation: Length is 3. k = 4 % 3 = 1. One rotation gives 2 -> 0 -> 1.
Example 3:
Input: head = 1 -> 2, k = 0
Output: 1 -> 2 -> NULL
Explanation: Rotating by 0 leaves list unchanged.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Agar list length L hai, to k = k % L rotations effective hoti hain. Tail ko head se connect karke list ko circular bana do! Naya head (L - k)-th node ke baad shuru hoga. Bas second-last cut point par temp->next = nullptr kar do!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Perform k % L single-step rotations: each time detach the last node and prepend it to the head.
Time: O(k * N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Store node values in vector, rotate vector using std::rotate, overwrite list values.
Time: O(2N) • Space: O(N) vector auxiliary space
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Traverse to tail counting length L. Connect tail->next = head to form circle. Advance L - k steps, set new head and break link.
Time: O(2N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Problem #61 • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Step-by-Step Single Node Rotation) 
ListNode* rotateRightBrute(ListNode* head, int k) {
    if (!head || !head->next || k == 0) return head;
    int len = 0;
    ListNode* curr = head;
    while (curr) { len++; curr = curr->next; }
    k = k % len;
    while (k--) {
        ListNode* prev = nullptr;
        ListNode* tail = head;
        while (tail->next) { prev = tail; tail = tail->next; }
        prev->next = nullptr;
        tail->next = head;
        head = tail;
    }
    return head;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Vector Array Slicing & Reassembly) 
ListNode* rotateRightBetter(ListNode* head, int k) {
    if (!head || !head->next || k == 0) return head;
    vector<int> v;
    ListNode* t = head;
    while (t) { v.push_back(t->val); t = t->next; }
    k = k % v.size();
    if (k == 0) return head;
    std::rotate(v.rbegin(), v.rbegin() + k, v.rend());
    t = head;
    int i = 0;
    while (t) { t->val = v[i++]; t = t->next; }
    return head;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Make Circular, Find (L - k)th Node, Break Loop) 
ListNode* rotateRightOptimal(ListNode* head, int k) {
    if (!head || !head->next || k == 0) return head;
    ListNode* tail = head;
    int len = 1;
    while (tail->next != nullptr) {
        tail = tail->next;
        len++;
    }
    k = k % len;
    if (k == 0) return head;
    tail->next = head;
    int stepsToNewTail = len - k;
    ListNode* newTail = head;
    for (int i = 1; i < stepsToNewTail; i++) {
        newTail = newTail->next;
    }
    ListNode* newHead = newTail->next;
    newTail->next = nullptr;
    return newHead;
}
Problem 43 • FAQs (Hard)

Merge Two Sorted Lists

Easy Problem #21
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

You are given the heads of two sorted linked lists list1 and list2. Merge the two lists into one sorted linked list and return its head. The list should be made by splicing together the nodes of the first two lists.

Example 1:
Input: list1 = 1 -> 2 -> 4, list2 = 1 -> 3 -> 4
Output: 1 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 4 -> NULL
Explanation: Both lists merged in non-decreasing order.
Example 2:
Input: list1 = [], list2 = []
Output: []
Explanation: Both lists are empty.
Example 3:
Input: list1 = [], list2 = [0]
Output: [0]
Explanation: Merging empty list with [0] yields [0].
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Two-pointer merge pattern (jaise Merge Sort me use hota hai). Ek dummy node banao dummy aur pointer tail = &dummy rakho. Compare karo: agar list1->val <= list2->val to tail ke aage list1 jodo, warna list2. Jo list bache usko aakhir me O(1) me seedha attach kar do!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Dump all values from both lists into vector, sort, and construct new list.
Time: O((N + M) log(N + M)) • Space: O(N + M) vector space
🟡 Better Approach:
Recursively pick smaller head node and assign head->next = mergeTwoLists(smaller->next, other).
Time: O(N + M) • Space: O(N + M) recursion stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Merge lists in-place using dummy node without allocating new nodes. O(N + M) time and O(1) space.
Time: O(N + M) • Space: O(1) auxiliary

ListNode* mergeTwoListsBrute(ListNode* list1, ListNode* list2) {
    vector<int> v;
    while (list1) { v.push_back(list1->val); list1 = list1->next; }
    while (list2) { v.push_back(list2->val); list2 = list2->next; }
    sort(v.begin(), v.end());
    ListNode dummy(0);
    ListNode* tail = &dummy;
    for (int x : v) { tail->next = new ListNode(x); tail = tail->next; }
    return dummy.next;
