🟡 2. Better Approach (Recursive Head Selection Merge) 
ListNode* mergeTwoListsBetter(ListNode* list1, ListNode* list2) {
    if (!list1) return list2;
    if (!list2) return list1;
    if (list1->val <= list2->val) {
        list1->next = mergeTwoListsBetter(list1->next, list2);
        return list1;
    } else {
        list2->next = mergeTwoListsBetter(list1, list2->next);
        return list2;
    }
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Iterative Dummy Head In-Place Splicing) 
ListNode* mergeTwoListsOptimal(ListNode* list1, ListNode* list2) {
    ListNode dummy(0);
    ListNode* tail = &dummy;
    while (list1 != nullptr && list2 != nullptr) {
        if (list1->val <= list2->val) {
            tail->next = list1;
            list1 = list1->next;
        } else {
            tail->next = list2;
            list2 = list2->next;
        }
        tail = tail->next;
    }
    tail->next = (list1 != nullptr) ? list1 : list2;
    return dummy.next;
}
Problem 44 • FAQs (Hard)

Flattening a Linked List

Hard Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Hard

Given a Linked List of size N, where every node represents a sub-linked-list and contains two pointers: next (points to next head) and bottom (points to a sub-linked-list in sorted order). Flatten the list so all nodes appear in a single sorted list connected via the bottom pointer.

Example 1:
Input: 5 -> 10 -> 19 -> 28 | | | | 7 20 22 35 | | | 8 50 40
Output: 5 -> 7 -> 8 -> 10 -> 19 -> 20 -> 22 -> 28 -> 35 -> 40 -> 50
Explanation: All columns are merged into a single sorted bottom-linked list.
Example 2:
Input: 5 -> 10 (each with 1 bottom node)
Output: Merged into sorted bottom order.
Explanation: 2 columns merged.
Example 3:
Input: Single column list
Output: Returns the column as-is.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Divide and Conquer (Merge Sort pattern): Rightmost do vertical lists ko merge2Lists function se merge karo. Recursion se list ke aakhiri do heads tak jao aur wapas unwinding ke waqt do-do vertical lists ko merge karte jao bottom pointers ke through!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Collect all values traversing both next and bottom pointers into vector, sort, rebuild bottom list.
Time: O(N log N) • Space: O(N) auxiliary vector
🟡 Better Approach:
Push heads of all vertical lists into a min-heap, repeatedly pop minimum and push its bottom child.
Time: O(N log K) where K is number of columns • Space: O(K) priority queue space
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Recursively flatten root->next, then merge root with the flattened right list via bottom pointers. O(Total Nodes) time and O(K) recursion stack.
Time: O(Total Nodes * K) • Space: O(K) recursion call stack
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Vector Collection, std::sort, Reconstruct) 
Node* flattenBrute(Node* root) {
    vector<int> v;
    Node* col = root;
    while (col) {
        Node* row = col;
        while (row) { v.push_back(row->data); row = row->bottom; }
        col = col->next;
    }
    sort(v.begin(), v.end());
    Node dummy(0);
    Node* tail = &dummy;
    for (int x : v) { tail->bottom = new Node(x); tail = tail->bottom; }
    return dummy.bottom;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Min-Heap (Priority Queue) K-Way Merge) 
struct Compare {
    bool operator()(Node* a, Node* b) { return a->data > b->data; }
};
Node* flattenBetter(Node* root) {
    priority_queue<Node*, vector<Node*>, Compare> pq;
    Node* col = root;
    while (col) { pq.push(col); col = col->next; }
    Node dummy(0);
    Node* tail = &dummy;
    while (!pq.empty()) {
        Node* curr = pq.top();
        pq.pop();
        tail->bottom = curr;
        tail = tail->bottom;
        if (curr->bottom) pq.push(curr->bottom);
    }
    return dummy.bottom;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Recursive Merge of Vertical Lists) 
Node* mergeBottom(Node* a, Node* b) {
    Node dummy(0);
    Node* res = &dummy;
    while (a != nullptr && b != nullptr) {
        if (a->data <= b->data) {
            res->bottom = a;
            res = a;
            a = a->bottom;
        } else {
            res->bottom = b;
            res = b;
            b = b->bottom;
        }
    }
    res->bottom = (a != nullptr) ? a : b;
    return dummy.bottom;
}
Node* flattenOptimal(Node* root) {
    if (root == nullptr || root->next == nullptr) {
        return root;
    }
    root->next = flattenOptimal(root->next);
    root = mergeBottom(root, root->next);
    return root;
}

        if (l1->val <= l2->val) { t->next = l1; l1 = l1->next; }

        else { tail->next = l2; l2 = l2->next; }

    ListNode* right = sortListOptimal(rightHead);
    return mergeSorted(left, right);
}
Problem 46 • FAQs (Hard)

Clone a Linked List with Next and Random Pointer

Hard Problem #138
Problem Statement Standard • Hard

A linked list of length n is given such that each node contains an additional random pointer, which could point to any node in the list, or null. Construct a deep copy of the list. Return the head of the copied linked list.

Example 1:
Input: head = [[7,null],[13,0],[11,4],[10,2],[1,0]]
Output: Deep copy with exact node values and identical next and random pointer connectivity.
Explanation: Every cloned node is newly created in heap with no shared pointers with original nodes.
Example 2:
Input: head = [[1,1],[2,1]]
Output: [[1,1],[2,1]]
Explanation: Node 1 random points to itself, node 2 random points to node 1.
Example 3:
Input: head = []
Output: []
Explanation: Empty list returns empty deep copy.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Agar hum hash map use karein map[originalNode] = copyNode, to O(N) extra space lagti hai. Lekin 3-Step In-Place Algorithm se bina kisi map ke O(1) space me clone ban sakta hai: 1) Har original node ke theek aage uska copy node insert kar do: original->copy->original->copy. 2) Random pointers set karo: curr->next->random = curr->random->next. 3) Dono lists ko separate/untangle kar do!
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Measure index offset of each random pointer relative to head, recreate list, connect random pointers using calculated indices.
Time: O(N^2) • Space: O(N) index mapping space
🟡 Better Approach:
Pass 1 creates clone nodes mapped in unordered_map. Pass 2 wires next and random pointers using map lookups.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) hash map auxiliary space
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Step 1: Interleave cloned nodes. Step 2: Wire random pointers. Step 3: Separate cloned list from original list. O(N) time and O(1) space.
Time: O(3N) = O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary

🔴 1. Brute Force (Two-Pass Distance / Offset Lookup) 
Node* copyRandomListBrute(Node* head) {
    if (!head) return nullptr;
    vector<Node*> orig;
    Node* t = head;
    while (t) { orig.push_back(t); t = t->next; }
    vector<Node*> cloned;
    for (Node* node : orig) cloned.push_back(new Node(node->val));
    for (size_t i = 0; i < orig.size(); i++) {
        if (i + 1 < orig.size()) cloned[i]->next = cloned[i + 1];
        if (orig[i]->random) {
            auto it = find(orig.begin(), orig.end(), orig[i]->random);
            int idx = distance(orig.begin(), it);
            cloned[i]->random = cloned[idx];
        }
    }
    return cloned[0];
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Hash Map Node-to-Clone Mapping) 
Node* copyRandomListBetter(Node* head) {
    if (!head) return nullptr;
    unordered_map<Node*, Node*> m;
    Node* curr = head;
    while (curr) {
        m[curr] = new Node(curr->val);
        curr = curr->next;
    }
    curr = head;
    while (curr) {
        m[curr]->next = m[curr->next];
        m[curr]->random = m[curr->random];
        curr = curr->next;
    }
    return m[head];
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (3-Step In-Place Interleaving Algorithm) 
Node* copyRandomListOptimal(Node* head) {
    if (!head) return nullptr;
    Node* curr = head;
    while (curr != nullptr) {
        Node* copy = new Node(curr->val);
        copy->next = curr->next;
        curr->next = copy;
        curr = copy->next;
    }
    curr = head;
    while (curr != nullptr) {
        if (curr->random != nullptr) {
            curr->next->random = curr->random->next;
        }
        curr = curr->next->next;
    }
    Node dummy(0);
    Node* copyTail = &dummy;
    curr = head;
    while (curr != nullptr) {
        Node* copy = curr->next;
        curr->next = copy->next;
        copyTail->next = copy;
        copyTail = copy;
        curr = curr->next;
    }
    return dummy.next;
}

Module 6: FAQs (DLL) (3 Problems)

3 Problems
Problem 47 • FAQs (DLL)

Delete All Occurrences of a Key in Doubly Linked List

Medium Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given the head of a Doubly Linked List and an integer key, delete all occurrences of nodes having data equal to key and return the updated head pointer.

Example 1:
Input: head = 2 <-> 2 <-> 10 <-> 8 <-> 4 <-> 2 <-> 5 <-> 2, key = 2
Output: 10 <-> 8 <-> 4 <-> 5 -> NULL
Explanation: All four nodes with value 2 are removed cleanly.
Example 2:
Input: head = 9 <-> 9 <-> 9, key = 9
Output: NULL
Explanation: All nodes match key, list becomes empty.
Example 3:
Input: head = 1 <-> 2 <-> 3, key = 7
Output: 1 <-> 2 <-> 3 -> NULL
Explanation: Key not present, unchanged.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
DLL traverse karte waqt agar temp->data == key mile: 1) Agar ye head tha to head = head->next. 2) Neighbor pointers prevNode = temp->prev aur nextNode = temp->next ko apas me jodo: prevNode->next = nextNode aur nextNode->prev = prevNode. 3) Node delete karo aur agle node par chalo.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Extract all values omitting the key into a vector, rebuild the entire DLL.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) auxiliary vector
🟡 Better Approach:
Recurse on head->next, check current node, unlink and delete if value matches key.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) recursion stack
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Traverse list once updating prev and next pointers with explicit memory deletion. O(N) time and O(1) space.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Vector Filter & Reconstruct DLL) 
Node* deleteAllOccurrencesBrute(Node* head, int k) {
    vector<int> v;
    Node* t = head;
    while (t) {
        if (t->data != k) v.push_back(t->data);
        t = t->next;
    }
    if (v.empty()) return nullptr;
    Node* newHead = new Node(v[0]);
    Node* prev = newHead;
    for (size_t i = 1; i < v.size(); i++) {
        Node* curr = new Node(v[i], nullptr, prev);
        prev->next = curr;
        prev = curr;
    }
    return newHead;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Recursive Deletion with Backtracking) 
Node* deleteAllOccurrencesBetter(Node* head, int k) {
    if (!head) return nullptr;
    head->next = deleteAllOccurrencesBetter(head->next, k);
    if (head->next) head->next->prev = head;
    if (head->data == k) {
        Node* nxt = head->next;
        delete head;
        return nxt;
    }
    return head;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Single Pass In-Place Bidirectional Unlink) 
Node* deleteAllOccurrencesOptimal(Node* head, int k) {
    Node* temp = head;
    while (temp != nullptr) {
        if (temp->data == k) {
            if (temp == head) {
                head = head->next;
            }
            Node* nextNode = temp->next;
            Node* prevNode = temp->prev;
            if (nextNode != nullptr) nextNode->prev = prevNode;
            if (prevNode != nullptr) prevNode->next = nextNode;
            delete temp;
            temp = nextNode;
        } else {
            temp = temp->next;
        }
    }
    return head;
}
Problem 48 • FAQs (DLL)

Remove Duplicates from Sorted Doubly Linked List

Easy Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Easy

Given the head of a sorted Doubly Linked List, delete all duplicate nodes such that each element appears only once.

Example 1:
Input: head = 1 <-> 1 <-> 1 <-> 2 <-> 3 <-> 3 <-> 4
Output: 1 <-> 2 <-> 3 <-> 4 -> NULL
Explanation: All consecutive identical values are removed, leaving single occurrences.
Example 2:
Input: head = 1 <-> 1 <-> 1 -> NULL
Output: 1 -> NULL
Explanation: Only 1 remains.
Example 3:
Input: head = 1 <-> 2 <-> 3
Output: 1 <-> 2 <-> 3 -> NULL
Explanation: Already distinct.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
List already sorted hai, iska matlab duplicate values hamesha bagal-bagal (consecutive) hongi! Pointer temp = head rakho. Ek inner runner pointer nextNode = temp->next chalao jab tak nextNode != null && nextNode->data == temp->data ho. Saare duplicates ko delete karke temp->next = nextNode aur nextNode->prev = temp link kar do.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Store seen elements in unordered_set, delete any node whose data already exists in the set.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) hash set auxiliary space
🟡 Better Approach:
Collect unique values using std::unique, rebuild new DLL from distinct values.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) vector space
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Scan consecutive duplicates, unlink block, free memory in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Hash Set Duplicate Tracking) 
Node* removeDuplicatesBrute(Node* head) {
    unordered_set<int> seen;
    Node* curr = head;
    while (curr) {
        if (seen.count(curr->data)) {
            Node* nxt = curr->next;
            Node* prv = curr->prev;
            if (prv) prv->next = nxt;
            if (nxt) nxt->prev = prv;
            delete curr;
            curr = nxt;
        } else {
            seen.insert(curr->data);
            curr = curr->next;
        }
    }
    return head;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Vector Unique Filtering & Rebuild) 
Node* removeDuplicatesBetter(Node* head) {
    if (!head || !head->next) return head;
    vector<int> v;
    Node* t = head;
    while (t) { v.push_back(t->data); t = t->next; }
    v.erase(unique(v.begin(), v.end()), v.end());
    Node* newHead = new Node(v[0]);
    Node* prev = newHead;
    for (size_t i = 1; i < v.size(); i++) {
        Node* curr = new Node(v[i], nullptr, prev);
        prev->next = curr;
        prev = curr;
    }
    return newHead;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Direct Consecutive Pointer Rewiring) 
Node* removeDuplicatesOptimal(Node* head) {
    Node* temp = head;
    while (temp != nullptr && temp->next != nullptr) {
        Node* nextNode = temp->next;
        while (nextNode != nullptr && nextNode->data == temp->data) {
            Node* duplicate = nextNode;
            nextNode = nextNode->next;
            delete duplicate;
        }
        temp->next = nextNode;
        if (nextNode != nullptr) {
            nextNode->prev = temp;
        }
        temp = temp->next;
    }
    return head;
}
Problem 49 • FAQs (DLL)

Find Pairs with Given Sum in Doubly Linked List

Medium Standard Problem
Problem Statement Standard • Medium

Given a sorted Doubly Linked List of positive distinct integers and an integer target, find and return all distinct pairs of nodes that sum up to target.

Example 1:
Input: head = 1 <-> 2 <-> 4 <-> 5 <-> 6 <-> 8 <-> 9, target = 7
Output: [(1, 6), (2, 5)]
Explanation: 1 + 6 = 7, and 2 + 5 = 7.
Example 2:
Input: head = 1 <-> 5 <-> 6, target = 6
Output: [(1, 5)]
Explanation: 1 + 5 = 6.
Example 3:
Input: head = 1 <-> 2, target = 5
Output: []
Explanation: No pair adds up to 5.
💡 Core Intuition / Kaise Sochen:
Sorted array me Two Pointers (Left at start, Right at end) use karte hain. Doubly Linked List me bhi prev pointers ki wajah se right pointer backward chal sakta hai! left = head rakho, right = tail par le jao. Agar sum == target to pair add karo aur dono ko inward shift karo (left = left->next, right = right->prev). Agar sum < target to left = left->next, warna right = right->prev.
🔴 Brute Force Approach:
Check every pair (node1, node2) using nested while loops.
Time: O(N^2) • Space: O(1) auxiliary
🟡 Better Approach:
Traverse list checking if target - current->data exists in unordered_set, store visited data in set.
Time: O(N) • Space: O(N) hash set auxiliary space
🟢 Optimal Approach:
Left starts at head, right at tail. Advance inwards based on sum comparison. O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
Time: O(2N) = O(N) • Space: O(1) auxiliary (excluding return vector)
Clean Standard • Zero Comments C++
🔴 1. Brute Force (Nested Loops All Pairs Check) 
vector<pair<int, int>> findPairsWithGivenSumBrute(Node* head, int target) {
    vector<pair<int, int>> ans;
    Node* t1 = head;
    while (t1 != nullptr) {
        Node* t2 = t1->next;
        while (t2 != nullptr && (t1->data + t2->data <= target)) {
            if (t1->data + t2->data == target) {
                ans.push_back({t1->data, t2->data});
            }
            t2 = t2->next;
        }
        t1 = t1->next;
    }
    return ans;
}
🟡 2. Better Approach (Hash Set Complement Lookup) 
vector<pair<int, int>> findPairsWithGivenSumBetter(Node* head, int target) {
    vector<pair<int, int>> ans;
    unordered_set<int> seen;
    Node* curr = head;
    while (curr) {
        int comp = target - curr->data;
        if (seen.count(comp)) {
            ans.push_back({comp, curr->data});
        }
        seen.insert(curr->data);
        curr = curr->next;
    }
    sort(ans.begin(), ans.end());
    return ans;
}
🟢 3. Optimal Approach (Two-Pointer (Head & Tail) Inward Traversal) 
Node* findTail(Node* head) {
    Node* tail = head;
    while (tail->next != nullptr) tail = tail->next;
    return tail;
}
vector<pair<int, int>> findPairsWithGivenSumOptimal(Node* head, int target) {
    vector<pair<int, int>> ans;
    if (head == nullptr) return ans;
    Node* left = head;
    Node* right = findTail(head);
    while (left->data < right->data) {
        int sum = left->data + right->data;
        if (sum == target) {
            ans.push_back({left->data, right->data});
            left = left->next;
            right = right->prev;
        } else if (sum < target) {
            left = left->next;
        } else {
            right = right->prev;
        }
    }
    return ans;
}
